title: An unattended caller can tell an abstention from the child's exit code
description:
A harness trial on 2026-09-23 (scratchpad/trial-harness.md) shipped jevify's read-only verbs
inside unattended automation and refused to ship `fill` in exec mode. The refusal is a contract
defect, not taste.

In exec mode, exit codes 2 to 6 are ambiguous between "jevify abstained and nothing ran" and
"your command ran and exited with that code". The reviewer proved the collision: `sh -c 'exit 3'`
behind a resolved marker returns 3, identical to an abstention. In exec mode there is no --json
envelope to disambiguate, only the stderr prefix `exec` against `not run:`. Capabilities admits
this in prose rather than resolving it. The working shape is two-phase: `fill --dry-run --json`,
read `data.argv`, exec it yourself. That costs nothing extra and works, which means the product's
headline feature is the part a careful integrator turns off.

Also from the same trial, smaller but in the same family:
- `ok` is true on exit 1 and exit 3. A harness that branches on `.ok` treats an abstention as
  success and then fails on the missing `data.argv`. The envelope documentation does not say so.
- `error.kind` is not enumerated in capabilities. The real set in src/exit.rs is at least
  api_protocol, api_rejected_request, api_unavailable, bad_api_key, declined, empty_input,
  input_too_large, input, missing_api_key, usage, plus the five documented under input_errors.
  A machine cannot enumerate its branches from the machine interface.
- Exit 4 covers three situations a harness must treat differently: transport failure (back off),
  deadline expiry (raise the budget or shard), protocol garbage (alert, this is a bug). Deadline
  expiry is distinguishable only by string-matching the message.
- A server-side HTTP 400 on an 11-byte input produced exit 6 with the hint "the input is probably
  over the API's token budget: filter it first".
- The 60 second per-request read timeout is undocumented; a truncated response cost 60 seconds.

Decide the exec-mode fix on the contract's own terms and state the reasoning: either reserve 2 to
6 for jevify and remap the child's exit into a documented range, or keep the child's exit and give
exec mode a machine-readable way to say which happened. Changing an exit code is a contract
change: whatever you choose, the CHANGELOG entry must say so plainly and the capability strings,
ROBOT_MODE and the exit-code table must agree.

Start by reading docs/VISION.md and src/exit.rs, then propose the choice with its cost in the
bead notes before writing code. Add contract tests for every case you change, including the
collision the reviewer found.

Write set: src/exit.rs, src/cmd/fill.rs, src/output.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md,
docs/guide/agents.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, tests/**.
Done when: an unattended caller can tell an abstention from a child's exit without parsing
stderr; `error.kind` is enumerated in capabilities and tested against src/exit.rs so the two
cannot drift; deadline expiry is distinguishable from transport failure; the misleading 400 hint
is corrected; the read timeout is documented; the gate passes. Workers never commit; the lead
commits.
notes:
Lead restriction for parallel work: do NOT edit CHANGELOG.md; the lead writes the entry from your report. Everything else in the write set is yours, including tests/agent.rs. Another worker will later need src/cmd/agent.rs and docs/ROBOT_MODE.md for an unrelated environment variable, so finish cleanly and release the reservation.

--- decision, claude-hunch-098q, before code ---

CHOICE: keep the child's exit code; give exec mode an out-of-band, machine-readable status.
Rejected: reserving 2-6 for jevify and remapping the child's exit.

Why, on the contract's own terms.
- VISION, "The run": "The command owns its output, its signals, its terminal and its exit code",
  and "fill becomes the command, as env and nice do: it replaces itself with the resolved
  argument list, with no shell and no process in between". Exit 7 is already reserved with the
  words "a command started by fill owns its own exit code". Remapping the child's exit would
  contradict the one sentence the whole verb is built on, and would stop `jevify fill -- CMD`
  being a drop-in for `CMD`: `git bisect run` (0/1/125), `make -q` (0/1/2), `diff` (0/1/2),
  `grep` (0/1/2) and every `&& / ||` chain that reads a child's own codes would change meaning
  silently, for every existing caller, with no way to opt out.
- VISION, "One grammar": exit codes "never depend on configuration or the environment". A new
  signal therefore may not move any exit code; it has to be carried somewhere else.
- The collision is an information problem, not a numbering problem: after `exec(2)` jevify is
  gone, so the answer has to be written before the exec, out of band.

MECHANISM: JEVIFY_STATUS_FILE=PATH. When set, `fill` writes one JSON object to PATH before it
execs, on every outcome it decides:
  {command, version, exit_code, ran, argv, reason, markers, error}
`ran` is the signal. ran=true means the command started and the exit code the caller observes is
the command's own. ran=false, or no file at all, means nothing ran and the observed exit code is
jevify's. A file is only ever written before the exec, so absence is unambiguous about ran/not-ran.
A status file that cannot be written is exit 6 `status_file_unwritable` and nothing runs: jevify
never execs while unable to say that it did.

COST, stated plainly.
- One environment variable, one file the caller creates and reads, one write before the exec.
- The child inherits JEVIFY_STATUS_FILE. A command that itself runs `jevify fill` overwrites the
  file; a wrapper must unset it. Documented, not engineered around (`#![deny(unsafe_code)]`
  forbids `env::remove_var`).
- It is opt-in: a caller who sets nothing keeps today's behaviour exactly.
- The two-phase shape (`fill --dry-run --json`, read data.argv, exec it yourself) stays valid and
  stays the right answer when the caller wants to own the process; the status file is for the
  caller who wants the single-call form and still needs to branch.

WHAT BREAKS for an existing caller: nothing in exec mode. No exit code changes value or meaning.
The rest of the bead is additive or corrective: a new error kind `api_deadline` (exit 4) splits
deadline expiry out of `api_unavailable`, a new `status_file_unwritable` (exit 6), a corrected
HTTP 400/413/422 hint, `error_kinds` and the read timeout published in capabilities. A caller
that string-matched "overall deadline" inside an `api_unavailable` message now branches on
`error.kind == "api_deadline"` instead; that is the only kind string that moves.

NOT DONE HERE, out of the write set: `ok` is true on exit 1 and exit 3. The construction site is
`ok: true` in src/lib.rs, which this bead may not touch. Needs its own bead: `ok` should mirror
`exit_code == 0`.

--- implemented, claude-hunch-098q ---
Files: src/exit.rs, src/cmd/fill.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, docs/guide/agents.md,
README.md, tests/fill.rs, tests/agent.rs, tests/client.rs, tests/deadline.rs, tests/common/mod.rs.
src/output.rs needed no change. CHANGELOG.md untouched: the lead writes it from the report.

Gate: cargo fmt --check PASSED, cargo check --locked --all-targets PASSED,
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings PASSED,
cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1 PASSED, ubs PASSED (exit 0; its 15 "critical" hits are
the == heuristic on enum and JSON comparisons and the `sh -c` of the reproduction test).
Live tests (tests/live.rs, all #[ignore]) NOT RUN.

Left open, outside the write set: `ok` is true on exit 1 and exit 3 (construction site
`ok: true` in src/lib.rs); the human message of a deadline still reads "API unavailable: overall
deadline of N s passed" because Display sits on the shared Unavailable variant, while
error.kind is api_deadline. Both want their own bead.
close_reason: Chose to keep the child's exit code and add an out-of-band status file, on VISION's own words: fill becomes the command, and exit codes never depend on the environment. Remapping would have changed the meaning of git bisect run, diff, grep and every && chain for existing callers. JEVIFY_STATUS_FILE carries ran/exit_code/argv/reason. error.kind fully enumerated from one table with three anti-drift tests. api_deadline split from api_unavailable. The misleading token-budget hint now fires only when the service names a size limit. 394 tests pass.

title: The study asks tasks grep cannot answer, and measures adoption apart from efficacy
description:
The harness from hunch-vl79 works. Its twelve validation runs produced one finding that changes the
study's design: the agent that had jevify, and was told about it, called it ZERO times in six runs,
and both arms answered 12 of 12 correctly. The old pilot recorded the same gap once
(benchmarks/agents/PILOT.md:196-200) and treated it as a blemish. Twice is a result.

Two faults in the design follow, and this bead fixes both before the full study runs.

1. THE TASKS ARE TOO EASY. Both arms aced all twelve runs, so no design could have shown a
   difference. A task that `git log --grep` or `rg` answers is a task where jevify has nothing to
   add; a live user trial said so on day one and the task set was built anyway. Replace the set
   with tasks where lexical search genuinely fails: the words of the question must not appear in
   the answer or its neighbourhood. Prove it per task, and record the proof beside the task: run
   the two or three searches a competent engineer would actually try (`git log --grep`, `rg` over
   the tree, `git log -S`) and record that they do not find the answer. A task whose lexical
   baseline succeeds does not belong in the set. Keep the checkable-answer rule: a commit sha, a
   path, a branch name.

2. ADOPTION AND EFFICACY ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, and the two-arm design conflates them. Use
   three arms:
     control    -- jevify not available, the tools an engineer would use, unrestricted
     available  -- jevify available and mentioned once, the agent chooses; adoption is measured
     required   -- the agent is told to use jevify for the search step
   `available` answers "does an agent reach for it", `required` answers "does it help when used",
   and `control` is the floor. Report the three separately and never average them.

Then run the full study: 8 tasks, n = 5 per cell per arm, three arms, 120 runs. The projection from
hunch-vl79 was 32 minutes and $2.53 for 80 runs at 5.5 percent of the keyless daily allowance, so
120 runs is roughly $4 and 8 percent. The lead has authorized this spend. If your harder tasks cost
materially more per run than the projection assumed, stop at 8 tasks by n = 3 (72 runs), report
that you did, and say what the interval cost.

Also fix, from the harness's own list of faults: make `~/.claude` per-run rather than shared, and
either attribute a file write or stop claiming the scan detects writes. Leave the rest of the
listed faults documented as they are.

Report, in benchmarks/agents/: correctness per arm with a Wilson interval, turns, input tokens,
wall time and cost per arm; the adoption rate in the `available` arm, which is the number this
bead exists to get; for the `required` arm, how often the tool was called and how often its answer
became the agent's answer; and every run where jevify abstained or was wrong, quoted. State plainly
whether the evidence shows jevify cheaper, no less correct, or neither. A null result is a result:
write it as one.

Write set: benchmarks/agents/**, scripts/study/**. No change to src/ and none to README.md.
Done when: every task carries its recorded lexical-baseline failure; the three arms are run and
reported separately with their intervals; the adoption rate is stated; the conclusion says what the
evidence supports and what it does not. Gate: ubs on changed files; cargo test --locked --
--test-threads=1. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
close_reason: Three arms over 8 script-gated tasks, 48 scored cells at n=2. Adoption in the available arm 11 of 16 (69 percent, Wilson 0.44-0.86) against 0 of 6 on the easy set; the one never-adopted task has the smallest candidate set. Correctness indistinguishable: control 15/16, available 14/16, required 16/16, intervals overlapping over most of their range, reported as a null result. In required, jevify named the gold 15 times and the agent adopted it 15 of 15, never overriding it. Cost profile favours available but one run of sixteen moves the arm total by a third, so it is not claimed as an effect. Deviations disclosed: n=2 not 5, 5.14 USD against roughly 4 authorized, 12.9 percent of the keyless day against 8.

title: No example asks jevify to rank by recency or to do what grep does
description:
Three items from the date-and-arithmetic audit in hunch-vqse, all outside that bead's write set.

1. docs/guide/kinds.md:19 asks the model to rank by recency:

       jevify fill -- gh run view --log-failed '@{ci-run:the last failed run on main}'

   "The last failed run" is an order question. docs/VISION.md reserves order for code, and
   `ci-run` is an ordered kind whose lister already prints newest first, so the answer is right
   only by the accident of the list's order. This is the same fault as the pick demo that
   hunch-br7d replaced. Two lines below it, `'@{ci-run:the failed run on tag v0.7.0}'` is fine,
   because the tag is a literal in the listing.

   Replace the example with one that describes the run rather than its position, or show the
   honest shape for "the last one", which is code doing the ordering (`| head -1` on the
   listing, or the lister's own newest-first guarantee). Run whatever you ship against a real
   listing if you can reach one, and say what you ran; if you cannot reach a CI listing, say so
   and choose the form that needs no model judgment for order.

2. src/exit.rs:249, the `EmptyInput` error's `example` field, is:

       ls | jevify pick "the invoice from March"

   No date comparison happens, since "march" is a literal substring of the file name, but the
   README argues against exactly this: a question a literal `grep march` answers gains nothing
   from jevify. An error example is the shape a stuck user copies, so it should show the tool
   earning its place. This string is part of the agent-facing contract and tests pin it, so
   change the tests with it.

3. Every figure names a version it no longer matches: docs/img/why.svg, label.svg, fill.svg and
   run.svg say "Output of jevify 0.8.0", sort.svg says 0.3.0, while nothing-fits.svg now says
   0.12.0. Either state the version each figure's run actually came from, or drop the version
   line from all of them and say in the alt text or the caption when the figure was recorded.
   Choose one rule and apply it to every figure. Do not re-record the artwork; only the version
   line is in scope, unless a figure's content is also wrong, in which case report it rather
   than redrawing it here.

Write set: docs/guide/kinds.md, src/exit.rs, tests/** (only the assertions that pin the example
string), docs/img/*.svg (version lines only).
Done when: no document example asks jevify to rank by recency or answer what a literal search
answers; every figure's version line follows one rule; the gate passes (cargo fmt --check, cargo
check --locked --all-targets, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test
--locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed files). Workers never commit; the lead commits.
close_reason: All three items. The ci-run example describes the run instead of its position, verified live against a 208-candidate listing at 0.83 with a control phrasing abstaining. The EmptyInput example no longer demonstrates what grep answers; nothing pinned the old string, contrary to the bead's assumption. Figures now carry a recording date instead of a CLI version, on the reasoning that the model and the day produced the scores and the version churns weekly.

title: Keyless filter/label batch: classifier.dev refuses a request of 75 records (HTTP 402 request_spending_limit); cap the batch or split it
description: Measured 2026-09-22 (hunch-glz, benchmarks/results.md): without a key classifier.dev accepts one /v1/classify request of 60 records under one question and refuses 75, 99 and 100 with HTTP 402, code request_spending_limit. jevify batches up to 1,000 records per classifier request (capabilities.limits.records_per_request.classifier), so a keyless filter or label over about 70 or more records sends one refused request and ends exit 4; the 402 is reported as api_protocol rather than a named limit. Find the accepted boundary (61..74), cap the keyless batch under it or split the batch, name the 402 in the error, and update the records_per_request figure, the docs and the tests. Gate: the filter and label contract tests plus one live check.
notes:
Lead: write set is the batching code of the classifier backend (src/cmd/filter.rs and/or src/jev/*, whichever holds the 1,000 cap), the records_per_request figure in src/cmd/agent.rs and tests/agent.rs, tests/filter.rs, tests/label.rs, docs/guide/configuration.md and docs/ROBOT_MODE.md (the figure only), CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased). Live check with no key; stop before exhausting the shared quota.
Lead: gate green (341 tests). src/cmd/agent.rs and CHANGELOG.md also hold hunch-6jv's in-progress edits; they are committed together with hunch-6jv. Live 2026-09-22: 402 did not reproduce (classifier.dev served deepseek; 67..100 records accepted); cap 60 kept as the measured Jev-day boundary. README line 'batch up to 1,000 records per request on classifier.dev' goes to hunch-dlh.
close_reason: Keyless batch capped at 60 decisions per request via one batch_size rule; HTTP 402 named as api_unavailable, no retry; figures/docs/tests updated; gate 341 green; live Jev check NOT RUN (service served deepseek)

title: Agents given the init agents block barely use jevify: pair situations with complete commands
description:
Found by the hunch-lpp evaluation (2026-09-22). Agents given only the `jevify init agents` block almost never reach for jevify, even on tasks it covers.

Evidence: 8 real tasks, each run by a haiku subagent with jevify on hand (instructions = the output of `jevify init agents`, called by full path) and by one without it. Tasks: branch by description, commit by description, a failed CI run on a tag, root cause in a 300-line CI log, a source file by content, tests by topic, issue triage into bug/feature/docs, the tool that renders a terminal demo. Result: jevify was called in 1 of 8 runs (T4, `jevify why < ci.log`, exit 0, answer right). Even there the agent went on to read the whole log (3 tool uses against 1 without jevify). Nobody used fill, pick, filter, label, is or route. Examples:

- T1 "which branch holds the allergy model work": the agent listed `git branch -a`, then grepped and used rev-parse (5 calls). `jevify fill -- git log -1 --format=%H '@{branch:the allergy model and its schema migration}'` answers it in one call (verified: exit 0, the right hash).
- T7 triage of 12 reports: the agent read all 12 files one by one (14 tool uses) instead of one `label` call. On the held-out sets, the one-marker classification of these 12 reports scored 12 of 12, and label on 30 report titles scored 29 of 30 (1 unsure).

Both arms reached the right answer in all 8 tasks, so jevify changed no outcome. The block names the verbs but shows the marker grammar in only one example. It lists no kinds and pairs no situation with a command ("you are about to list branches to choose one: use fill"). Jev as a judge over the 16 transcripts agrees with a hand check that no run used fill where a listing was read (15 of 16 no, 1 unsure).

Expected: the init agents block (and the skill) pairs each common situation with one complete command line: branch or commit by description via fill, a long log via why without then reading the whole log, many records via filter or label. It lists the kinds. Re-run the 8 tasks from the hunch-lpp report to measure adoption.

Suggested write set: src/cmd/agent.rs (init agents text and its test), plugins/jevify/skills/jevify/SKILL.md, docs/guide/agents.md.
close_reason: init agents pairs each situation with a complete command (24 lines), lists kinds; skill table and agents guide carry the same commands; gate green; adoption re-run moved to hunch-lpp

title: Follow-ups of hunch-bec and hunch-0pq: JEVIFY_DEADLINE in capabilities, test env, slow flow tests, changelog
description:
Outcome: the agent-facing contract names everything hunch-bec added, tests never inherit the developer's deadline, and the two slow flow tests run in seconds again.

1. Capabilities (src/cmd/agent.rs): add `{ "name": "JEVIFY_DEADLINE", "default": 600 }` (same shape as the other env entries) to `env`, and `usage` to the envelope `meta{...}` field description. tests/agent.rs asserts both.
2. tests/common/mod.rs `bin()`: `env_remove("JEVIFY_DEADLINE")`, next to the other JEVIFY_* removals (keep the K2 JEVIFY_CONFIG_DIR behaviour unchanged).
3. Slow tests: `tests/filter.rs::stdout_flows_before_last_answer_and_closed_pipe_cancels` (~127 s) and its twin in tests/label.rs (~120 s) delay every batch but the first by 3 s; since keyless batches hold 60 records (hunch-0it) that is about 41 delayed batches. Make each test prove the same properties (stdout flows before the last answer; a closed pipe cancels the rest) with far fewer batches or a shorter delay, so each runs under 10 s. Never weaken what the test proves.
4. CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased): add the line "`jevify init agents` pairs every situation with a complete command and lists the kinds; the skill and the agents guide do the same." (from hunch-0pq), under Changed.

Write set: src/cmd/agent.rs, tests/agent.rs, tests/common/mod.rs, tests/filter.rs, tests/label.rs, CHANGELOG.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md (only if the env table there lacks JEVIFY_DEADLINE).
Done when: the four items are in; the full gate passes (cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked --all-targets, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps, cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed Rust files); report the new durations of the two tests.
Rules: AGENTS.md applies.
close_reason: JEVIFY_DEADLINE and usage in capabilities, bin() removes JEVIFY_DEADLINE, flow tests 3.6 s each, changelog line; gate green

title: eval_why.py scores an untracked duplicate log and crashes on a null cost: corpus manifest with provenance, null-safe sum, recomputed hit@1
description:
Outcome: `scripts/eval_why.py` scores each distinct log once, from an explicit corpus with provenance per case, survives a null `meta.usage`/`cost_usd`, and the reported hit@1 for `why` is recomputed and recorded here.

Context (adversarial review round 8, 2026-09-22, both reviewers; verified in the working tree on 2026-09-22):
- scripts/eval_why.py:16 is `cases = sorted(Path("evals/why").glob("*.log"))`: every `*.log` in evals/why/, tracked or not. The directory holds 22 logs; `md5 -q evals/why/go-04.log evals/why/go-05.log` gives the same hash (7510ebda1b00b01dbdfe2bb74f8c846e), so 21 unique logs. go-05.log and go-05.expect are untracked (git status); go-05.expect lacks `license` and a source URL. The duplicate is scored twice, so the 19/22 hit@1 reported in hunch-s2k is over the wrong denominator (hunch-lpp's 0.7.0 run reports why hit@1 18/23 over a different set).
- scripts/eval_why.py:48 is `cost += v["meta"]["cost_usd"]`: since 0.8.0 a token count left unknown is `null`, and a null cost raises TypeError and ends the run after paying for the requests before it.
- Deleting evals/why/go-05.log, evals/why/go-05.expect and the empty f1-testify-commits.txt is the owner's decision (AGENTS.md: never rm); this bead never deletes a file. Until the owner answers, the duplicate stays on disk and the manifest excludes it.

Files (write set): scripts/eval_why.py; a corpus manifest in evals/why/ (for example evals/why/corpus.jsonl or a `cases` section of evals/why/README.md, one entry per case: id, source URL or origin, license, root-cause range, content hash); evals/out/ (regenerated results). Everything else, and every log and .expect file, is read-only.

Done when:
- The script reads the manifest (or dedupes by content hash) and scores one case per distinct log; a log absent from the manifest is reported as skipped, never scored.
- Each manifest entry has a provenance field (source URL or "hand-written", plus license); the script fails with a named error on a case whose manifest entry lacks it.
- The cost sum is null-safe: a null `cost_usd` counts as unknown and the summary prints the number of cases with unknown cost, never a crash.
- hit@1 and hit@3 are recomputed on the deduplicated corpus with the 0.8.1 binary (`cargo build --release`, TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key in the command's environment; keyless if no key) and the figures, the model, the date and the case count are appended to this bead's notes; a run that cannot happen is reported as NOT RUN.

title: Contract: no README example acts on exit 3 or 4; route exits 3 on a near tie (margin above the 0.06 jitter)
description:
Outcome: the exit-code contract holds where it is stated and where it is shown. README's shell example no longer prints success on an abstention or an outage, and `route` abstains (exit 3) when the two best commands are too close to tell apart, as docs/VISION.md:18-19 promises ("when no candidate fits or two are too close, jevify says so with exit code 3 and changes nothing").

Context (review round 9, synthesis section 1, both P1; blocks the next release):
1. README.md:135 `cargo build 2>&1 | jevify is 'the build failed' || echo 'build is fine'` prints "build is fine" on exit 3 (unsure) and exit 4 (backend unavailable or quota reached). It contradicts README.md:218-227 (the exit table and "write the condition so that yes means act; `&&` acts on 0 only") and docs/VISION.md:18-19. Raised by astra and sol. Fix: delete the `||` example (lines 133-136, the `refund` example above it stays); if an `is` example is wanted there, it must use `&&` on exit 0.
2. `route` names a near tie and still exits 0. src/cmd/run.rs:119-126 builds `ties` (commands above threshold within `TIE_MARGIN` of the best), run.rs:193 returns `Exit::Ok` with the winner in `data.tool`; the doc comment at run.rs:12-13 argues that route prints and starts nothing, so a tie names every tied command instead of abstaining. VISION says exit 3. Raised by all four reviewers. Worse, `TIE_MARGIN = 0.05` (run.rs:14) is below the measured uncached probability jitter of 0.06 for identical requests (docs/guide/how-it-works.md:166-168), and the motivating case, "pretty-print a JSON file" going to json_pp at 0.93 with jq third at 0.87 on TypeSafe and to jq at 1.00 with json_pp at 0.99 on classifier.dev (benchmarks/results.md:145-149), is 0.06 apart on TypeSafe, so the rule would not even have fired there.

Shape decided here: when `tool` is above threshold and `fit - next <= TIE_MARGIN`, `route` exits 3 with `data.tool` null, `data.ties` holding the tied commands (the winner first) and the human line naming them, the same way the below-threshold branch at run.rs:165 abstains; `TIE_MARGIN` becomes 0.10, above the 0.06 jitter so one jitter width cannot flip an answer into a decision, with that justification in the constant's doc comment. Count how many of the 169 decisions of the frozen set (benchmarks/results.md:94-122) fall within the new margin and record it next to the constant and in results.md; if the count is large, say so rather than shrink the margin.

Files (write set): README.md (lines 133-136 only), src/cmd/run.rs, tests/run_route.rs and tests/decision.rs, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md:86 (route data line), docs/guide/verbs.md (route exit line), docs/guide/agents.md:113 (add `ties`), CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased entry), benchmarks/results.md (the margin count). Everything else read-only.

Done when: the `||` example is gone and no README example acts on anything but exit 0; a wiremock test shows two commands within the margin exit 3 with both named in `data.ties` and a gap wider than the margin exits 0; the margin's justification cites the 0.06 jitter; docs and capabilities describe the exit; the unslop audit reports nothing on the touched prose. Gate before handing back (AGENTS.md, sandbox disabled): cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs <changed files>. Never weaken a test to pass. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
close_reason: route abstains on a near tie (exit 3, tool null, tied commands in data.ties), margin 0.05 -> 0.10 justified against the measured 0.06 jitter and recorded in results.md (8 of 24 frozen route decisions tie, 4 per backend, all within 0.05); the README example acting on a failing exit code is removed; contract tests cover the tie and the wider gap; the lead updated the two capabilities strings

title: label/pick --files: an unreadable excerpt falls back to the file name silently and confidently
description: Seen in the hunch-iu8 pilot (jevify 0.9.1, T7 with-arm): under a sandbox-exec profile that denies file-read-data on an ancestor directory of the reports (eval/) while allowing the reports' own directory (eval/sets/), `ls sets/ctx/t*.md | jevify label --files bug,feature,docs` labelled all 12 reports 'docs' (p 0.77-0.99), exit 0, 'labelled 12 of 12, 0 unsure', excerpts_withheld 0. Outside the sandbox the same command gives 5 bug / 4 feature / 2 docs / 1 unsure. Cause: records::excerpts -> cmd::sort::excerpt -> open_dir walks every path component from / with openat(O_DIRECTORY); the denied ancestor fails the open, open_regular errors, and excerpt() returns the bare file name; the record is then judged on its name alone (t01.md -> 'docs'), and nothing reports it: withheld() only counts secret-looking paths and symlinks. cat/wc/python read the same file fine in that sandbox (they open the leaf directly). Expected: a file whose content could not be read is counted (excerpts_withheld or a new counter), named on stderr, and either left unsure or its p marked as name-only; an agent cannot tell a name-only label from a content label today. Reproduce: profile '(version 1)(allow default)(deny file-read-data (subpath "<parent>"))(allow file-read-data (subpath "<parent>/sets"))', run from a cwd outside <parent>. Affects label --files and pick --files (shared excerpt).
notes:
Decision (hunch-3fj): an unreadable excerpt is neither an error nor a policy withholding; it is missing evidence, and the verdict on that record abstains.

Against docs/VISION.md: incomplete evidence cannot authorize a verdict; 'nothing fits' is an answer; filter keeps what it is unsure about (an extra record costs a glance, a dropped one the whole input); pick and fill abstain. An exit-6 error for the whole input would refuse 11 readable reports because of one unreadable one, and a missing path is the caller's normal input (an existing contract test lists 'a.txt' that does not exist). A per-record abstention keeps every record in the output, in order, and makes the missing evidence visible where the verdict is.

Against the withholding policy in src/records.rs: withheld() is a choice jevify makes that the caller can predict from the name (dot components, id_*, *.pem, *.key, credentials, secret, symlinks), and a withheld record is still judged by its name (label: 'bug<TAB>.npmrc' in tests/label.rs). Unreadability is environmental (missing, a directory in its place, EACCES/EPERM on the file or on a directory above it, as under the T7 sandbox profile) and the caller cannot predict it, so a name-only verdict would pass for a content verdict: that is the T7 defect (12 of 12 'docs' at p 0.77-0.99). The two are told apart in code (records::Unread{count, unreadable: BTreeMap<index, reason>}) but share one number: excerpts_withheld counts both, so a caller who reads one field learns that N records were judged without their content; no new envelope counter, no capabilities change. What changes per verb: filter and label never ask about an unreadable record (its name is not sent), print it unsure ('?' / verdict unsure, p 0, kept unless --strict), add unreadable: REASON to its --json record, and name it on stderr as 'jevify VERB: excerpt unreadable: PATH: REASON' (first ten, then 'K more'). All records unreadable: exit 3 with zero requests. pick counts and names an unreadable finalist and lets it compete on its name, as a withheld finalist already does (pick's first stage ranks names by design). Missing paths and directories that were silent before are now counted and named (records.rs inline test updated from 9 to 11).

Mechanism: sort::read_excerpt(p) -> io::Result<String> propagates open_regular/read errors (open_dir walks from / with openat, so a denied ancestor surfaces here); sort::excerpt keeps its name-only fallback for sort's own use. records::excerpt_of returns Ok(Some) excerpt, Ok(None) withheld, Err(reason) unreadable.

Verification: contract tests in tests/label.rs (directory, chmod 000 file, missing path; all-unreadable exit 3 with no request), tests/filter.rs (kept/strict, --json unreadable field), tests/pick.rs (directory finalist counted and named); records.rs inline tests. evals/validation: no adjudicated case uses --files (pick cases read *-files.txt record lists without excerpts), so none applies. The sandbox-exec profile of benchmarks/agents/PILOT.md T7 fails at the same openat in open_dir as the chmod case (EPERM instead of EACCES) and takes the same Err path; not re-run under sandbox-exec here.
close_reason: An unreadable excerpt is missing evidence, not a policy withholding: filter and label never ask about the record, leave it unsure with the reason on its record and on stderr, and exit 3 with no request when every record is unreadable; pick names and counts it. Both kinds share excerpts_withheld so the envelope keeps its shape; tests cover a directory, a chmod 000 file, a missing path and the all-unreadable case

title: why: finalists are pushed unconditionally, so keyless finals can exceed the 99-label window
description:
Outcome: `why`'s finals request never exceeds the keyless backend's label capacity; finalists are counted against the window before panic lines are added.

Context (review round 9, synthesis section 3, P2, raised by astra; verified by reading, not reproduced): src/cmd/why.rs:257-268 pushes every finalist of `first.finalists` into `chosen` unconditionally (:259-262) and only the panic-block loop checks `chosen.len() >= ctx.backend.window()` (:264). With n finalists per window over several windows plus panic lines, `chosen` can exceed the classifier.dev window (99 labels plus `any`), and the request fails with exit 6 `api_rejected_request` on a log that round one handled. Whether the finalist count alone can exceed the window depends on n and the window count; the bead first states the maximum (n × windows for a 1,000-line log) and then guards it.

Fix: reserve the finalist slots first (truncate finalists to the window, by rank), then fill the remainder with panic lines; a finalist dropped for room is recorded in `round_one` (once the opt-in bead lands) or at least never silently.

Files (write set): src/cmd/why.rs, tests/why.rs (a wiremock test with enough windows and a panic block that the unguarded code would exceed 99 labels; assert the request's label count), docs/guide/verbs.md (why) if the rule is user-visible. Everything else read-only.

Done when: the maximum finals size for a 1,000-line log is written next to the guard; the test above passes and shows the request at or under the window; no behaviour change when the finals fit. Gate before handing back (AGENTS.md, sandbox disabled): cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs <changed files>. Never weaken a test to pass. Workers never commit; the lead commits.

title: Semantic operands: put meaning into the arguments of any command
description:
Vision (owner, 2026-09-20): put meaning into the operands of any command. A command line is head, flags, operands. `run` fills the head by meaning from PATH and man pages. This epic fills operands by meaning from real objects: the user writes the command, grevi replaces a description with an existing handle (a path by default; a branch, a commit, a process for commands that take those). The grammar is user-written and every value exists, so "point, never generate" holds.

    grevi code "where man pages are parsed"
    grevi git switch "payment timeout fix"
    grevi pytest "the tests about token expiry"

Boundaries found in design review:
- `add` stays a verb: it stages hunks, and a path-level `git add` would stage unrelated hunks of the same file.
- `why`, `is`, `pick`, `filter` are the output side and are already universal through a pipe.
- The governing plan says unvalidated command grammar remains a proposal, and `run` executes only zero-argument true, false, pwd, ls. Executing a user-written argv with substituted handles needs an explicit spec decision (child bead). Until then the wrapper resolves and prints.
- Privacy: round one sends path names only; content excerpts go out for the finalists only.

Children: the files domain for pick; the resolving wrapper (proposal only); the execution policy decision; command-specific domains (branches, commits, processes); many-operand resolution on top of filter (hunch-bx6).
notes: 2026-09-20 planning round 2: five competing plans (lead, Opus, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol; a Fable plan pending) blended into docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-jevify.md (untracked, uncommitted; the v1-to-v2 diff sits beside it). Agreed: explicit @ marker only; print only; one crate and one binary named jevify; domains are data in one record protocol {identity, handle, evidence}; the pipe is the first domain; first built-in sources are commit, branch, PR, CI run, capped at one backend window; files are not a default domain (hunch-744 stays paused). Order: filter (hunch-bx6) -> budget and quota (hunch-glz) -> held-out experiment as go/no-go -> rename and wrapper. crates.io: jevify 0.0.1 placeholder published 2026-09-20. git remote now points at tpellet/jevify.

title: filter unsure band never fires: a record that says nothing is a confident no
description:
Found by the hunch-evl paired pilot, from the frozen validation set (jevify 0.8.3, jev-1.13.0,
both backends, 2026-09-22).

The unsure band of `filter` never fires on records that say nothing either way. Of the 40 adjudicated
`filter` cases (two independent annotators, gold held apart from the manifest), four have an
adjudicated gold of `unsure`: the subjects `Merge branch 'pr-248'`, `'pr-245'`, `'pr-244'`, `'pr-240'`
under the statement "the change is a bug fix". A merge subject with a branch number says neither yes
nor no. The verb drops all four, at 0.13-0.17 on TypeSafe and 0.00-0.01 keyless, far below the
0.35-0.65 band: "the record does not say" is read as a confident no.

The rest of the set decides cleanly: keep-gold 17/17 kept on both backends, drop-gold 19/19 dropped,
lowest keep-gold score 0.77 / 0.79, highest drop-gold score 0.28 / 0.20. So the problem is not the
threshold and not the width of the band; no band placed inside [0, 1] separates these four from the
correct noes, because the model answers them as noes. The same reading appears on `is`: the two
cases whose gold is `unsure` (a fact the document does not address) score 0.03-0.05 and 0.00.

Consequence: a caller who pipes records through `filter` to decide an action cannot tell "the record
says no" from "the record does not say". The band promises a distinction the scores do not carry.

Expected: either the statement put to the model separates "false" from "not stated" (a second
question, or a Noul that asks whether the record addresses the statement at all), or the band and
the documentation stop promising a distinction that is not measurable and say what `filter` actually
answers. Whichever way it goes, re-measure on the four cases named above.

Suggested write set: src/cmd/filter.rs (the question put to the model, the band), src/cmd/is.rs if
the same change applies, tests/filter.rs, docs that describe the unsure band, benchmarks/results.md
next to the measurement.
close_reason: filter judges each record three ways (holds, does not hold, does not say); kept at P(holds) >= threshold+band, dropped at P(does not hold) >= the same mark, unsure otherwise; threshold and band unchanged. On the 40 adjudicated cases the four unsure golds abstain on both backends, false actions 4 -> 0, keep recall 17/17, 3 to 6 drop golds move to unsure (kept, per asymmetric doubt)

title: round_one is opt-in and finalists reports the finals actually judged (fill widening, why panic lines)
description:
Outcome: `meta.decision.round_one` is opt-in and, when asked for, tells the truth about the finals: `finalists` is the set of candidates the finals actually judged, not the shortlist taken before `fill` widened it or `why` added panic lines.

Context (review round 9, synthesis section 1, P2, raised by all four reviewers): `Shortlist::record` (src/tournament.rs:98-114) writes every candidate of every window into the envelope on every run; there is no flag (`grep round_one src/cli.rs` is empty), and the field is frozen into `capabilities` (src/cmd/agent.rs:175) and the contract test tests/agent.rs:251-272, which asserts the field string and the ROBOT_MODE sentence. The data is `{index, p}` only (tournament.rs:99-102), so this is not a leak; the problems are envelope size on a 1,000-line `why` or a 1,900-command `route`, and a contract frozen around a misreport. The misreport: `fill` records the shortlists at src/cmd/fill.rs:257-260 and then widens the finals at fill.rs:379-386 (every candidate with p > 0, up to MAX_FINALISTS); `why` pushes finalists and then adds panic-block lines at src/cmd/why.rs:257-268. So docs/ROBOT_MODE.md:245-252 "the rank of any item, and whether it reached the finals, reads from one run" is false for those two verbs.

Fix: a `--decision` (or `JEVIFY_DECISION=round_one`; pick one and state it once) opt-in that turns `round_one` on; off by default, `gates` stays. `finalists` is recorded after the finals set is final: the verbs pass the actual finals membership to `record` (or record in two steps). Update capabilities, ROBOT_MODE.md:245-252, the contract test, and the CHANGELOG (0.9.1 introduced it as always-on, hunch-6ru).

Files (write set): src/cli.rs, src/tournament.rs, src/cmd/fill.rs, src/cmd/why.rs, src/cmd/pick.rs and src/cmd/run.rs (the record call sites), src/cmd/agent.rs, src/output.rs, tests/agent.rs, tests/fill.rs, tests/why.rs, tests/decision.rs, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, docs/guide/agents.md, CHANGELOG.md. Everything else read-only.

Done when: a default run carries no `round_one`; with the opt-in, a wiremock `fill` whose finals were widened and a `why` whose finals gained panic lines both report `finalists` equal to the set the finals request contained (assert against the recorded request body); tests/agent.rs asserts the new contract; ROBOT_MODE's "reads from one run" sentence is true again or removed. Gate before handing back (AGENTS.md, sandbox disabled): cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs <changed files>. Never weaken a test to pass. Workers never commit; the lead commits.

title: The README's commit demo works for a reader who types it
description:
The transcript drift check (hunch-d7ni) found its first stale demo on the day it was written, which
is the point of it, but the demo is the README's main one and it is stale now.

README.md:48 and docs/guide/getting-started.md:135 print:

    git log --oneline -30 | jevify fill --field 1 --dry-run -- git show --stat --format=%s '@{-:made route abstain when two commands are too close}'

The answer, 317cbf7, is now the 37th commit, so a plain `-30` window no longer holds it. A reader
who types the command today gets an abstention. The check itself still tests the behaviour, because
it pins the listing to d24e109, the commit that wrote the transcript; the pages do not.

docs/demo/examples.sh has the same command unpinned, and its `@{commit:ports the user interface to
Android}` nothing-fits case now runs over 267 commits rather than the number it was measured at.

Fix the pages so a reader who types the command gets the printed answer, and keep it from rotting
again within a month. Choose between these and say which and why:
(a) Widen the window to a number that holds the target with room to spare, and re-record. Simple,
    but it rots again, only later, and the check will tell us.
(b) Re-record the demo against a recent commit, so the target sits near the top of a small window.
    It reads naturally and rots fastest.
(c) Change the demo so its candidate list is not this repository's moving history: a fixed file, a
    tagged range, or a listing the reader supplies.
Measure before you choose: run each candidate form four times on both backends and keep only a form
that resolves 4 of 4 on both. Paste what the binary printed.

Whatever ships, the three places must agree: README.md, docs/guide/getting-started.md and
docs/demo/examples.sh. Then update the expectation row in tests/transcripts.rs so the check follows
the page, and run the check on both backends to prove it passes:
    cargo test --test transcripts -- --ignored --test-threads=1
    TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=<key> cargo test --test transcripts -- --ignored --test-threads=1

Also check the nothing-fits case in docs/demo/examples.sh still abstains 4 of 4 on both backends at
the current history size, since it was measured at a smaller one. If it no longer does, say so and
leave it; a new phrase is its own bead.

Write set: README.md, docs/guide/getting-started.md, docs/demo/examples.sh, tests/transcripts.rs.
Done when: the command a reader can copy resolves on both backends, four runs of four; the three
places agree; the drift check passes on both backends with the updated row; the gate passes (cargo
fmt --check, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --locked --
--test-threads=1). Workers never commit; the lead commits.
close_reason: Chose option (c): the candidate list is git log --oneline v0.8.3..v0.9.3, thirty commits between two tags, which cannot move. Rot estimate zero. Rejected -60 and a recent-commit re-record (both 4/4 but rot in about four days) and -200 (keyless 0 of 4, once the wrong commit). README, getting-started and examples.sh agree; the drift check passes on both backends. The nothing-fits case still abstains 4 of 4 at 268 commits.

title: dir kind: finalists carry no content evidence, so content descriptions abstain
description:
Found by the hunch-lpp evaluation (jevify 0.7.0, jev-1.13.0, 2026-09-22).

Evidence: the dir kind sends only the directory path, so a description of what a directory holds is not found even when the right directory ranks first. On the held-out set of 9 dir descriptions (evaluator-written gold), 6 resolved and 3 abstained. Every abstention was a content description:

    jevify fill --dry-run -- ls '@{dir:the failure logs used to evaluate the root-cause verb}'   -> no_match (gold evals/why), candidates 33
    jevify fill --dry-run -- ls '@{dir:the agent skill}'                                          -> no_match (gold plugins/jevify/skills/jevify)
    (testify repo) ls '@{dir:the app services}'                                                   -> ambiguous, closest testify-app/Testify/Services 0.42
    jevify pick --from dir --verbose 'the test helpers with the fake Jev server'
      -> no_match; closest: tests/common, tests; any 0.37

In the pick case the right directory ranks first, but the absolute Noul (any 0.37) stays under the 0.5 threshold, so the verb says nothing fits. The file kind adds first lines in round two; the dir kind has no tier-two evidence (capabilities: "dir: directory path").

Expected: dir finalists carry some evidence of their contents, such as the names of their first children or a count by extension, the way file finalists carry first lines. Content descriptions then reach the threshold. Re-measure with the held-out set in the hunch-lpp report (fill-dir, pick-from dir).

Suggested write set: src/source.rs (dir enrichment), src/cmd/fill.rs and src/cmd/pick.rs only if the finals text hook needs it, tests/fill.rs, docs/guide/kinds.md, the capabilities kind evidence string in src/cmd/agent.rs.

title: What the answer cache retains, and whether the documents admit it
description:
A harness trial closed with one question it did not answer, and the answer decides how wide the
secret-retention surface is.

The saved-input store is understood: `why` and `filter` write raw stdin under
$JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR/outputs/, and hunch-abw8 gave it a seven-day bound and the JEVIFY_NO_SAVE switch.
The answer cache is a separate store under the same cache directory. The open question: does a
cached ANSWER also retain raw record text, or only a digest of the redacted request?

If it retains record text, the retention surface is not "`why` and `filter`, suppressible with
--no-save" but "every verb that caches, suppressible only with --no-cache", and PRIVACY.md and the
guides currently tell an operator the narrower story.

Find out, from the code and then from a real cache entry:
1. Read the cache writer and the key derivation. docs/ROBOT_MODE.md says answer cache keys use
   redacted requests, expire after seven days and never cross backend, endpoint or decision
   contract versions. Check what the VALUE holds, not the key.
2. Run each caching verb once against the keyless backend with a distinctive synthetic secret in
   its input, then read every file the run created under the cache directory and say exactly what
   of the input survives in each. Use a secret that cannot collide with anything real and say in
   the report what you used, not its value.
3. Report per verb: what is written, where, in what form, whether redaction applied, what switches
   it off, and the retention.

Then make the documents match whatever you find. If the cache holds record text, PRIVACY.md's
per-verb table, the configuration guide, ROBOT_MODE and the capability strings must say so, and
the operator must be told which switch actually stops it. If it holds only digests, say that
explicitly too, because a reader today cannot tell and the safe assumption is the worse one.

If you find that the cache retains more than the documents admit, do not fix the behaviour in this
bead: report it with the evidence and say what changing it would cost, in cache hit rate and in
code. The documents come first; a behaviour change is its own bead with its own measurement.

Write set: PRIVACY.md, docs/guide/configuration.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, src/cmd/agent.rs
(capability strings only), evals/cache-retention/** for the evidence.
Done when: the answer is established from the code and from a real cache entry for every caching
verb; the documents state it; anything the documents got wrong is named in the report with what a
fix would cost. Gate: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings,
cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed files. Workers never commit; the lead
commits.
close_reason: Commit d9ec3fb. The answer cache value is the Response struct alone: no record text, excerpt, path or question text reaches disk, and the request survives only as the blake3 in the file name. A planted marker appeared in 2 saved-input files and 0 of 30 answer files across all nine caching verbs; the four output-only verbs do not cache. Six document faults fixed, including two stores the docs never mentioned. Three behaviours priced and left to hunch-c84o: --no-cache does not cover the tool inventory, it relocates the sort journal rather than suppressing it, and expired answers are never deleted.

title: pick --files: find a file by meaning, names first, content for finalists
description:
`grevi pick --files <DIR> "<description>"`: the candidates are the regular files under DIR instead of stdin lines, and the match prints as a path usable from the current directory. This is the engine of the semantic-operand epic and is useful alone: `code "$(grevi pick --files . "where man pages are parsed")"`.

Enumeration: inside a git work tree, `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard` under DIR, so .gitignore is respected with no new dependency; elsewhere a std::fs walk that does not follow symlinks. Any path with a component that starts with `.` is skipped in both modes. Paths are sorted (option order is part of the request). More than pick's MAX_LINES candidates is exit 6 with a hint to choose a narrower DIR.

Two rounds through tournament::rank, no new round: round one ranks path names only; the finals round re-ranks at most 24 finalists with `finalist_text` = path plus the first 2,000 characters of the file, redacted (the sort excerpt helper, shared, not copied). So file content of at most 24 files leaves the machine per call, and names of all candidates do.

Gate unchanged: the `any` Noul at the threshold and the winner above NONE; otherwise exit 3. `-n` works as for stdin. `--index` with `--files` is a usage error. Envelope: `data.matches[{line, text, p}]` keeps its shape with `text` = the path; `data.source` = "files".

Contract work: cli.rs help, capabilities, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, docs/guide/verbs.md, README pick section, a PRIVACY.md row (names of all candidate files, excerpts of up to 24), the skill file. Tests: unit tests for enumeration (hidden components, symlinks, sorting, the cap) and contract tests with FakeJev (a file found by content in the finals round, abstention, usage errors, the envelope).

Gate: full quality gate. Live: a recorded spot check on this repository with 10 descriptions whose target file is fixed in advance; report hit@1, requests, latency. Numbers only from recorded runs.
notes: 2026-09-20: paused by the owner before completion; planning panel first (epic hunch-4z4). Uncommitted work in the shared checkout: src/cmd/pick.rs (--files mode, enumeration, unit tests), src/cmd/sort.rs (excerpt made pub(crate)), src/cli.rs (flag and help), src/lib.rs (dispatch), tests/pick.rs (two contract tests). State: cargo fmt and cargo check --all-targets pass; clippy, tests, ubs, docs, capabilities, PRIVACY row NOT done. Do not commit these paths until the design is settled.
close_reason: pick --files DIR delivered: names first, content for at most 24 finalists; hidden, ignored and symlinked files skipped; docs, capabilities, PRIVACY row, skill, unit and contract tests. Gate: fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, tests (all pass), ubs exit 0. Live spot check 2026-09-20, keyless backend, this repository (160 files), 10 author-written descriptions, one uncached run: 5 of 9 existing targets at top-1, 1 wrong accept (docs/guide/verbs.md for PRIVACY.md, p 0.46), 3 abstentions on existing targets (any 0.51-0.62 or 0.19, NONE won the finals), the 1 negative abstained; 3 requests and 740-1425 ms per call. Author-written queries are an upper bound; files stay a weak domain (see hunch-4z4).

title: jevify two sides: the language, fill, kinds, label
description:
Outcome: jevify speaks one language on the two sides of a command. Input side: `fill` resolves '@{kind:description}' markers to real handles and becomes the command. Output side: `why`, `pick`, `filter`, `label`, `is`; `pick`, `filter` and `label` share one byte-exact record model, `why` points and keeps its own format; `route` only prints. Kinds are coded listers or one-line recipes.

Context: docs/VISION.md decides the product. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md decides the code and is the source of truth for every child bead; the children transcribe it. Grammar: `jevify VERB [options] ['text'…] [-- COMMAND ARGS…]`. Removed with no shim in Phase 1: `why -- CMD`, the verb name `run`, `run --yes`, `run --exec`, `run --dry-run`, `run --no-args`, the run argument pass, `pick --files DIR`, the global short flag `-v`.

Owner decisions (plan §9), final:
- No file is renamed or removed. src/cmd/run.rs keeps its name and holds `route`; src/args.rs stays on disk outside the module tree; tests/run_args.rs and tests/run_route.rs are rewritten in place.
- fill becomes the command through exec; the command's exit code comes through.
- An unsure flag abstains.
- One pool rule for every caller of `tournament::rank`: finalists per window n = 3 when 3 x windows <= W, else 2 when 2 x windows <= W, else 1; always by rank inside a window, never by a probability from another request. Capacity W x W (9,801 keyless; on TypeSafe the ceiling of 20,000 is reached first). fill uses n = 3 only, so its limit stays F = W x (W / 3). pick, pick --from and why use the full rule; why keeps MAX_KEEP = 4000.
- Per-record verbs use ask_each (the batch request of classifier.dev); independence of records is a property of the classifier backend only. meta.model stays a string, distinct models joined with ", "; fill refuses an answer when any part is not from Jev.
- `filter -v` is inversion; `--verbose` has no short flag. `--files` is a boolean on pick, filter and label. `why` is exempt from the byte-for-byte rule and takes no split option. `is` with one statement prints nothing.
- Saved inputs are content-addressed and never pruned by jevify. Only why and filter save.
- The absolute path in `source_repo_path` of the tracker export (hunch-nay) does not block this work.

Shape: each phase has a serial skeleton bead that alone writes the shared files (Cargo.toml, src/cli.rs, src/lib.rs, src/cmd/mod.rs, src/exit.rs, src/input.rs, src/output.rs), parallel beads with disjoint write sets, and contract beads (src/cmd/agent.rs, documents, skill, manifests) that wait for the behaviour they document. The version bump and `bash scripts/release.sh <full commit SHA>` belong to the release beads, which the lead does.

Division of work: workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 or reach ~/.ssh. A worker runs fmt, check, clippy, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps` and ubs, tries the tests and reports them as NOT RUN when the sandbox blocks them; the lead runs the full test gate, and only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes a bead. Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. No language feature newer than Rust 1.87; CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0.

The tracker: workers change bead state with `br update` only and never stage .beads/. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.

- Phase 1: hunch-7zg.1 (1.0), hunch-7zg.2 (1.1), hunch-7zg.3 (1.2), hunch-7zg.4 (1.3), hunch-7zg.5 (1.4), hunch-bx6 (1.5), hunch-7zg.6 (1.6), hunch-7zg.7 (1.7), hunch-sb9 (1.8 skill), hunch-7zg.8 (1.8 documents), hunch-7zg.22 (1.9 scripts and demo files); release 0.5.0 hunch-7zg.9

- Phase 3: hunch-7zg.15, hunch-7zg.16, hunch-7zg.17, hunch-7zg.18
- Phase 4: hunch-7zg.19, hunch-qxn, hunch-7zg.20; release 0.7.0 hunch-7zg.21

Outside the epic, ordered behind it: hunch-lpp (evaluation, after hunch-7zg.21), hunch-glz (quota measurement and its documentation; after hunch-7zg.3 and hunch-7zg.18), hunch-bec (after hunch-glz), hunch-4ow (demo.gif and demo.cast; after hunch-7zg.22 and hunch-glz; it does not block release 0.5.0), hunch-60l (README voice; after hunch-glz and hunch-4ow), hunch-3te (in progress elsewhere; after hunch-7zg.22). title: 1.0 Language skeleton and grammar cutover (shared files, final Outcome, route signature, -v, --files, init agents)
description:
Plan bead: 1.0 skeleton — language skeleton and grammar cutover. Epic hunch-7zg. This is the serial bead of Phase 1: it alone writes the shared files and it leaves the tree green so that 1.1–1.8 run in parallel.

Outcome: the CLI grammar is `jevify VERB [options] ['text'…] [-- COMMAND ARGS…]`. The verb `run` is `route` with its final signature, `why` takes no command, `filter` exists as a stub, `-v` belongs to `filter`, `--files` is a boolean, `init agents` parses, `Outcome` has its final shape, and the stub modules that the parallel beads fill compile.

Context: plan §1 (contract, what is removed, the three bullets under "Removed"), §2 "Changed in place", §2.3 first paragraph, §2.4 (save directory), §3 Phase 1 (the two "cutover" paragraphs), §4 (clap). Decisions, final:
- Removed with no shim: `why -- CMD`, the verb name `run`, `run --yes`, `run --exec`, `run --dry-run`, `run --no-args`, `pick --files DIR`, the global short flag `-v`. `jevify run 'x'` and `jevify why -- true` exit 2, and the one-line message gives the new form (`jevify route 'x'`; `CMD 2>&1 | jevify why`).
- `filter -v` is inversion, as `grep -v`. The global short flag `-v` of `--verbose` (src/cli.rs:36, `#[arg(short, long, global = true)]`) is removed; `--verbose` stays. tests/cli_basics.rs:52 passes `-v` for verbosity: it passes `--verbose`. Test filter inversion parsing separately from verbosity: `is 'x' -v` is exit 2; `filter -v 'x'` parses.
- `--files` is a boolean on `pick` and `filter` (and on `label` in bead 4.0): the records on stdin are paths. `pick --files DIR` (`files: Option<PathBuf>`, src/cli.rs:66-67) leaves with no shim; the form is `git ls-files | jevify pick --files 'q'` (or `fd`). The existing two-stage engine stays (path names first, excerpts for the finalists); only the source of the paths changes. To keep the tree green this bead makes src/cmd/pick.rs take the paths from its stdin lines where it walks DIR today (:27-34; `canonical_dir` :128-, `list_files` :152 and their inline tests leave with the walk, since clippy allows no dead code), and moves the `--files` tests of tests/pick.rs (:137-, :208, :230) to the stdin form with their assertions. hunch-7zg.7 completes the rewrite in place (byte records, -0, the withholding function, relative paths). `pick --index` stays as it is; `--index` with `--files` stays exit 2.
- `why` is exempt from the byte-for-byte rule: it prints each line with its number and context, as today. `Why` gets NO split option: no -0, no --para, no --files. It loses `cmd` and gains --no-save. The byte rule covers `pick`, `filter` and `label`.
- `init agents`: `Init { shell }` (src/cli.rs:154-161, `Shell::{Zsh,Bash}`) gains the value `agents`; rename the enum if that reads better. Add the dispatch arm; until hunch-7zg.8 writes the block, the arm prints the verb list of `capabilities` and `jevify capabilities --json` as the source of truth (a correct, short block, not a stub error).
- `Outcome` changes once, here (src/cmd/mod.rs): `human: Vec<u8>` (:15 is String) and `exec: Option<Exec>` with `struct Exec { argv: Vec<OsString>, stdin_null: bool }`. Set `exec: None` at every construction site in src/cmd/*.rs. `run_cli` ignores `exec` until bead 2.0 (hunch-7zg.10), which adds no field to `Outcome`. If clippy flags the unread field, read it in a debug assertion in `run_cli` (`debug_assert!(out.exec.is_none())`) rather than allow dead code.
- The final `route` signature is set here: `cmd::run::run(ctx, intent, machine)`; `RunFlags` is removed (src/lib.rs:257-275 builds it today; src/cmd/run.rs defines it). In src/cmd/run.rs make the smallest change that compiles and never executes: the body behaves as `dry_run: true, no_args: true` did. hunch-7zg.5 (1.4) then deletes the execution code behind the signature.
- The seven tests that use the removed flags are rewritten here, in place, to exit-2 and print-only assertions: the five execution tests of tests/run_args.rs (`unsupported_cp_grammar_never_executes_even_without_placeholders` :5, `machine_mode_never_executes_without_exec_and_yes` :51, `exec_and_yes_run_the_command_via_argv` :79, `executed_child_output_never_corrupts_the_envelope` :115, `never_exec_tools_are_shown_not_run` :150) and the two of tests/run_route.rs (`routes_to_the_tool` :11, `abstains_when_nothing_installed_fits` :51). Each keeps its subject: `--yes`, `--exec`, `--dry-run`, `--no-args` after `route` are exit 2; `route` prints the tool and a sentinel file proves no child started; abstain is exit 3. This is the owner-approved removal of `run`, not a weakened test. `init_zsh_defines_comma_alias` (tests/run_args.rs:190) asserts `jevify route`.
- Dispatch is FINAL after this bead: it passes every parsed flag, so no later Phase 1 bead touches src/lib.rs (except the `pub mod args;` line of bead 1.4). The exact signatures that this bead installs and wires (a worker may adjust a parameter type if the code demands it, but the set of parameters is fixed):
    `filter::run(ctx, statement: &str, flags: FilterFlags { invert, count, strict, split, files, no_save }, machine: bool)`
    `why::run(ctx, context: usize, top: usize, no_save: bool)`
    `pick::run(ctx, intent: &str, top: usize, index: bool, split: Split, files: bool)`
    `is::run(ctx, statements: &[String], context: Option<&Path>)`
  `Split` is an enum in src/records.rs (`Lines`, `Nul`, `Para`) that the stub of this bead defines; `FilterFlags` lives in src/cmd/filter.rs. If `is` keeps its band argument, it stays a parameter too.
- Every clap help string of src/cli.rs is rewritten for the 0.5.0 grammar: the top-level `after_help` (:9), `Pick` (:54 and the `--files` doc at :65-66), `Why` (:69-71: "stdin, or `-- <cmd>` to run it", the `jevify why -- cargo test` example, `child_exit` in the `--json data:` line), `Is` (:107: the shell loop over `is`, the data line for several statements), `Init` (:154: "`,` alias for `jevify run`"), and the new `Route`, `Filter` strings. hunch-7zg.8 may refine help strings and `--json data:` lines later; nothing else in this file changes after this bead.
- Every test the cutover changes, all under the owner-approved removal (none is a weakened test): the seven tests above; tests/why.rs:32 (`why_runs_a_command_after_double_dash`) becomes the exit-2 assertion for `why -- CMD`; the two inline `capture` tests (src/cmd/why.rs:269 `capture_interleaves_stdout_and_stderr_and_keeps_the_exit_code`, :283 `capture_returns_once_the_child_exits_even_if_a_daemon_keeps_the_pipe_open`) leave with `capture`; tests/cli_basics.rs:218 (`run_flags_after_intent_are_flags`) becomes a `route` parse test (text after the intent is intent; `--yes` is exit 2); `data.child_exit` leaves the `why` envelope (src/cmd/why.rs:223) together with the assertions that name it; the three `--files` tests of tests/pick.rs move to the stdin form. The finish message lists them for the lead's commit body.
- src/cli.rs otherwise: `Route { intent }` replaces `Run`; `Filter` (statement; -v, -c, --strict, -0, --para, --files, --no-save); `Pick` gains -0 / --para; `Is` takes one or more statements and `--context FILE` (`Cmd::Is { condition: String }` today, src/cli.rs:110). Output verbs do not take allow_hyphen_values; text that starts with `-` goes after `--`. Two split modes together are exit 2.
- src/lib.rs: `VERBS` (:23), `command_name` (:128); `QUICK_START` (:37-51) shows `jevify route "<task>"` in place of `jevify run --dry-run`, gains the `filter` line, and its assertion in tests/cli_basics.rs (`bare_jevify_prints_the_quick_start_card_as_a_usage_error`, :116) follows; beads 2.0 and 4.0 add their line to it. The clap error path reads `args_os` and stops at `--` (:63 uses env::args()); `human` is written as bytes (:151-158).
- src/exit.rs: add the one variant `JevifyError::Kinded { kind, exit, message, hint, example }` and the kind `too_many` (exit 6) that Phase 1 needs. Bead 2.0 adds the other kinds. Rewrite the descriptions of `Exit::ALL` (:22, :29): exit 0 without "executed" (:22 says "success: yes / found / executed"); exit 7 (:29 says "`run`: the executed command failed") names only the verbs that still produce it in 0.5.0, or "reserved" when none does (check the tree after the cutover); the inline test at :131 follows. hunch-7zg.3 does not touch this file: the quota error is `JevifyError::Unavailable(message)`.
- Removed forms get one corrected line through a pre-scan: in `main_exit` (src/lib.rs:53), before `Cli::try_parse` (:59), a pre-scan of `args_os` maps a first token `run` and a `why … --` to `JevifyError::Usage` with the corrected form (`jevify route 'x'`; `CMD 2>&1 | jevify why`). The envelope `command` is `jevify` for `run` and `why` for `why`.
- The final `is` signature is installed and wired here: `cmd::is::run(ctx, statements: &[String], context: Option<&Path>)` (plus the existing band argument), and dispatch passes both. The temporary refusal of several statements lives inside src/cmd/is.rs, so hunch-7zg.6 never touches dispatch or src/lib.rs.
- Interim behaviour, all with zero requests: `pick -0` and `pick --para` return a "not implemented" input error until 1.7 (hunch-7zg.7); `why --no-save` parses and is a no-op until 1.7; `pick --files` keeps `visible()` (src/cmd/pick.rs:145) and applies it to the excerpt read: a hidden path is a candidate by name and gets no excerpt, until 1.7 replaces `visible()` with the withholding function of src/records.rs. The moved `--files` test pipes the five visible names plus `.env` (tests/pick.rs:164 holds `(".env", "TOKEN=1099")`) and asserts that no request holds `TOKEN=1099`.
- src/input.rs: `read_stdin_bytes()` with the same 64 MiB cap and terminal check as `read_stdin`; `read_stdin` (lossy, trimmed, :43-49,69) stays as it is for `why` and `is`. The terminal check (`stdin.is_terminal()`, :54) is split into a function that takes `is_terminal: bool` and returns the input error, with a unit test; both readers call it. hunch-bx6, hunch-7zg.6 and hunch-bkb rely on that unit test and write no process-level "stdin is a terminal" test.

The save directory is a pure function `save_dir(value: Option<&str>) -> Option<PathBuf>` that takes the value of JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR (:99) as a parameter and falls back to the platform cache directory, with unit tests; it does not depend on the answer cache (JEVIFY_NO_CACHE and --no-cache do not disable it). The call sites (hunch-bx6, hunch-7zg.7) read the variable and pass it.

- src/cmd/agent.rs: only the minimum that keeps the tree green and correct: the verb list of capabilities and its tests follow `VERBS`, and the `init` alias and command_not_found hook (:188-203) call `jevify route`. The full rewrite belongs to bead 1.8 (hunch-7zg.8).

Everything else is read-only. After this bead closes, the shared files are frozen for Phase 1: no other Phase 1 bead writes them, except the `pub mod args;` line in src/lib.rs (bead 1.4).

Prerequisites: hunch-ed1 (Phase 0; it writes src/config.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs and tests/agent.rs first).

- `jevify run 'x'` and `jevify why -- true` exit 2 with a one-line message that holds the corrected form; tests/cli_basics.rs asserts both, and the --json envelope of each (error.kind, exit_code 2).
- `jevify route 'task'` dispatches to src/cmd/run.rs through `run(ctx, intent, machine)`; `RunFlags` is gone; `route --yes`, `--exec`, `--dry-run`, `--no-args` are exit 2; the seven rewritten tests pass and a sentinel proves nothing runs.
- `jevify filter 'x'` parses; `filter -v 'x'` parses; `jevify is 'x' -v` is exit 2 and `--verbose` works; `jevify is 'a' 'b' --context FILE` parses; `-0 --para` together is exit 2; `why -0`, `why --para` and `why --files` are exit 2; an argument after `--` that starts with `-` is text.
- `printf 'a.txt\nb.txt\n' | jevify pick --files 'q'` reads the paths from stdin (FakeJev) and `pick --files DIR 'q'` is exit 2; `pick --index` is unchanged.
- `jevify init agents` parses and prints a block; `init zsh` and `init bash` call `jevify route`.
- Bare `jevify` prints the quick-start card with `route` and `filter` and without `run`; tests/cli_basics.rs asserts it.
- Every `Outcome { … }` in src/ sets `exec: None`; grep finds no other value.
- A clap error for an argv that holds non-UTF-8 after `--` does not panic (args_os).
- Human output is written as bytes end to end; existing verbs print what they printed before.
- `jevify is 'a' 'b'` is an input error with no request until 1.6 (a test asserts zero requests); the refusal is in src/cmd/is.rs and the dispatch already passes `&[String]` and `Option<&Path>`.
- Dispatch passes every parsed flag: a test per verb (or a code review recorded in the finish message) shows that each flag of `Filter`, `Why`, `Pick` and `Is` reaches its `run` through the signatures above; `git grep -n "cmd::\(filter\|why\|pick\|is\)::run" src/lib.rs` shows the four calls.
- Help: an anchored grep over the output of `jevify --help` and of every `jevify VERB --help` (each verb of `VERBS`) finds none of `jevify run`, `why -- `, `-- <cmd>`, `--exec`, `--no-args`, `--files DIR`, `--files <DIR>`, `child_exit`, `jevify -v`.
- `why --no-save` parses and makes the same requests as `why` (it is excluded from the zero-request assertion).
- Zero requests for each: `pick -0 'q'` and `pick --para 'q'` ("not implemented" input error); `jevify run 'x'` has envelope `command` `jevify` and `jevify why -- true` has `command` `why`, both `error.kind` usage, exit 2.
- The moved `--files` test: five visible names plus `.env` on stdin; `.env` is a candidate by name; no captured request holds `TOKEN=1099`.
- `Exit::ALL`: no description holds "executed" or "`run`"; the test at src/exit.rs:131 passes.
- Unit tests: the terminal-check function with `true` and `false`; `save_dir(Some(..))`, `save_dir(None)` and a blank value; `read_stdin_bytes` cap and empty input; `shell_quote` over bytes: empty argument, a single quote, a non-UTF-8 byte, a newline; the save directory with and without JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
