- README.md holds no reference to demo.gif (`grep -n 'demo\.gif' README.md` finds only the `ffmpeg … demo.gif` example line, if it stays); demo.gif and demo.cast are untouched.
- Every example command in the documents runs against the binary from main.
- Present tense, no meta, no retrospective language outside CHANGELOG.md; no real key path, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key`.
- The gate below passes.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
- The `ubs` gate when the changed files are only Markdown or JSON: run `ubs <changed files>`; when it reports that nothing was scanned, record "ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned" in the bead and validate every JSON file with `jq .`. That is a pass. Any file ubs does scan (Rust, shell, Python) must still exit 0.
notes: Implementation ready for lead review; not closed. All 15 allowed files changed, including configuration.md because it named the removed routing verb. capabilities matches the parser and VERBS, all entries have usage/exit/data, init agents is 20 lines, obsolete-form scans pass, README recording reference removed with recording files untouched. fmt/check/clippy/rustdoc/ubs passed; UBS exit 0, no critical findings, warning inventory reviewed as test assertions and static metadata access. Full test and lib test each reached 82 passing units then sandbox denied the non-UTF-8 fixture (Operation not permitted, os error 1); full integration suite did not run. Agent suite: 5 passed, existing redirect test could not bind mock port (PermissionDenied, Operation not permitted). Two new contract tests also pass individually. 25 shell blocks pass bash syntax and local link targets exist; 25 documented invocations accepted by current binary help parser. Live inference and external example producers not verified: outbound API unavailable in sandbox. Source verification: only add has a declined-confirmation path; sort has no prompt; multi-statement is uses data.statements. No code outside write set changed. No staging, commit, push or closure. Test-created temporary fixtures retained; no hand-written scratch files. One heredoc text write was hook-blocked for a documented eval example; skipped shell command and used patch editor. Lead must run full unsandboxed gate and live example verification before closing.
close_reason: README, guide, ROBOT_MODE, PRIVACY, CHANGELOG, AGENTS.md, help strings, capabilities and init agents for 0.5.0. The README quick-start example ran live on the keyless backend. Lead gate outside the sandbox: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full cargo test --locked (18 suites pass, 4 live tests NOT RUN); JSON files validate with jq; anchored greps find no removed or future form.

title: Release 0.5.0 (lead only): the language, filter, is
description:
Release 0.5.0, after Phase 0 and Phase 1. Epic hunch-7zg. THE LEAD DOES THIS BEAD, not a worker: a release publishes to a public repository and to crates.io. A worker that finds this bead ready reports it to the lead and takes nothing.

Outcome: version 0.5.0 (the language: grammar cutover, byte records, `filter`, `is` with statements and --context, `route` print-only, saved input) is tagged, built by cargo-dist and published.

Context: plan §3 (phase shape: "then the version bump and the release through bash scripts/release.sh"; "A release bead runs ubs on every file it changes"), project AGENTS.md "Release" and "Public repo: scan before every push". The contract beads do not bump the version; it happens here, last and alone. The absolute path in `source_repo_path` of .beads/issues.jsonl (hunch-nay) does not block this release; the owner has said so.

Files (write set): Cargo.toml (version), Cargo.lock (the jevify entry), CHANGELOG.md (the 0.5.0 heading and date). Nothing else. The lead also exports the tracker (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves, in its own commit.

Prerequisites: hunch-ed1, hunch-7zg.1, hunch-7zg.2, hunch-7zg.3, hunch-7zg.4, hunch-7zg.5, hunch-bx6, hunch-7zg.6, hunch-7zg.7, hunch-sb9, hunch-7zg.8, hunch-7zg.22. This bead blocks hunch-7zg.10 (Phase 2 skeleton, which writes Cargo.toml next). It does not wait for the epic, and the epic does not wait for anything but its children.

Procedure:
1. Check the Phase 1 acceptance of plan §3 by hand on the default backend (the seven commands under "Done when"); report what ran and what did not. Live tests without a key are NOT RUN.
2. Bump the version to 0.5.0 in Cargo.toml, refresh Cargo.lock (`cargo check`), set the CHANGELOG heading. Run the whole gate. Commit: `chore: release 0.5.0 (hunch-7zg.9)`; no Co-Authored-By, no session trailer; signed.
3. Scan: `gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v`, then read `git diff origin/main..HEAD`. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push.
4. Push main. Wait for a successful `main` CI run on that commit. Review the outgoing release diff.
5. `bash scripts/release.sh <full commit SHA>`. The script reads the committed version and pushes its signed tag; cargo-dist builds the GitHub assets and calls publish-crates.yml. Never publish the shared local working tree. Never replace an existing tag. If publishing fails, check whether the registry accepted the version before rerunning failed jobs. If only the tag push failed, inspect the retained signed tag and push that exact tag after the usual scan.

Done when: the tag v0.5.0 exists on the remote, the GitHub release has its assets, crates.io shows 0.5.0, `git status` shows main up to date with origin, and the report records the commands run.

Gate (before the release commit, sandbox disabled):
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
  ubs Cargo.toml Cargo.lock CHANGELOG.md        # every file this bead changes
Rules: main only, no branch, no worktree; never rm, git stash, git restore, git reset; stage and commit only these paths with `git commit -- <paths>`; never weaken a test to release. The `ubs` gate when the changed files are only Markdown, TOML or JSON: run `ubs <changed files>`; when it reports that nothing was scanned, record "ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned" in the bead and validate every JSON file with `jq .`. That is a pass. The binary recordings demo.gif and demo.cast belong to hunch-4ow and do not block this release.
close_reason: Released 0.5.0: acceptance commands ran by hand on the keyless backend (filter on test output, flow with head, jq in and out, --files, is --context, route, removed forms exit 2); full gate green; CI success on 0a507a6; scripts/release.sh pushed the signed tag v0.5.0; release workflow success; crates.io serves 0.5.0. 4 live tests NOT RUN (no key set).

title: fill file: a decisive names round substitutes a confidently wrong file for a content phrase; run the finals (owner picks b or c)
description:
Outcome: `fill` never substitutes a confidently wrong file for a phrase that describes a file's content; it selects the gold file or abstains.

Context (from hunch-u7s, 2026-09-22, jev-1.13.0, live; raised to a correctness blocker by review round 8, both reviewers): 'the code that splits input into records' resolves to src/input.rs at 0.51-0.70 on names alone (decisive Found, ratio guard passes vs records.rs 0.14-0.20), so the excerpt round is skipped (src/cmd/fill.rs:358-366: a decisive Found on names returns before the finals) and fill confidently runs the command on the wrong file. The 0.8.1 change (every name not ruled out reaches the finals, up to 24) only helps when the names round is undecided. Running the finals after a decisive names Found fixes this case (records.rs 0.96) but costs one extra request per file fill and flipped 'the workflow that publishes to crates.io' to scripts/release.sh 0.77, because .github/ excerpts are withheld (hidden component) and the withheld finalist competes on its name alone. Held-out figures (hunch-lpp at 0.8.0): name phrases 7/7, content phrases 0/4 with two confident wrong picks. The user documents do not state the risk; the only mention is the 0.7.0 known-limits entry of CHANGELOG.md, and its wording is stale (hunch-dlh/N1 corrects that entry).

Options, the owner picks; no threshold or ratio change in any of them:
(a) keep as is and document (both reviewers reject this);
(b) always run the finals for `file`, with a testable rule for a finalist whose evidence is withheld (astra's preference; "neutral treatment" needs a definition a test can check, for example: a withheld finalist cannot beat a finalist with evidence unless its name already decided);
(c) run the finals after a Found only when the runner-up name also matches (opus-5-5's preference: no extra request in the common case, and a withheld `.github/` finalist never enters).

Interim, before the owner answers (a worker, one sentence each): docs/guide/kinds.md:29 (the `file`/`dir` row) and the README passage that describes the `file` kind state that a phrase describing only a file's content can be answered confidently and wrongly, and that `--dry-run` shows the file before anything runs. Present tense, no meta language (AGENTS.md).

Files (write set): src/cmd/fill.rs (the decision after the names round), src/tournament.rs if the rule lives there, tests/fill.rs (FakeJev contract: a withheld finalist cannot win on its name; the two-round contract), evals/fill/file.jsonl (unchanged gold, re-run), docs/guide/kinds.md, README.md (one sentence), CHANGELOG.md Unreleased. Evidence and request bodies: session scratchpad u7s/ (local only, never in the repository).

Done when, whichever option:
- The four content phrases of evals/fill/file.jsonl select the gold file or abstain (live, jev-1.13.0 or the current default, TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key; NOT RUN if no key), and the name phrases stay 5/5.
- A withheld `.github/` finalist cannot win on its name alone: a FakeJev contract test proves it.
- The request-count change per `fill` is measured and reported in the notes against the keyless quota figures of README (20,000 classifications a day per IP; `fill` 3,267 candidates per marker without a key).
- The interim sentences are in kinds.md and README, or removed when the fix makes them false.
- The AGENTS.md gate passes; workers never run git add, git commit, git push or br close.
notes:
Lead decision N3 (review round 8, 2026-09-22): P3 owner decision -> P1 bug, correctness blocker; both reviewers reject option (a). astra prefers (b), opus-5-5 prefers (c). Interim doc sentence in kinds.md and README assigned to a worker now. Earlier description kept inside the Context paragraph.
OWNER DECISION 2026-09-22: option (c). Run the finals after a decisive names Found only when the runner-up name also matches the phrase; no extra request when the runner-up does not match. The rule is a heuristic: define it explicitly, test both branches, and report the measured request-count change and the name-phrase results (must stay 5/5).
IMPLEMENTED (c) 2026-09-22, src/cmd/fill.rs runner_up_matches: after a decisive names Found on a tier-two kind, the finals run only when the runner-up is in play, defined as RIVAL_RATIO * (none + sum of every name but the winner) > best.p (the winner does not beat the field it leads by the winner ratio; equivalently the winner holds under two thirds). Read from round one only: no request, no threshold change, no new ratio. Why not runner-up vs NONE: the backend reports two decimals; measured live, 'the workflow that publishes to crates.io' gave release.sh 0.01 against NONE 0.01, a ratio rule sent the withheld .github/ finalist into a finals and flipped it to scripts/release.sh 0.77, while 'the code that splits input into records' gave records.rs 0.14 against NONE 0.15 and a beats-NONE rule kept src/input.rs. The field rule separates every measured run: content winners 0.51-0.59 vs field 0.41-0.49; name winners 0.91-1.00 vs field 0.00-0.09.
LIVE 2026-09-22 jev-1.13.0, 197 candidates, JEVIFY_NO_CACHE=1: content 4/4 (stages hunks gold 0.85; splits input into records gold 0.98, names input.rs 0.58/records.rs 0.17/NONE 0.15 -> finals; recipe engine abstain none 0.34; retry/backoff abstain none 0.65). Names 5/5 (marker 0.96, release 0.92, privacy 1.00, manpage 0.93, publish-crates 0.98 on names alone; helm chart abstain none 1.00). Request count per fill, measured through the logging proxy: name phrases 1 request (unchanged); 'splits input into records' 2 (was 1); the other content phrases 2 (unchanged). Against README (20,000 classifications a day per IP; fill 3,267 candidates per marker without a key): the extra request costs one more classification per marker only when a decisive names winner holds under two thirds; a names-only marker stays at one. Contract test tests/fill.rs decisive_names_reach_the_finals_only_when_the_runner_up_is_in_play covers both branches and shows the .github/ winner never enters a finals; unit test in fill.rs covers the boundary. Interim sentence in docs/guide/kinds.md; README sentence and CHANGELOG line reported to the lead (files owned by hunch-hd8).
close_reason: Owner option (c): after a decisive names Found on a tier-two kind, the finals run only when the winner does not beat the rest of the field (other names plus NONE) by the winner ratio. Live: content phrases 4/4 gold or abstain, name phrases 5/5, one extra request only for the affected case; gate green

title: Enforce Jev protocol, request and cache boundaries
description: Reconciled review: validate all decision-bearing API fields; prevent malformed labels and missing dimensions; enforce classifier field and option limits without silently dropping candidates; isolate endpoint cache entries; redact outbound semantic fields consistently while preserving opaque IDs and non-secret identifiers. Add deterministic regressions. Lead coordinates documentation and publication.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic repairs and regressions for v0.3.3. Combined gate: 124 tests passed, 4 live tests not run; fmt/check/clippy/docs pass. Remaining semantic and filesystem guarantees tracked separately.

title: No hook exposes round-one ranks or the finalist set
description:
Found by the hunch-evl paired pilot (jevify 0.8.3, 2026-09-22).

Nothing exposes round one. `tournament::shortlist` returns the per-window rankings and the finalist
set, and both stay inside the process: the JSON envelope prints only candidates that beat NONE in
the deciding round, --verbose adds no round-one field, and there is no environment variable that
prints or dumps them. `why` and `pick` print "finalists per window: N" on stderr when N is not 3,
which is the count, never the members.

Consequence for measurement: the finalist-miss rate (how often the right candidate misses its
window's finalists at n = 3, 2, 1) can only be reconstructed, by cutting the input into the same
W=200 windows the code uses and re-ranking the window that holds the gold on its own. That doubles
the requests, only sees candidates above NONE, and repeats work the real run already did. The
hunch-lpp and hunch-evl reports both carry the reconstruction, and both had to say so.

Expected: a way to read round one from a real run without a second run: for example the JSON
envelope carrying a round_one field with the per-window ranks and the finalist indices behind an
existing flag, or a trace file that records both rounds. The contract already reports the window
count and the finalists-per-window count; this adds the members.

Suggested write set: src/tournament.rs (expose what shortlist already computes), the verbs that
call it, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md and the envelope tests if a field is added.
close_reason: meta.decision.round_one exposes what Shortlist already computed, with no extra request: each window's full ranking with P(NONE) and Noul, the finalist indices and n, for why, pick (stdin, --files, --from) and fill; capabilities, ROBOT_MODE and the decision tests guard it. Verified no regression on the validation pick/why cases and the why corpus; route hook left to a follow-up

title: pick over a plain listing prefers a docs page to the source file a description names
description:
Found by the hunch-evl paired pilot (jevify 0.8.3, jev-1.13.0, TypeSafe, 2026-09-22).

`pick` over a plain listing of paths answers with a documentation page whose name matches the
description instead of the source file the description names. Round one is not at fault: in each
case the gold ranked first in its own W=200 window. The answer is lost in the finals.

36 descriptions over three lists above one window (pydantic-ai path listing 2,834 paths / 15
windows; testify commits 409 / 3; jevify test names 209 / 2). Gold ranked 1st in its window in
36/36, so the finalist miss rate is 0/36 at n = 3, 2 and 1. End to end 30/36. All six losses are
a sibling chosen in round two:

    'the weather example agent'
        gold examples/pydantic_ai_examples/weather_agent.py
        picked docs/examples/weather-agent.md
    'the retrieval augmented generation example'
        gold examples/pydantic_ai_examples/rag.py
        picked docs/examples/rag.md
    'fetching a web page as an agent capability'
        gold pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/capabilities/web_fetch.py
        picked docs/capabilities/web-fetch.md
    'search the available tools lazily instead of listing all of them'
        gold pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/capabilities/_tool_search.py
        picked pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/_tool_search.py
    'events streamed out of a Temporal workflow'
        gold pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/durable_exec/temporal/_event_stream.py
        picked tests/durable_exec/temporal/cassettes/test_agent/...
    'resetting the app now wipes every stored model'
        gold d3d5264, picked 6bf878f

Four of the six prefer a documentation page to the implementation. The description asks for the
thing that does the work, not the page about it; on a plain stdin listing the finals see only the
paths, so a name that reads like the description wins. Related but distinct from hunch-u7s and
hunch-8ar, which are about the --files path and the file kind: here there is no excerpt stage at
all.

Expected: a description of behaviour resolves to the file that implements it, or the verb reports
ambiguity between the implementation and its documentation page rather than answering the page with
0.9 confidence. Re-measure with the 36-case set in the hunch-evl report.

Suggested write set: src/cmd/pick.rs (the finals for the stdin path, prompts), src/tournament.rs
only if the rule changes, tests/pick.rs.
close_reason: The finals of stdin pick rank the entry that is or does the described thing above a page that documents it, a test or a recording, unless the request asks for one; round one, one-window lists, --files and --from unchanged. Pilot set 30/36 -> 34/36 with all four docs-page losses fixed; adjudicated pick cases decide identically. Remaining losses are sibling implementations, which belong to the evidence beads

title: README revamp in the owner's voice: digital-double, unslop, de-slopify, readme-reviser
description:
Outcome: a README the owner recognises as his own writing, and that a stranger understands in thirty seconds. The owner read the hunch-dlh version and said: "No, revamp the readme using my double and unslop skill. The current one is too bad."

What is wrong with the current README (read it first, it is 274 lines):
- It reads like documentation written by a machine: five sections of the same shape (title, one paragraph, an SVG, a console block, a closing sentence), every paragraph the same length, every sentence the same rhythm.
- The opening sentence is a list of four things in apposition, then a second sentence about the model. A reader learns what the tool touches before learning why they would want it.
- The console blocks are long and unpruned: they show status lines, cache paths and file lists that carry no meaning for a first reader.
- Nothing in it sounds like a person: no opinion, no restraint, no aside, nothing that says why this exists or where it does not help.

The writing process is the work. Follow it in order and say in the report what each step changed:
1. Voice. Invoke the Skill tool with skill "digital-double". Read its references/voice.md and the technical-English section of references/voice-examples.md. The owner is a French engineer writing technical English: short sentences, concrete nouns, dry humour, no salesmanship, an honest limit stated plainly.
2. Draft. Rewrite the README from the substance, not by editing sentences of the old one. Keep every fact and every command correct.
3. Invoke the Skill tool with skill "unslop" and run its two-pass flow (diagnosis, then reconstruction) over the whole draft.
4. Invoke the Skill tool with skill "jfp:de-slopify" over the result.
5. Invoke the Skill tool with skill "jfp:readme-reviser": present tense, as if it was always so.
6. Read the result aloud in your head. Cut every sentence that adds nothing. The README is allowed to be shorter than it is now.

Rules for the content:
- Lead with the problem a reader has, in their words, before any command.
- Keep the four animations (docs/img/why.svg, fill.svg, label.svg, nothing-fits.svg). They are good; the owner asked for them.
- Prune every console block to the lines that carry the point. Never invent output: cut, do not edit. Every example stays reproducible by docs/demo/examples.sh.
- Say plainly where jevify does not help. The honest "nothing fits" is a feature; the `file` content-phrase limit is a real one.
- No meta language ("this guide", "captured on"), no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). Dates only next to a measurement. History belongs in CHANGELOG.md.
- Facts must match the installed release: verify each command against `jevify --help`, `jevify capabilities --json` and a live run before it goes in.

Files (write set): README.md, and docs/guide/getting-started.md only if the README's opening moves material there. docs/demo/examples.sh may gain or lose an example if the README's examples change. Everything else is read-only; CHANGELOG.md is the lead's.

Done when:
- The process above ran, step by step, with each skill invoked through the Skill tool.
- Every command and every line of output is verified against the installed release.
- The unslop audit reports no AI patterns on README.md.
- The owner reads it and says it is clear. The lead asks; until then this bead stays open.
notes: Lead: when the owner's review comes, add one honest sentence to the README file-kind passage, in the README's own voice: a phrase describing a file's content and not its name is decided by the excerpts unless the names round is one-sided, where fill can still answer confidently and wrongly; --dry-run shows the file before anything runs. docs/guide/kinds.md already states it (hunch-8ar).

title: An operator can turn off input saving from the environment, and the store prunes
description:
A harness trial on 2026-09-23 found that `why` and `filter` write raw stdin to
$JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR/outputs/<blake3>.log, mode 0600, never pruned. The reviewer confirmed a
synthetic AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY written verbatim, and confirmed that JEVIFY_NO_CACHE=1 does not
suppress it. `--no-save` suppresses it, but it is a per-call flag with no environment variable,
so a CI fleet cannot turn it off centrally: every call site must remember it.

This is the feature working as designed (saved inputs are what make `--full` and the status line
useful), and it is also the kind of default that ends a product's credibility the first time
someone finds a key in a cache directory.

Do three things:
1. Add an environment variable that disables saving fleet-wide, and make it obvious in
   capabilities, the configuration guide, ROBOT_MODE and PRIVACY.md. Follow the naming of the
   existing variables.
2. Give the store a bound. It is never pruned today. Decide a default retention consistent with
   the seven-day answer cache, prune on write, and say so in PRIVACY.md. Do not delete anything
   outside the store, and do not prune on read.

Also in the same area, from the same trial: `data.complete` on filter and why reports whether the

CHANGELOG must say so) or document it where it appears. State which you chose and why.

PRIVACY.md, docs/guide/configuration.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, CHANGELOG.md, tests/**.

title: The commit kind stops giving confident wrong answers when subjects lie
description:
A hostile live trial on 2026-09-23 (scratchpad/trial-hostile.md) found the product's worst
failure shape. The `commit` kind never reads a diff. A commit candidate carries its subject line
and its changed paths, nothing else. So a commit whose subject overpromises beats the commit that
holds the change.

Reproduction, in a scratch repository of ten commits paired as a docs-only commit with a truthful
sounding subject and a code commit with a dull subject that holds the real change:

    jevify fill --dry-run -- git show --stat '@{commit:the commit that changed the gateway timeout value in the code}'
    -> 1b92db5 0.98 (next 0.00, none 0.02) fix: payment gateway timeout

The change is in 4711c5a "chore: tidy imports in payments". Five descriptions, three runs each:
15 of 15 wrong, p 0.93 to 0.99, runner-up 0.00 every time. It recovers only when the description
already names the answer ("the commit whose diff edits src/payments.rs").

The control is why this matters: on this repository's own history, where subjects are honest, the
same class of query is right. The tool demonstrates well on the author's repository and fails on
the reader's. Our own measurement agrees: evals/commit-attractor scored 11 of 27 keyless with
descriptions written from diffs, which is exactly this blind spot, and we read it as weakness in
the kind rather than as a missing evidence source.

Decide between these with measurement, not taste. Both are legitimate; say which the numbers
support and why.
(a) Give the finals round the diff. `fill` already runs a tier-two finals round for `commit`; the
    finalist's evidence could include a bounded diffstat or a clipped patch. Measure the cost:
    requests, wall time, and how many finalists still fit the keyless window at 99. Measure the
    gain on evals/commit-attractor and on a new adversarial set built like the one above, where
    the subject lies. If the window cannot hold the diff for 24 finalists, say what it can hold.
(b) If the evidence says (a) costs more than it returns, then the kind must stop implying it
    knows what a commit did. Say in README, the kinds guide and the capability note that a commit
    is matched on its subject and its changed paths, and that a repository whose subjects
    overpromise will get a confident wrong answer. Demote the commit demo out of the README's
    first screen.

Either way, add the adversarial lying-subject set to evals/ so the failure cannot return
unnoticed, and record the result in benchmarks/results.md.

Write set: src/cmd/fill.rs and src/source.rs only if (a) wins, evals/commit-subjects/**,
benchmarks/results.md, README.md, docs/guide/kinds.md, src/cmd/agent.rs (capability strings).
Done when: the choice is made on measured evidence and recorded; the adversarial set exists and
is scored on both backends; no document implies the commit kind reads a diff unless it does; the
gate passes. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
close_reason: Option (a) chosen on measurement and implemented. The adversarial set (evals/commit-subjects/, 20 cases over a scratch repo and ripgrep at a pinned sha) went 0/20 to 20/20 on both backends. commit-attractor rerun like-for-like moved 9 to 12 of 27 keyless and 14 to 22 of 27 TypeSafe, one fewer wrong answer on each. The real finding: on a single-window repository the commit finals never ran, so diff evidence alone would have changed nothing; the kind also had to lose the names shortcut and keep the candidates the subjects scored 0.00. All 24 finalists still fit the keyless budget.

title: fill status line: ambiguous names the wrong rival when NONE decided, and no_match prints an empty field
description:
Found by the hunch-lpp evaluation (jevify 0.7.0, jev-1.13.0, 2026-09-22).

Evidence: when NONE is the close rival, fill reports `ambiguous` and names the second candidate as the rival. It leaves out the NONE probability, which was the actual reason.

    (testify repo) jevify fill --dry-run --verbose -- ls '@{dir:the app services}'
    jevify fill: not run: arg 2 dir: ambiguous; closest: testify-app/Testify/Services (0.42), testify-app (0.08); candidates 86 of 86, omitted 0; model jev-1.13.0

decide() in src/tournament.rs returns Ambiguous when best < 2 * max(second, none). Here best is 0.42 and second 0.08, so NONE must lie between 0.21 and 0.42. A caller who reads the line sees a 5x lead and cannot tell why nothing ran. --verbose adds nothing.

Related, same status line: a no_match prints an empty field, "no_match; ; candidates 181 of 181". Seen on every no_match of the held-out run (file, dir, tool, branch).

Expected: an abstention names the rival that decided it, NONE included, with its probability (for example "ambiguous; closest: X (0.42), none (0.30)", or report it as insufficient_evidence). no_match leaves out the empty closest field or fills it with the top candidates.

Suggested write set: src/cmd/fill.rs (status formatting near the Decision::Ambiguous arm), tests/fill.rs (status line assertions with a NONE rival and with no_match).
notes: Lead: also take item (2) of hunch-cpo: with 0 candidates, fill says plainly that there is nothing to choose from (for example 'no branch to choose from') instead of no_match with an empty closest field; keep exit 3 unless the plan or VISION says otherwise, and add the reason to the capabilities abstention reasons if a new reason string is introduced (src/cmd/agent.rs joins the write set for that line only).
close_reason: Ambiguous names blocking rivals incl. NONE, no_match names top candidates, empty listing says 'no KIND to choose from' (exit 3, no_match), no empty segment; tests/fill.rs 35/35; ubs 0; other failures were in hunch-0it's in-progress files

title: Bound retries and subprocess work with explicit deadlines
description:
Outcome: a verb has one overall deadline with cancellation; retries wait exactly what `Retry-After` says without extra premature requests; usage in `meta` distinguishes attempts, successes, waits, cache hits and unknown usage; local `man` and `pdftotext` child processes have a timeout and bounded input.

Context: the epic hunch-7zg delivers part of the earlier scope, and this bead keeps it unchanged: hunch-7zg.3 sends classifier chunks in parallel and sets the final 429 policy (`rate_limit_day` is never retried, exit 4; other 429s are retried after `Retry-After`; one wait of `ask_each` is capped at 60 s, and a longer `Retry-After` is not retried and names the limit); hunch-q8p delivers the lister runner with its deadline (`try_wait` poll, `kill`, 200 ms for the readers, a listing valid only after exit 0 and EOF on both streams). Reuse the quota measurement of hunch-glz (benchmarks/results.md) and the telemetry evidence of hunch-hjp. Remaining scope, final:
- An overall deadline per verb, with cancellation of queued requests when it passes (exit 4 `unavailable`, the message names the deadline); the sum of retry waits never exceeds it.
- `Retry-After` behaviour: no request is sent before the named wait ends; a test proves the gap.
- Usage accounting in `meta`: attempted, succeeded, waited (count and total ms), cache hits, and unknown usage kept apart from a measured zero (`Telemetry`, src/output.rs:46; src/config.rs:190-198).
- Local child processes: `man` (src/manpage.rs, src/inventory.rs) and `pdftotext` (src/cmd/sort.rs) run with a timeout through the same poll-and-kill pattern as the lister runner (reuse it from src/source.rs if its signature allows; do not write a third one), with stdin at /dev/null and bounded output.

Files (write set): src/jev/client.rs, tests/client.rs, src/output.rs, src/config.rs (the `meta` function only; `Config` gains no field for the epic's directories, and a deadline setting, if any, is a parsed variable like the existing ones), src/manpage.rs, src/inventory.rs, src/cmd/sort.rs, tests/sort.rs, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md (the `meta` fields), docs/guide/configuration.md (the deadline variable, if one is added), CHANGELOG.md. Everything else is read-only; README.md is not in this bead.

Prerequisites: hunch-8ay (closed), hunch-7zg.3, hunch-7zg.18 (the epic's writers of these files are closed by then), hunch-glz (its measurement is reused, and it writes docs/guide/configuration.md and CHANGELOG.md first).

Done when:
- tests/client.rs: a mock that answers 429 with `Retry-After: 1` twice receives its third request no earlier than 2 s after the first; an overall deadline shorter than the waits ends with exit 4 and no further request; `rate_limit_day` behaviour is unchanged (one request, exit 4).
- `meta` under --json carries the five usage fields; a cache hit counts as a cache hit and not as a request; missing usage is null, not zero (tests/cli_basics.rs already asserts the null form and stays green).
- A fake `man` and a fake `pdftotext` that sleep are killed at the timeout and the verb continues without their text (unit tests with an injected deadline and an injected PATH through `Command::env`; no `set_var` in src/).
- docs/ROBOT_MODE.md names the `meta` fields in the present tense; CHANGELOG.md has the entry.
- The full gate passes (cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs on the changed files).
- Division of the gate: the worker runs fmt, check, clippy, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps` and ubs, and tries the tests; when its sandbox blocks them (it cannot bind 127.0.0.1) it reports them as NOT RUN with the error. The lead runs the full test gate, and only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead. Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains); CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0, and a red CI on this work is the worker's to fix forward. Commit subject, for the lead: "fix: <summary> (hunch-bec)", under 72 characters, no Co-Authored-By.

The lister runner with its deadline is hunch-q8p. The remaining scope of this bead stays here: an overall deadline and cancellation for a verb, the usage accounting, the timeout of local man/pdf child processes. title: 2.4 fill core: resolve markers and become the command
description:
Plan bead: 2.4 — fill core. Epic hunch-7zg. This bead replaces the earlier "resolving wrapper, proposal only" design: fill runs the command it resolved.

Outcome: `jevify fill -- CMD ARGS…` resolves every '@{kind:description}' marker to a real handle and becomes the command; one call replaces list, read, choose, act. Any doubt means nothing runs.

Context: plan §2.1 (all nine steps, the pool-rule table, the status lines, the error kinds), §1, §2.3 "The model", §3 Phase 2 "Done when", §5 `tests/fill.rs`, §7, §8.1–8.4, §9.2–9.5, §9.15–9.16; vision "The input side". Built on src/marker.rs (hunch-7zg.11), src/source.rs (hunch-q8p), src/tournament.rs (hunch-zxz), src/records.rs, `ask`/`ask_each` and the exec path of `run_cli` (hunch-7zg.10): all read-only here. Flow: lex -> read inputs -> enumerate -> resolve -> substitute -> print or exec. Decisions, final (owner, plan §9):
- fill becomes the command through exec: it returns `Outcome.exec = Some(Exec { argv, stdin_null })` (the field exists since bead 1.0; this bead adds nothing to `Outcome`) and `run_cli` calls `CommandExt::exec` as its last act. No child, no signal code. The command's exit code comes through; exit 7 leaves fill. `stdin_null` is true when step 2 consumed stdin, false otherwise. Everything that must reach the disk is written before exec (cache entries go through a rename; stderr is unbuffered). A literal argv[0] that is not on the PATH is exit 6 `cannot_run` before any request.
- A handle is an `OsString` (`Record.handle`) and is substituted as bytes: a handle or a path that is not UTF-8 reaches the command unchanged.
- An unsure `flag` abstains: `is::band_verdict(p, threshold, band)` (src/cmd/is.rs:121; it is `pub` and returns `(Exit, &'static str)`), called with `ctx.threshold` and the band 0.15, a constant in src/cmd/fill.rs (the default of `is --band`; `fill` has no option for it): `not run: arg 5 flag --draft: unsure 0.48; write --draft or drop the marker`. Yes keeps the argument, no removes the whole argv element.
- Windows up to F = W x (W / 3) (13,200 on TypeSafe, 3,267 on classifier.dev); fill uses three finalists per window ONLY (`Finalists::ThreeOnly` of hunch-zxz; it never goes to two or one, because a wrong act costs more than no act); the pool is never cut; at most two rounds; every request of a round is in flight at the same time. Round 1: one window per W candidates per listing marker, plus all `one` and `flag` markers over the context: one Choice per `one`, one Noul per `flag`, 20 questions per request. Round 2: one request per listing marker (finals, or the tier-two retry with one window). The `limit` fill passes to `source::enumerate` is F.
- Kind names are validated HERE, before any other I/O (no stdin read, no lister, no request): the lexer (hunch-7zg.11) keeps no registry and returns every syntactically valid kind other than `-`, `one` and `flag` as a named kind with its span. `fill` checks each name against the coded kinds and the shipped recipes of the registry in src/source.rs (from Phase 3, hunch-7zg.17 extends the same check to the user's kinds.jsonl, read only when a name is in neither, with no change to src/marker.rs). An unknown name is exit 2, nothing runs: the message names the nearest kind, lists the kinds, and shows the `@@{` spelling for a literal, built from the span: for `{user}@{host:>8}` it shows `'{user}@@{host:>8}'`.
- Rounds through the two calls of src/tournament.rs, no callback: `shortlist` (round 1; it returns the full `Ranking` of each window), then `source::enrich(kind, handles)` for the tier-two evidence of the finalists only (enumeration is tier one only; `enrich` is async, reads on the blocking pool, and runs the withholding function first for path kinds), then `window` for the finals. The finalists come from `shortlist` in the finalist order that hunch-zxz defines (by rank, then window index: rank 1 of every window, then rank 2, then rank 3); `fill` does not reorder them, and "tier-two evidence for the first 24" means the first 24 of that order. With one window, `fill` decides from the `Ranking` of `shortlist` with no second request; round 2 runs only when the ratio failed and the kind has tier-two evidence.
- `--dry-run` prints one command: one physical line unless an argument holds a newline, which stays inside its single quotes (`output::shell_quote`). Status lines on stderr escape a newline in a handle or an argument as `\n` (the helper of src/output.rs), so each status line stays one line with its prefix. Every error of `fill` is rendered by `run_cli` as `jevify fill: not run: <kind>: <message>` (hunch-7zg.10 owns that rendering).
- The leading-`-` rule lives here, per marker, because it depends on the marker's position and a listing is shared between markers (`source::enumerate` does only the unconditional hygiene: newline, carriage return, NUL): a handle that starts with `-` is dropped for a marker that opens its argument when the kind is not a path, and kept for an embedded marker. Each marker has its own omitted count in its status line and in `data.markers[]`.
- More than F candidates: an ordered kind keeps the newest F and says so; any other kind is exit 6 `too_many` with the count and the two ways to narrow (a literal path prefix, or a narrower list piped into '@{-:…}'). Zero candidates is exit 3 `no_match` with no request.
- A `one` marker holds at most W options (`Backend::window()`: 99 on classifier.dev, 200 on TypeSafe), because NONE takes one slot of the Choice; more is exit 2 with the count, before any request. The lexer has no backend, so the check lives here.
- Decision per listing marker: `tournament::decide(&Ranking, ctx.threshold)` (found when `any >= threshold` and `p(best) >= 2 x max(p(second), p(NONE))`; equal scores abstain). `one`: the same ratio over the options and NONE. Same evidence with different handles ends as `ambiguous`, and the status line says `N candidates share the same evidence`.
- The model guard: `meta.model` is a string in which distinct contributing models are joined with ", " (hunch-7zg.3). fill runs a command only when EVERY part starts with `jev`: the helper is `jev::all_jev` over `ctx.meta().model` (`pub fn all_jev(model: &str)`, src/jev/mod.rs:160 before hunch-7zg.23, which edits that file: find it by name; `Meta.model` is an `Option<String>`, src/output.rs:95, and `None` after a request was answered refuses like the empty string); do not split the string here. Otherwise the error is `JevifyError::Unavailable(format!("answered by {model}, not Jev"))`: exit 4, kind `api_unavailable` (src/exit.rs:88; no new kind), and the line names the model that is not Jev. A non-Jev dimension followed by a Jev dimension refuses. Since hunch-7zg.23 a missing or empty model name is the part `unknown`, which does not start with `jev`: a mixed unknown/Jev answer refuses too, and so does an answer with no model name at all.
- All or nothing: any abstention means nothing runs: exit 3, empty stdout, one line per failed marker: `jevify fill: not run: arg 3 branch: ambiguous; closest: tp/auth (0.41), tp/auth-v2 (0.38)`. Reasons: `no_match`, `ambiguous`, `unsure_flag`, `insufficient_evidence` (a context above the evidence budget, no request). A fill abstention is an `Outcome` (not a `JevifyError`) with exit 3 and `error: null`: `data.reason` is the reason of the FIRST failed marker in argv order, and `data.markers[]` lists every marker with its own reason (and the resolved ones with their handle). There is NO `error.kind` for an abstention: `run_cli` renders outcomes with `data` and `error: None` (src/lib.rs:221-229) and `report_error` renders errors with `error` and `data: null` (:255-268), and that code does not change. The reason strings are the constants that hunch-7zg.10 put in src/exit.rs. Errors proper (exit 2, 4, 6: usage, the model guard, `lister_failed`, `too_many`, `cannot_run`, `stdin_is_tty`) stay `JevifyError`s with `error.kind`; when a marker fails with such an error, the first one in argv order is returned.
- Enumerate each distinct (kind, prefix) once, in parallel. stdin is read once, on the blocking pool, up to 64 MiB, by `fill` itself (`source::enumerate` never reads stdin: `fill` passes the bytes in `Scope::Input { bytes, split, field, key }`); a required stdin that is a terminal is exit 6 `stdin_is_tty`. `fill` tests `std::io::stdin().is_terminal()` itself, before the read, through a pure `fn(bool) -> Result<(), JevifyError>` in src/cmd/fill.rs that returns the kind `stdin_is_tty`: `check_terminal` (src/input.rs:61) is private and returns `EmptyInput`, and src/input.rs is in no Phase 2 write set. An `EmptyInput` from the read (stdin was empty, src/input.rs:56 and :87) is not an error for `fill`: it maps to an empty listing, which becomes exit 3 `no_match` with no request. The entry point has the signature that hunch-7zg.10 fixed: `run(ctx, flags: FillFlags { dry_run, quiet, candidates, context, field, key, split }, cmd: &[OsString], machine: bool)`.
- --dry-run: the quoted command on stdout, one line, through `output::shell_quote`; exit 0. With a machine format the envelope carries data.argv; an argv that is not UTF-8 is exit 6 `cannot_run` there. A machine format without --dry-run is exit 2 (CLI, bead 2.0).
- Status lines on stderr, all prefixed `jevify fill:`, in the forms of plan §2.1; the last is `exec <quoted command>` or `not run: <reason>`. `-q` prints only `not run:` lines. jevify sets no variable for the command; environment and working directory pass through.
- Kinds at this bead: `-`, `branch`, `one`, `flag`. Phase 3 adds kinds through the registry.
- Live tests (#[ignore]) for one `branch` and one `one` per backend go into tests/live.rs (hunch-7zg.5 and hunch-bx6 wrote that file in Phase 1).

Files (write set): src/cmd/fill.rs, tests/fill.rs (new), tests/live.rs (added tests). tests/bin/argv.sh is read-only (hunch-7zg.10 owns it). Everything else is read-only.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.11, hunch-q8p, hunch-zxz (and hunch-7zg.10 through them), hunch-7zg.23 (model provenance keeps `unknown`; the model guard relies on it).

Done when, as contract tests in tests/fill.rs (FakeJev; the helper `sh tests/bin/argv.sh <exit-code> args…` prints its arguments NUL-separated, prints `stdin:eof` or `stdin:data`, exits with the code; PATH-dependent cases put fake `git` first on the PATH through assert_cmd's `.env`):
- The dry-run output equals the argv a run receives, a non-UTF-8 literal argument and a non-UTF-8 handle (from '@{-:…}' over -0 input) included.
- The `gh issue create` example of the vision (two `one`, one `flag`, context on stdin) sends one POST for its three markers.
- Abstain prints nothing on stdout and runs nothing; an unsure `flag` runs nothing (exit 3); an answer from another model runs nothing (exit 4), and so does a response whose first dimension is answered by another model and whose second by Jev; a sentinel file proves each. The refusal is exit 4 with `error.kind` `api_unavailable` and the message `answered by <model>, not Jev`.
- Mixed unknown and Jev provenance runs nothing: a response in which one dimension names no model and another names Jev (`meta.model` holds `unknown`) is exit 4, and the sentinel file is absent; a response with no model name at all runs nothing either.
- An unsure `flag` is decided with the band 0.15 around the threshold: with threshold 0.5, p = 0.60 and p = 0.40 abstain (`unsure_flag`), p = 0.70 keeps the argument, p = 0.30 removes the element.
- Several failed markers: a `no_match` at arg 2 and an `unsure_flag` at arg 4 give exit 3, `error` null, `data.reason` `no_match`, two `not run:` lines, and both in `data.markers[]` (under --json with --dry-run).
- Unknown kinds: `'@{widget:x}'` and `'{user}@{host:>8}'` are exit 2 before any other I/O (piped stdin is not consumed, the fake `git` records no invocation, the mock receives no request); the message names the nearest kind and holds `'{user}@@{host:>8}'`; `'{user}@@{host:>8}'` next to a real marker passes through as the literal `{user}@{host:>8}`.
- Tier two for finalists only: with several windows of branches, the fake `git` (it records its invocations) ran tier-two commands for the finalists and for no other branch; with one decisive window it ran none and the mock received one request.
- A handle that holds a newline cannot occur (enumeration drops it); a literal argument with a newline prints under --dry-run inside single quotes and reads back exactly through `sh -c`; the `exec` status line holds `\n` and stays one line.
- One listing, two markers: over the same stdin list, `'@{-:x}'` (standalone) drops a handle that starts with `-` and counts it, while `'--value=@{-:x}'` (embedded) keeps it and can resolve to it.
- A lister whose child keeps the pipe open gives exit 6 `lister_failed` and sends no request (a fake `git` first on the PATH).
- A `one` with W options resolves and with W + 1 is exit 2 with the count and no request, on each backend.
- 0, 1 and 2 candidates; a tie; NONE close to the best; same evidence with different handles; a handle with a newline or a leading `-`.
- W, W + 1, F, F + 1 candidates on each backend; `F + 1` lines are `too_many` with no request; 250 lines resolve in two rounds and the finals hold three finalists of every window; fill never prints `finalists per window`; two close rivals in one window both reach the finals and end as `ambiguous`; the right candidate in the last window wins.
- A branch with a remote twin resolves.
- stdin ownership: the command prints `stdin:eof` with '@{-:…}', `stdin:data` otherwise; --candidates FILE and --context FILE leave stdin to the command; stdin with two roles is exit 2.
- The command's exit code comes through (`fill -q -- sh tests/bin/argv.sh 1 '@{-:x}' <<< x` is 1); `-q`; a machine format without --dry-run is exit 2; `one` + `flag` in one request; a `flag` no removes the element; a missing program is exit 6 `cannot_run`. "stdin is a terminal": an inline unit test of the pure function of src/cmd/fill.rs (`true` gives exit 6 with the kind `stdin_is_tty`, `false` gives `Ok`), with no process-level terminal test. An empty stdin for '@{-:…}' is exit 3 `no_match` with no request, not an input error.
- By hand on the default backend when the network allows (NOT RUN otherwise): the seven commands of plan §3 Phase 2 "Done when".
- The gate below passes.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
notes:
Notes written before the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md are superseded by the description, which transcribes that plan (epic hunch-7zg). Where an older note and the description disagree, the description holds. In particular: there is no --run flag (fill runs by default and --dry-run prints), no --evidence, and a marker stands anywhere inside one argument.
Lead decisions 2026-09-21: (1) the model guard applies under --dry-run too: an answer that is not from Jev is exit 4 and no command is printed. (2) Meta.model is Option<String>; None after an answered request is a refusal, as the description says.
Worker implementation is in src/cmd/fill.rs, tests/fill.rs and tests/live.rs. Fill resolves registry and context markers in two rounds, preserves raw argv, guards every contributing model and returns Exec only after all markers resolve. Added 22 contract tests, four passing inline unit tests and ignored live branch/one coverage. Final fmt, all-target check, all-target clippy and rustdoc with warnings denied passed. Full tests are blocked in the worker sandbox: wiremock cannot bind localhost, and the existing records non-UTF-8 fixture cannot be created; final lib run passed 111 tests with that one sandbox denial. close_reason: fill core. Lead gate outside the sandbox: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full cargo test --locked (19 suites pass, 4 live tests NOT RUN), ubs exit 0. title: The pick demo does not hang on a 0.04 margin, and the animation shows what ships
description:
Two things the transcript check and the demo work turned up, both about the README showing
something a reader cannot rely on.

1. The `pick` demo is close to a coin flip on the free backend. `jevify pick "last month's
   electricity bill"` (README.md:141, docs/guide/getting-started.md:67) chose
   `con_edison_electric_bill_july.pdf` at 0.46 against a runner-up of 0.42 on one keyless run,
   where the page shows the August bill; two later runs agreed with the page. A demo that
   depends on a 0.04 margin will fail in front of a reader, and the weekly drift check will
   flag it at random.

   Measure it: run the demo twelve times on each backend with JEVIFY_NO_CACHE=1 and record best,
   next and the chosen file every time. Then decide, and say which the numbers support:
   (a) The demo is fine and the one failure was the measured run-to-run spread
       (evals/variance/, 1.6 percent of answers cold). Keep it, and say nothing.
   (b) The file names are genuinely ambiguous, because "last month" is a date question and the
       names carry months. Change the demo's records or its description so the right answer is
       clear to a reader at a glance and the margin is wide, and re-record.
   (c) The demo asks jevify to reason about dates, which the guides tell readers to leave to
       other tools. If that is what it is doing, the demo teaches the wrong use and should be
       replaced with one that asks about meaning.
   Prefer the option the reader is best served by, not the one that keeps the current text.

2. docs/img/fill.svg still animates `git log --oneline -30` and narrates 0.99. The console block
   beneath it in README.md now shows `git log --oneline v0.8.3..v0.9.3` resolving at 0.70
   keyless (next 0.15, none 0.15), because that listing holds two other routing commits.
   Redraw the animation to the command that ships, with the numbers a real run produced. Keep the
   hand-built style: read docs/img/why.svg and docs/img/label.svg and match their structure,
   timing and palette. No generator, no dependency, no external font.

Whatever changes in the pages, update the matching row in tests/transcripts.rs and run the check
on both backends to prove it passes:
    cargo test --test transcripts -- --ignored --test-threads=1
    TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=<key> cargo test --test transcripts -- --ignored --test-threads=1

Write set: README.md, docs/guide/getting-started.md, docs/img/fill.svg, docs/demo/examples.sh,
docs/demo/ (the pick demo's record files, if you change them), tests/transcripts.rs.
Done when: the pick demo's outcome is measured over twelve runs per backend and the choice is
made on those numbers; the animation shows the command that ships; the drift check passes on both
backends; the gate passes (cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings,
cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed files). Workers never commit; the lead
commits.
close_reason: Option (c) on the numbers: the demo was a date comparison, which VISION reserves for code, and its answer was right only in September. 24 runs never misfired but the margin never exceeded 0.29 and one keyless run sat exactly on 0.50. The replacement asks about meaning and shares no word with the answer's name: 0.97-1.00 on both backends, 24 of 24. fill.svg redrawn to the shipped command with the numbers a real run produced.

title: 1.5 filter and the scorer: print every record for which a statement is true
description:
Plan bead: 1.5 — filter and the scorer. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: `CMD | jevify filter 'statement'` prints every record of its input for which the statement is true, byte for byte and in input order, keeps what it is unsure about, flows, and leaves a way back to the full input. The scorer that `label` reuses lives here.

Context: plan §1 (filter row: exit 0 kept some, 1 kept none, 3 every record unsure; the `-v` bullet), §2.3 "The scorer" (all bullets) and the `--files` and machine-format bullets above it, §2.4, §3 Phase 1 "Done when", §5 "Output verbs". Built on src/records.rs (hunch-7zg.2), `Client::ask_each` (hunch-7zg.3) and src/save.rs (hunch-7zg.4), all read-only here. Bead 1.0 left the stub src/cmd/filter.rs and the CLI flags. Decisions, final:
- One Noul per record through `ask_each`: the labels are "the statement holds" and "the statement does not hold"; the statement goes into `instructions` together with "judge this one record". Verdict per record with `is::band_verdict` (src/cmd/is.rs:54-62, read-only): yes, no, unsure.
- Asymmetric doubt: unsure records are kept in both directions (with and without -v). `--strict` drops the unsure. `-v` is inversion, as `grep -v`: it keeps the records where the statement is false; it is not verbosity (`--verbose` has no short flag since bead 1.0). `-c` prints the count.
- Byte-identical records are judged once; every occurrence is printed.
- Flow: hold a `BTreeMap<usize, Vec<Response>>` of finished batches and a cursor. When the batch at the cursor arrives, its kept records are written and the cursor moves; later batches wait in the map. `run_cli` writes `Outcome.human` only after dispatch returns (src/lib.rs:151-158), which is too late for a flow: on the human path this verb writes its records straight to a locked stdout (`std::io::stdout().lock()`), handles a write error of kind BrokenPipe there as exit 0 (drop the stream, which cancels the queued requests), and returns an empty `human`. With a machine format nothing flows and the envelope comes at the end.
- A machine format and a record that is not UTF-8: the envelope entry carries `text` as lossy UTF-8, `lossy: true` and the record's 1-based `ordinal` (the helper of src/records.rs); no base64. The caller recovers the bytes from its own input or the saved input.
- `--files`: the records are paths, the evidence is the excerpt, through the one async function of src/records.rs (the withholding function first, then the path resolved against the working directory, then the read inside spawn_blocking). Never call `sort::excerpt` here. The status line says `excerpts withheld: N` when N > 0.
- Independence of records is a property of the classifier backend only (on TypeSafe 20 records share a state and each question names its record). `filter A | filter B = filter B | filter A` is a contract test on FakeJev, not a claim about the model; do not state it as a property in a message or a comment.
- Before the first request, on stderr: `jevify filter: 10074 records, 3120 distinct, 4 requests`. ONE summary status line, prefixed `jevify filter:` and written by the verb before it returns. It is NOT required to be the last stderr line: `--verbose` diagnostics (src/lib.rs:160-170) and the error lines of `report_error` (:196-205) may follow it, and this bead cannot and need not change that renderer; tests assert that stderr contains the line, not its position. The same holds for `jevify filter: answered X of Y` on a quota 429, which comes before the error lines. The line, as the vision shows: `jevify filter: kept 31 of 10074, 2 unsure, full output: PATH` (or `jevify filter: kept 31 of 10074, 2 unsure, full output: not saved (<reason>)` with data.complete=false). The input is saved before the first request unless --no-save.
- The ceiling is 20,000 distinct records: exit 6 `too_many`, no request, and the message says to narrow with grep or head. There is no flag to raise it.
- 429: a 429 whose body `code` is `rate_limit_day` is never retried by the client (hunch-7zg.3) and ends the verb with exit 4, message "daily quota of the free backend reached"; the printed records are a correct prefix and the verb writes the one status line `jevify filter: answered 3000 of 3120` before it returns the error. A `rate_limit_minute` 429 is retried inside the client (one wait up to 60 s) and is invisible here except in time. A 429 whose `Retry-After` exceeds 60 s is not retried: exit 4, the message names the limit, and the prefix rule is the same. The save directory comes from `config::save_dir(Option<&str>)` (bead 1.0); this verb reads JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR and passes it.
- The model: `meta.model` is a string, distinct models joined with ", " (hunch-7zg.3). A part that does not start with `jev` is named in the status line: `answered by ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-micro, not Jev`; output verbs still answer.
- No -e, -n, -A/-B/-C, no JSON mode, no --max-records (cut on purpose, plan "Later"). Line numbers come from `grep -n -C2 -F -f <(jevify filter 'x' < build.log) build.log`.
- The signature of this verb is `filter::run(ctx, statement: &str, flags: FilterFlags { invert, count, strict, split, files, no_save }, machine: bool)`, installed and wired by bead 1.0 (hunch-7zg.1), whose dispatch passes every parsed flag; `Split` (`Lines`, `Nul`, `Para`) comes from src/records.rs. This bead fills the body: it may adjust a parameter type if the code demands it, never the set of parameters, and it never touches src/lib.rs or src/cli.rs.
- Any test that uses raw `cargo_bin` (not `common::jevify()` / `jevify_classifier()`) and invokes `filter` or `why` sets `JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR` to a temporary directory or passes `--no-save`.
- Expose the scorer (records + questions -> ordered per-record responses with flow, the locked-stdout writer included) as `pub(crate)` so bead hunch-qxn (`label`) calls it without editing this file.
- The live test for one filter batch per backend goes into tests/live.rs (#[ignore]), after hunch-7zg.5 has migrated `live_run_routes_tar` in that file.

Files (write set): src/cmd/filter.rs, tests/filter.rs (new), tests/live.rs (one added test). Everything else is read-only. If the CLI lacks a flag, the owner of src/cli.rs is hunch-7zg.1: post in its thread.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.2, hunch-7zg.3, hunch-7zg.4 (and hunch-7zg.1 through them), hunch-7zg.5 (it writes tests/live.rs first).

Done when, as contract tests in tests/filter.rs (exit code and --json envelope for each path):
- 2,500 records on the classifier backend send three requests; 20 per request on TypeSafe; 20,001 distinct records send none and exit 6 `too_many`.
- Coloured `rg`-style output, CRLF, a NUL under -0 and non-UTF-8 records come out byte-identical; blank records are dropped; order is input order. Under --json a non-UTF-8 record is `text` (lossy), `lossy: true`, `ordinal`.
- Flow: the first batch is on stdout before the last is answered (delayed mock); a closed stdout (`| head -3` equivalent) ends with exit 0 and fewer requests than the full run; the human path returns an empty `human` (no record is printed twice).
- -v inverts (a record judged no is kept, one judged yes is dropped, an unsure one is kept), and `--verbose` is separate; -c; --strict; unsure kept and counted; exit 0 kept some, 1 kept none, 3 every record unsure; empty stdin. "stdin is a terminal" is covered by the unit test of src/input.rs (hunch-7zg.1); no process-level test here.
- No test writes outside its temporary directory: the saved inputs land under the per-test `JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR` that `jevify()` and `jevify_classifier()` set (hunch-7zg.3); a test that sets its own save directory uses a temporary one.
- `filter A | filter B` equals `filter B | filter A` on FakeJev.
- -0 --files judges file excerpts and prints the paths unchanged; a relative path works from the working directory; a captured request for `filter --files` over a directory with a `.npmrc` holds no content of the `.npmrc`, and the status line says `excerpts withheld: 1`.
- stderr contains the one status line `jevify filter: kept K of N, U unsure, full output: PATH` (one line, not two; containment, not position), also under `--verbose`, where diagnostics follow it; two runs give one file; an unwritable save directory gives `not saved` and data.complete=false; --no-save.
- A `rate_limit_day` 429 (the FakeJev quota responder) leaves a correct prefix, exit 4, a stderr that contains `jevify filter: answered X of Y` before the error lines, and exactly one request reached the quota responder; a `rate_limit_minute` 429 with `Retry-After: 1` is retried and the run completes.
- An answer from a model that is not Jev is named in the status line, and meta.model holds the joined string.
- By hand on the default backend, when the network allows (report as NOT RUN otherwise): `cargo test 2>&1 | jevify filter 'reports a failed assertion'` and `seq 1 10074 | jevify filter 'x' | head -3`.
- The gate below passes.

The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. - The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
notes: Implementation and contract tests added in the authorized three paths. Worker checks: fmt, check --locked --all-targets, clippy --locked --all-targets -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, UBS all exit 0. Filter unit and offline preflight pass. Full test and lib attempts pass 80 units but sandbox blocks records::tests::non_utf8_file_excerpt with Operation not permitted; filter contract attempt passes offline preflight and cannot bind wiremock ports for ten tests. Live classifier probe cannot send requests to classifier.dev. Lead must run full and filter contracts outside sandbox before acceptance, commit and closure. Shared scorer: pub(crate) score(client, evidence, questions, callback) delivers ordered response batches; callback false cancels; write_record handles locked stdout and BrokenPipe. No commit, push, close or dependency changes.
close_reason: filter and the scorer. A live keyless run judged 41 records in one request and kept the one panic line. Two gate failures went back to workers: status lines per mode, and withholding judged on the path as written. Lead gate outside the sandbox: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full cargo test --locked (18 suites pass, 4 live tests NOT RUN), ubs exit 0.
