title: One cache flag, one meaning, and every store with a stated retention
description:
hunch-6pv8 established what each store in the cache directory keeps and corrected the documents. It
also found three behaviours that the documents now describe accurately but that a reader would still
call wrong. It priced each and deliberately changed none. Decide each on its own merits.

1. `--no-cache` does not cover the `tool` kind's inventory. `source::Env::from_process` reads
   `JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR` for itself and never sees the flag, so `pick --no-cache --from tool` still
   writes the inventory file. `route`'s copy honours the flag. One switch with two behaviours is a
   trap. The fix is to thread the configured cache directory into `Env::from_process` rather than
   reading the variable there: a few lines plus every caller's tests, no hit-rate effect, and one
   rebuild of about two seconds per PATH when a user does pass the flag. Do this unless reading the
   code tells you the flag was deliberately scoped to answers only, in which case rename nothing
   and say so in the documents instead.

2. `--no-cache` relocates `sort --apply`'s recovery journal to the system temporary directory
   instead of suppressing it. Nothing turns the journal off, and it has no expiry. The journal is
   what `--undo` reads, so suppressing it removes the ability to undo a move: that is a real
   trade-off, not an oversight. Decide whether `--no-cache` should suppress it (and `--undo` then
   fail with a message saying why), or whether the journal should be exempt from the flag and say
   so plainly, since it is the one store whose loss costs the user something. Whichever you
   choose, the journal needs a stated retention: it currently has none.

3. Expired answers are ignored but never deleted. `save::prune` touches only `outputs/`, so the
   answers directory grows without bound even though entries past seven days are never served.
   A prune shaped like `save::prune` costs nothing in hit rate. Apply the same care the saved-input
   prune took: only the answers subtree, only files the cache named itself, no recursion into
   anything it did not create, no symlink followed, prune on write, best effort, and a test that
   plants a file outside the subtree and proves it survives.

Read src/jev/cache.rs, src/save.rs, src/source.rs and src/cmd/sort.rs before deciding anything, and
read the no-delete rule in AGENTS.md before writing item 3.

For each item, write the decision and its reasoning into the bead with
`br update <id> --append-notes` before you implement it, and state in your report what breaks for an
existing caller. Items 1 and 2 change what a documented flag does, so the CHANGELOG entry must say
so plainly and the capability strings, PRIVACY.md, the configuration guide and ROBOT_MODE must
agree with the code when you are done.

Write set: src/jev/cache.rs, src/save.rs, src/source.rs, src/cmd/sort.rs, src/config.rs,
src/cmd/agent.rs, PRIVACY.md, docs/guide/configuration.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, CHANGELOG.md,
tests/**.
Done when: one flag has one meaning or the exception is documented where a reader meets the flag;
every store in the cache directory has a stated retention and the answers subtree enforces its own;
the pruning cannot leave its subtree and a test proves it; the gate passes (cargo fmt --check,
cargo check --locked --all-targets, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test
--locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed files). Workers never commit; the lead commits.
notes: BLOCKED on the other session (jevify-f6) until hunch-080s, hunch-x4w and the filter recalibration land: this bead's write set (src/jev/cache.rs, src/source.rs, src/cmd/sort.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs, docs) overlaps theirs. Do not dispatch a worker until that session reports its gate green.

title: classifier.dev fallback when there is no TypeSafe key
description:
Outcome: grevi works with no TypeSafe key, by using classifier.dev as a second backend. Lead-added bead (Thomas, 2026-09-19): "have an additional bead to have classifier dev as an alternative API if you don't have a typesafe api key".

KEY FACT from Thomas (2026-09-19, supersedes any guess): classifier.dev runs Jev behind the scenes and serves it for free. So the features should be at full parity, not a degraded mode. Design for parity and prove it; do not write caveat copy about a weaker fallback unless a measurement forces you to.

What Thomas gave us: "Zero-shot text classification over plain HTTP. You send text and a list of labels, you get back the label that fits and how sure the model is. There is no API key or account required for free use... the OpenAPI 3.1 description is at https://classifier.dev/openapi.json and a short index at https://classifier.dev/llms.txt".

Step 1 - research before code (record findings in the bead notes):
- Read https://classifier.dev/llms.txt and https://classifier.dev/openapi.json (curl, sandbox disabled). Establish: endpoints, request and response shape, label limit, text size limit, rate limits, latency, whether it returns the same probabilities as Jev, and the terms of use for a client like grevi.
- Map grevi's two question kinds onto it: "which one" (choice over options plus NONE) and "is it" (absolute yes/no with a probability). Since the model is the same, the work is the wire format, not the semantics. If a shape is missing (NONE, absolute yes/no, batching, the 200-option window), say so plainly and name the workaround.
- Verify parity, do not assume it: run the existing evals (scripts/eval_run.py, scripts/eval_why.py) against both backends and record the two numbers side by side. Equal numbers are the expected result and the evidence we publish. A real gap is a finding: report it before writing any copy about it.

Step 2 - implementation (small, behind the existing client seam):
- A backend chosen by config: TypeSafe Jev when a key is present, classifier.dev when none is. GREVI_BACKEND=typesafe|classifier forces either. No key, no prompt, no signup path.
- Reuse the existing cache, retry, timeout and error mapping. Keep exit codes and the JSON envelope identical. meta reports which backend and model answered.
- health reports the active backend. capabilities lists the new env var and the backend field.
- Respect the free service: honour its rate limits, set a clear user agent (grevi/<version>), and keep concurrency conservative by default.
- Tests: contract tests with a wiremock fake for the new backend (no live network in the default run), plus one #[ignore] live test.
- Docs: README (a short "No key needed" paragraph - grevi runs out of the box, a TypeSafe key gets you your own quota), docs/guide/configuration.md and faq.md, PRIVACY.md (with this backend the text goes to classifier.dev instead of TypeSafe).

Out of scope: a local model, other providers, changing the threshold semantics, any change to the Jev path's behaviour.

Gate and rules: full gate (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, tests, doc, cargo deny, ubs exit 0 on changed code) plus the live checks above; RULE ZERO (no rm in any form, no prompts, no redirects to variable paths); shared checkout under Agent Mail (register, reserve paths, thread = this bead ID, report to lead-0); CI pre-check, claim, work; signed commits; pre-push gitleaks and diff read; push; CI green.
notes:
Research (curl, 2026-09-19): POST https://classifier.dev/v1/classify, no key. Dimensions mode {items:[text], dimensions:{name:{labels,instructions}}} maps grevi Questions 1:1. Limits: 100 labels/dimension, 20 dimensions/request, 32,000 chars/input, 4,000 chars/instructions, 16,000 chars of definitions; free 3,000 classifications/min and 20,000/day per IP; Retry-After on 429; errors {error,code} with stable codes. PARITY CONFIRMED: a live call answers model "jev-1.13.0", the exact build grevi pins, and the 502 codes are literally typesafe_<status> - classifier.dev is a free front end to Jev, not a weaker model.
Gaps and the honest mapping: (1) 200-option window does not fit 100 labels -> the classifier backend windows at 99 + NONE; (2) per-option criteria have no field -> folded into the dimension instructions; (3) a Jev Noul is absolute, a dimension is relative -> a Noul goes out as a two-label choice between its true/false criteria (using the criteria sentences as labels, not "yes"/"no", measurably better, see below) and P(true) is that label score; (4) >20 questions -> the client splits an ask into sequential chunks of 20 and merges; (5) 32k-char input -> tournament and `is` take the min of their own budget and the backend cap; (6) usage counts classifications not tokens -> meta.input_tokens and cost_usd are 0, which is true: it is free. NONE and batching need no workaround.
Evals, both backends, GREVI_NO_CACHE=1, 2026-09-19. eval_run hand-written: 34/39 top-1 classifier vs 34/39 typesafe (abstain correct 8/10 vs 8/10). eval_run NL2Bash held-out: 34/120 vs 33/120 (abstained 70 vs 66). eval_run args spot check: tool right 9/20 vs 12/20 (n=20, grevis weakest path either way). eval_why: hit@1 14/20 and hit@3 15/20 on BOTH; data.any median 0.94 vs 0.78. Cost: $0.00 classifier, $0.53 typesafe. Verdict: parity.
First mapping attempt used plain "yes"/"no" labels for a Noul and lost 8 points on NL2Bash (26/120); switching the labels to the criteria sentences (the services own guidance: a semantic label beats a code) recovered it to 34/120. That is the change that bought parity.
Observed once in ~3,400 classifier requests: exit 4 api_protocol on one NL2Bash route (a dimension came back without scores, which the API documents as possible). Not reproducible; grevi reports it honestly as exit 4 rather than inventing a distribution.
close_reason: classifier.dev backend: keyless by default, same Jev model, parity proven on both evals. ubs exit 0 on all changed files after restructuring one match guard (self.backend == Backend::Classifier tripped its timing-safe-comparison check; now a precomputed body_rejected with matches!, behaviour identical).

title: file kind: tier-two excerpt carries meaning, content phrases resolve
description:
Outcome: the `file` kind resolves a phrase that describes a file's content, not only its name. The plan's Phase 3 acceptance case passes live on the default backend: `jevify fill --dry-run -- cat 'src/cmd/@{file:stages hunks}'` substitutes `src/cmd/add.rs`, and `'src/@{file:the recipe engine}'` substitutes `src/source.rs`.

Evidence (live acceptance for hunch-7zg.21, 2026-09-22, default backend, model jev-1.13.0): both cases above abstain with `no_match; candidates 11 of 11` and `candidates 32 of 32`, exit 3, one request each (fresh cache). `pick --from file 'the recipe engine'` also abstains (any 0.27). Name-matching phrases resolve (`the tool inventory` → inventory.rs 0.87, `the git diff parser` → gitdiff.rs 0.94). Cause: the tier-two evidence of `file` is the file's first lines (`source::enrich_in`, through `records::excerpts`), and in Rust files the first lines are `use` statements with no meaning. It is also possible that tier two never runs for one-window listings (every one-window `file` fill sent exactly 1 request); check this first, because plan §2 says tier two goes to the finalists.

Files (write set): src/source.rs (the `file` excerpt and/or the tier-two trigger), src/records.rs only if the excerpt helper must change (keep the withholding policy first and unchanged), tests/fill.rs (one contract test with FakeJev proving that tier-two evidence for a `file` finalist carries meaningful lines, for example the module doc comment `//!` or the first lines after the imports, and that a withheld path still carries none). Everything else is read-only.

Decision (lead): the excerpt skips leading blank lines, `use`/`import`/`#include`/`mod`/`extern crate`/`package` lines and license/shebang headers, keeps doc comments (`//!`, `///`, `"""`, `#` comment blocks), and takes the first N meaningful lines with the same byte bound as today. Keep it simple: a line-prefix filter, no parser. If tier two never runs for one-window listings, make it run for the finalists as plan §2 says (still at most two rounds).

Done when:
- The contract test above passes; the existing suite stays green; the gate passes (cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked --all-targets, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps, cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed files).
- Live, with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key (never read or print the key), both acceptance commands above substitute the expected file under --dry-run. Report the status lines. If one still abstains after the fix, report the scores and stop; do not tune the threshold or the ratio.

Rules: AGENTS.md applies (main only, Agent Mail reservation, no rm/stash/restore/reset, no commit, no new dependency, Rust 1.87 floor, never weaken a test).
notes: Lead decision L1 (2026-09-22): the one-window shortcut sends the finals (round two) on NoMatch as well as on Ambiguous, for kinds with tier-two evidence; only a decisive Found skips round two. Still at most two rounds; the decision rule after round two is unchanged, so abstention stays possible. Write set adds src/cmd/fill.rs (the condition at :346), src/cmd/pick.rs (:249), tests/tournament.rs and any test asserting one request for a low-any single window of a tier-two kind (update the expected request count, never weaken the assertion), and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md §2 (the round-two sentence). Reason: plan §3 Phase 3 acceptance (stages hunks -> add.rs) requires content evidence, which names-only round one cannot give. If the live acceptance still abstains after L1, report the round-two scores; the lead then releases with the case documented as a known limit.
close_reason: Excerpts drop imports/headers; round two runs on NoMatch for tier-two kinds (L1); contract tests; gate 336 green, ubs 0. Live acceptance still abstains on jev-1.13.0 (stages hunks: NONE 0.73 vs best 0.19; recipe engine: NONE 0.48 vs best 0.27): released as a documented known limit, follow-up in hunch-lpp evaluation

title: CI fails on every release tag: a fill doc-example test needs branches that a tag checkout lacks
description:
Found by the hunch-lpp evaluation (jevify 0.7.0, 2026-09-22).

Evidence: the CI run on the v0.7.0 tag failed (run 35736209634), and so did the one on the v0.6.0 tag (35672171134). The release workflow succeeded both times. The failing test is tests/agent.rs `documented_input_side_shell_examples_run_against_the_binary`, at tests/agent.rs:64:

    jevify fill --dry-run -- git switch '@{branch:the auth refactor}'
    jevify fill: not run: arg 3 branch: no_match; ; candidates 0 of 0, omitted 0; model not requested

A tag push checks out a detached HEAD with no local or remote branch refs, so the branch lister returns 0 candidates. The test depends on the branches of the checkout it runs in. The main-branch runs pass.

Expected: (1) The test builds its own repository with known branches, as other fill tests do, or it runs the documented example against a fixture. CI on tags then passes. (2) Product side: an empty listing and "nothing fits" are two different answers. With 0 candidates, fill says so plainly (for example "no branch to choose from") instead of reporting no_match with an empty closest field. Decide whether that remains exit 3.

Suggested write set: tests/agent.rs, and src/cmd/fill.rs only for (2).
notes: Lead scope: this bead does item (1) only. Write set: tests/agent.rs (plus a fixture under tests/ if needed). Item (2), the empty-listing message, moves to hunch-b25, which owns the fill status line.
close_reason: Doc-example test builds its own git repo (branches, commits, files), no dependency on checkout refs; gate 336 green; item (2) moved to hunch-b25

title: A drifted README transcript fails a check instead of shipping
description:
Three README transcripts were found on 2026-09-22 to show answers the binary no longer gives:
the commit demo named a wrong commit, the two-candidate fill demo abstains where the page shows
0.73, and the nothing-fits demo picks a commit on TypeSafe four runs of four. Each was true when
written. Nothing in the repository notices when the behaviour moves under a documented example.

tests/agent.rs already runs the documented input-side shell examples against the binary, but
against a fake or with no backend, so it checks the command parses and runs, not that the answer
is still the answer.

Outcome: an opt-in check that runs every transcript in README.md and docs/guide/getting-started.md
against a real backend and fails when the answer drifts. Model it on tests/live.rs: #[ignore] by
default, run in CI only where a key or the keyless backend is available, never part of the
ordinary `cargo test` gate.

What it must catch, taken from the three failures:
  - a marker that resolved now abstaining, or the reverse
  - a marker resolving to a different item than the page shows
  - the nothing-fits example resolving to anything at all
What it must tolerate: the score moving. Compare the decision and the chosen item, not the
probability, and say in the test why. A transcript whose decision is stable only on one backend
is a transcript that does not belong in the README: make the check run both backends.

Decide where the expected answers live. Extracting them from the Markdown is brittle; a small
table beside the test, with the file and line each expectation came from, is probably better.
Choose and say why in the test's doc comment.

Also decide what the check does about a demo whose input is the repository itself, since the
history grows: pin what can be pinned (a commit range, a fixed candidate list), and say so.

Write set: tests/ (a new file), docs/guide/contributing.md or AGENTS.md if the procedure needs
recording, .github/workflows/ if you add a job. No change to src/.

Done when: the check exists, is ignored by default, passes today against both backends on every
README and getting-started transcript, and fails when a transcript's expected item is changed by
hand (show that it fails). Gate: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets
-- -D warnings, cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed files.
Workers never commit; the lead commits and closes.
close_reason: Commit f19a206. tests/transcripts.rs, three ignored tests: a live half that runs every README and getting-started transcript on both backends comparing decision and chosen item only, and a no-network half that proves the expectation table still matches the page it cites. Proven both ways: passes on both backends (13 transcripts, 31 classifications keyless, 22 keyed) and fails when an expected item is changed by hand. Weekly workflow, never on push. It found a stale demo on day one, filed separately.

for the `--no-save` flag or a non-blank `JEVIFY_NO_SAVE`; a successful save prunes the store's

title: Rework README and docs: use cases, live demos, simpler examples, owner's voice
description:
Outcome: a first-time reader of README.md understands in 30 seconds what jevify does, why they want it, and how to try it. The documents read as Thomas wrote them: plain, concrete, no AI slop.

Why: the owner reads the current README and docs and "does not even know what it is doing". The documents describe mechanics (verbs, envelopes, tiers, kinds) before the reader sees one useful result.

Scope (write set): README.md, docs/guide/*.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md (prose only; the contract stays byte-for-byte the same), docs/demo/ (new: demo scripts and recordings). src/, tests/, CHANGELOG.md and docs/VISION.md are read-only. Runs after release 0.7.0 (hunch-7zg.21) so `label` and the kinds are in the documents.

What to do:
1. Lead with use cases, not verbs. Open README.md with three to five short, real problems an agent or a human has ("which branch is the release work on?", "which of these 900 log lines is the cause?", "fill this command's argument from what exists"), each as one command and its real output. Then the one-line idea: jevify points at the right thing among real things, and says "nothing fits" honestly.
2. Simpler examples. Every example runs on a typical macOS dev machine against a public repository or a small fixture in docs/demo/. Show the real output, captured from a live run with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key. No invented output.
3. Interactive demos. Record terminal demos (for example with vhs or asciinema, whichever is already installed; no new dependency in the crate) from scripts committed in docs/demo/. Embed them in README.md as GIF/SVG. Each demo is under 20 seconds and shows one use case.
4. Move reference material down. The machine envelope, exit codes, calibration and kinds reference stay complete, but in docs/ROBOT_MODE.md and docs/guide/, linked from a short "Reference" section.
5. Voice. Write in Thomas's voice. Before writing, load and follow these skills: `digital-double` (read references/voice.md and the technical-English section of references/voice-examples.md), then pass every changed document through `unslop` (two-pass rewrite) and `jfp:de-slopify`. Also apply `jfp:readme-reviser` framing: present tense, as if it was always so.

Rules: AGENTS.md "Docs state what jevify does" (no meta language, no retrospective language, dates only next to a measurement); user-facing docs say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key and "a typical macOS dev machine", never a real key path or personal tooling; the repository is public (no local paths, no personal details). No communications drafts in the repository. The agent-facing contract (exit codes, envelope, error kinds) does not change.

Done when:
- README.md opens with use cases and a demo, and a reader reaches a working command within the first screen.
- Every example output in README.md and docs/guide/ comes from a live run, and docs/demo/ holds the script that reproduces it.
- At least three recorded demos are embedded and render on GitHub.
- The owner reads README.md and says it is clear. This is the acceptance gate; the lead asks for it.
- `unslop` audit mode reports no AI patterns on the changed documents.
- Tests still pass (tests that check documents, for example tests/agent.rs guards on capabilities and docs, stay green).
notes:
Owner preference (replaces the earlier note): animations like the ones in commit 4c39b84 (docs/img/run.svg, docs/img/sort.svg: hand-built animated SVGs that replay one real command) are valuable to highlight jevify's important features. Do not reuse or update those two animations: the product has changed. Choose the features that matter most today (for example fill resolving a marker, pick --from, label, the honest 'nothing fits'), and make one animated SVG in that style for each, in docs/img/, replaying a captured live run and showing how jevify reaches its answer. The old SVGs are a style reference only. A vhs/asciinema recording is a fallback, and the demos never add a dependency to the crate.
Lead: README says 'batch up to 1,000 records per request on classifier.dev'; since hunch-0it the keyless batch is 60 records per request. Fix it in the rework.
Lead 2026-09-22: committed and pushed for the owner's review; open until the owner says the README is clear. Four animated SVGs (why, fill, label, nothing-fits); docs/demo/examples.sh reproduces every README example; 60-records fix applied in README and four guide pages.
Lead decision N5 (review round 8, 2026-09-22): stays open for the owner. The owner is asked again only after hunch-hd8 (contract and docs drift: README.md:66 dry-run 'exec', verbs.md:43 origin/ ref, VISION.md:231 1,000-record batches, fill finalist figure, exit 7 name) lands, so the README examples match the installed release. hunch-hd8 is now a blocking dependency of this bead. Voice work of hunch-60l is folded here; hunch-60l keeps only the measured agent-harness section.
Owner 2026-09-22 read the reworked README: 'too bad', asked for a revamp with the digital-double, unslop and jfp skills. That revamp is hunch-9hx; the structure, the live examples and the four animations of this bead stay.

title: The nothing-fits demo abstains on both backends, or we learn why not
description:
Found while measuring the commit kind (hunch-e4os, evals/commit-attractor/): docs/demo/examples.sh
line 39 runs `@{commit:rewrote everything in Go}` as the nothing-fits demonstration. On TypeSafe
it returns 041e6d1 ("feat: scaffold hunch CLI and dispatch") in 4 runs of 4, at 0.52 to 0.73
against none 0.20 to 0.26. Keyless it abstains, as the demo intends.

So the demonstration of "jevify says nothing fits" acts on TypeSafe. Decide which it is and fix
the right thing:

(a) The description is not actually unmatchable in this history. A scaffolding commit in a Rust
    repository is a weak but real neighbour of "rewrote everything in Go". If so, pick a
    description this history genuinely cannot match, verify it abstains in four runs on BOTH
    backends, and use it in examples.sh, README.md and the nothing-fits SVG caption if it names
    the phrase. Say in the file why that phrase is unmatchable.
(b) The gate is wrong on this case: a best of 0.52 against none 0.26 passes the ratio rule
    (src/tournament.rs, WINNER_RATIO 2.0) while a reader would call it nothing. If the evidence
    says the rule is wrong rather than the phrase, do not change the rule in this bead: report
    it with the numbers and file what would have to change and what it would cost on
    evals/validation and evals/holdout.

Measure before choosing. Run at least 6 candidate phrasings on both backends, 4 repeats each,
with JEVIFY_NO_CACHE=1, and record best, next and none for every run. A phrase that abstains
3 times in 4 is not good enough for a demo; require 4 of 4 on both backends.

Write set: docs/demo/examples.sh, evals/commit-attractor/nothing-fits/** (runs and a short
note), README.md and docs/img/nothing-fits.svg only if the chosen phrase appears there.
Another worker holds README.md and most of docs/ right now: check with `br show hunch-yh8 --json`
and Agent Mail before reserving, and if README.md is taken, do your part in examples.sh and the
runs, and leave the lead a one-line note of the README change needed.

Done when: the demo abstains 4 of 4 on both backends with the phrase that ships, or the bead
reports that no phrase does and explains what that says about the gate; the runs are recorded;
and the gate passes (cargo fmt --check, cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed
files). Workers never commit; the lead commits and closes.
close_reason: Explanation (a): the description was matchable, not the gate too loose. TypeSafe answered rewrote-everything-in-Go at 0.67-0.71 against none 0.21-0.24, three times the required ratio. Eight phrasings, four repeats, both backends: every genuinely unmatchable description holds none at 0.94+ on TypeSafe and above best keyless. examples.sh now runs 'ports the user interface to Android' (none 1.00 TypeSafe 4/4). Rule change priced and not warranted.

title: Next step 2: source-held-out set for the 0.9.x behaviours, both backends, three days, with availability, fallback and 402 rates
description:
Outcome: the 0.9.x behaviours (three-way `filter`, `why` panic finals, `pick` preferring the thing, route ties, the `fill` finals shortcut, branch prefix) are measured on a source-held-out set that was not used to choose any wording or threshold, on both backends, repeated over three days, with availability, fallback and 402 rates recorded. This is next step 2 of the round 9 synthesis (section 6).

What it proves: generalisation beyond the development set (the three-way filter's wordings were chosen on both splits, benchmarks/results.md:193-195, so the frozen set no longer tests it), and whether "no key" is reliable: the keyless promise rests on one free endpoint that on the measurement day answered with another model and refused batches over 60 (results.md:33-43), and backends disagree on 9 of 153 adjudicated cases with gaps to 0.54 (results.md:157-161).

Method: new cases drawn from repositories, logs and PATHs not used anywhere in evals/ or benchmarks/ (source-held-out, not just case-held-out), at least 20 per verb touched by 0.9.x, gold by two annotators as in evals/validation/README.md with adjudication recorded; three runs per backend on three different days, `JEVIFY_NO_CACHE=1`; per run: coverage, accuracy, abstentions, false actions, and for the keyless backend the answering model (`meta.decision.model.answering`), 502/402 counts and fallback events from telemetry. Report decided-case accuracy and abstention correctness separately, as results.md:94-122 does. Depends on the contract bead: the envelope must report finals and gates truthfully before it is read.

Files (write set): evals/holdout/ (cases, gold, adjudication), benchmarks/results.md (new section) or benchmarks/holdout.md, scripts/ (the runner). No change to src/ in this bead; anything it finds is filed as a new bead.

Done when: the three days are recorded per backend with the rates above, the section states what generalised and what did not with the numbers, and the README's qualitative claims are checked against it. Gate before handing back (AGENTS.md, sandbox disabled): cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs <changed files>. Never weaken a test to pass. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
notes:
hunch-hwt landed the set and the runner (commit 0f3702c). What remains here is the three measurement days: run scripts/holdout_run.py on each backend on three different days with JEVIFY_NO_CACHE=1, then holdout_score.py, and write the section. Day 1 can run as soon as the release is out. Read the set's honesty caveat before quoting its accuracy: one reader labelled both passes.
Hold the three measurement days until hunch-080s and hunch-x4w land. Measuring now would measure a binary about to change: x4w alone turns 7 of 56 study calls from a failed command into a working one, and 080s changes which argv shapes are accepted. Start day one on the post-080s release.

title: Does the commit kind work keyless on a real repository, or is 332191a an attractor
description:
Observed while re-running the README demos (hunch-34c): the `commit` kind on the keyless backend
returns the same wrong commit, 332191a, as best for several unrelated descriptions, and a
description that nearly quotes its target's own subject line -- `@{commit:keyless batches of at
most 60 records}` -- returns no_match with none at 0.34. Eight other phrasings abstained or
picked 332191a. The pool was 246 commits over 3 windows.

If this reproduces, the `commit` kind does not work on the free backend at the sizes a real
repository has, and README tells readers to start keyless. That is a product claim, not a
cosmetic one.

This bead measures; it changes no code. Decide first whether 332191a is an attractor: build a
set of at least 20 commit descriptions over this repository, each written from a commit's own
diff without looking at its subject line, spread over the history so the targets sit in
different windows. Include the eight phrasings above if you can recover them from the bead
hunch-34c notes. Run each on both backends with JEVIFY_NO_CACHE=1 and record the answer, the
gate scores, the window count and the answering model.

Report, per backend: how often the right commit is first; how often the same wrong commit
returns for different descriptions, and which; whether the failures cluster by window; whether
the right commit was even in the finals (JEVIFY_DECISION=round_one gives the finalists); and
whether the pool size or the excerpt content explains it. Compare against the `branch` kind on
the same repository as a control, since both take the names shortcut.

State plainly which of these the evidence supports: the kind is sound and the descriptions were
weak; the shortlist drops the right commit before the finals; the evidence a commit carries is
too thin to tell commits apart; or the free backend cannot do it at this pool size. If the
answer is that a documented feature does not work keyless, say so and file what must change.

Write set: evals/commit-attractor/** (cases, runs, a short README with the finding),
benchmarks/results.md (one new dated section). No change to src/. Anything this finds that needs
a code or documentation change is a new bead, not this one.

Done when: the runs exist for both backends, the report answers every question above with its
numbers, and the conclusion names which explanation the evidence supports and which it rules
out. Gate: ubs on changed files; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1.
Workers never commit; the lead commits and closes.
close_reason: Measured, commit 14fd88e. No attractor: every wrong answer is a distinct near neighbour and 332191a comes back only for the description of its own diff. Hit@1 11/27 keyless, 14/27 TypeSafe, branch control 12/14 on both; the oldest window is 0/5 on both backends; keyless fails by abstaining with the target already in the finals. Pool size is not the cause (2/7 at both 60 and 248 on one subject line); the tier-two finals round is what makes the kind work. Ruled out: shortlist loss, thin evidence overall, free-backend failure.

title: Phase 0: JEVIFY_BASE_URL is https and host-bound; the key never follows it elsewhere
description:
Plan bead: Phase 0 — base URL. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: JEVIFY_BASE_URL can no longer send the bearer token and the evidence to an arbitrary host. Today src/config.rs and src/jev/client.rs send both to whatever the variable names, and `health` builds its own client that follows redirects.

Context: plan §3 "Phase 0". Decisions, final:
- JEVIFY_BASE_URL must be https.
- The TypeSafe backend accepts only the host api.typesafe.ai; the classifier backend accepts only classifier.dev.
- 127.0.0.1 and localhost accept any scheme, for wiremock (every contract test depends on this).
- A URL with userinfo is refused.
- Redirects are not followed (reqwest redirect policy none). This also covers the `health` client built at src/cmd/agent.rs:127 (`reqwest::Client::new()`, whose default policy follows redirects): build it with the same no-redirect policy.
- Host rules: hosts are compared case-insensitively; a trailing dot is refused; an explicit port other than 443 is refused on the two known hosts.
- A refusal is a configuration error before any request; use the existing error path of src/config.rs and keep error kinds stable.
Source: src/config.rs (Backend, base URL parsing; `Backend::window` at :34; JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR at :99), src/jev/client.rs (client construction), src/cmd/agent.rs:120-135 (`health`), tests/client.rs, tests/agent.rs (the `health` tests, :63-), tests/common/mod.rs (read-only; shows how tests point jevify at wiremock).

Files (write set): src/config.rs, src/jev/client.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs (the `health` client, and the `JEVIFY_BASE_URL` string of capabilities at :38, which says "overrides the base URL of whichever backend is active" today and may state the https and host rule), tests/client.rs, tests/agent.rs (the `health` redirect test only), docs/guide/configuration.md, PRIVACY.md, CHANGELOG.md. Inline unit tests in src/config.rs. Everything else is read-only.

Prerequisites: none. This bead blocks hunch-7zg.1 (1.0), which writes src/config.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs and tests/agent.rs next.

Done when:
- tests/client.rs holds and passes: plain http refused; unknown host refused; a TypeSafe key with classifier.dev refused; userinfo refused; a 302 not followed (the mock's redirect target receives no request); localhost accepted.
- tests/agent.rs holds and passes: `jevify health` against a mock that answers 302 to a second mock never reaches the second mock (assert zero requests there), and exits with the unavailable or protocol error the existing path gives, not 0.
- Unit tests in src/config.rs, each with its expected outcome:
  - `https://API.TypeSafe.AI` (upper case) with a key: accepted, treated as api.typesafe.ai.
  - `https://api.typesafe.ai.` (trailing dot): refused.
  - `https://api.typesafe.ai:443`: accepted. `https://api.typesafe.ai:8443` and `https://classifier.dev:8443`: refused.
  - `https://api.typesafe.ai.evil.example`: refused.
  - the binding is symmetric: `https://api.typesafe.ai` for the classifier backend (no key): refused; `https://classifier.dev` with a TypeSafe key: refused.
  - `https://classifier.dev:443` for the classifier backend: accepted (an explicit 443 is accepted; any other explicit port on a known host is refused).
  - an empty or blank value: the default URL of the backend, as for every variable today (`env`, src/config.rs:73-78, treats it as unset). A value that is not a URL: refused.
  - `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` and `http://localhost:PORT`: accepted on both backends.
  - `https://user:pw@classifier.dev`: refused.
- No key or evidence reaches a refused host (assert zero requests on the mock).
- docs/guide/configuration.md and PRIVACY.md state the rule in the present tense; CHANGELOG.md has the entry.
- The gate below passes.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
close_reason: Base URL bound to the backend's HTTPS host on 443, loopback exempt, userinfo refused, redirects off for inference, prewarm and health. Lead gate outside the sandbox: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full cargo test --locked (all suites pass, 4 live tests NOT RUN), worker ran check, doc and ubs exit 0.

title: classifier.dev scores 9/20 on the run args spot check, TypeSafe 12/20
description:
Measured during hunch-classifier-fallback-41x (commit 2fd203d): the two backends tie on every eval except the 20-case argument spot check, where classifier.dev picks the right tool 9/20 against TypeSafe's 12/20. Same model (jev-1.13.0), so the gap is in the wire mapping, not the model.

Investigate before it becomes lore:
- Re-run the spot check on both backends with GREVI_NO_CACHE=1, several times, and report the spread. 20 cases is small; establish whether 9 vs 12 is real or noise.
- If real, compare the exact requests grevi sends to each backend for the same case: the man-page excerpts, the option set, the NONE handling, and how the per-option criteria are folded into instructions on classifier.dev (it has no criteria field).
- Prime suspects, in order: the 100-option cap changing the window composition; criteria folded into instructions losing per-flag definitions; the 20-questions-per-request split changing what each question sees.
- Fix the mapping if the cause is ours. If the free service genuinely cannot express what the args pass needs, document that one line honestly in README and docs/guide/configuration.md rather than hiding it.

Also in scope, cheap: one transient api_protocol (exit 4) fired in about 3,400 classifier requests when a dimension came back with no scores (documented as nullable). Not reproducible. Decide whether one retry on that shape is right, or whether reporting it honestly is already correct.

Gate: full gate plus the live eval runs, with the numbers in the close reason.
close_reason: Obsolete with the run argument pass, which docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md (epic hunch-7zg) removes in bead 1.4 (hunch-7zg.5): route only prints, and fill is the only place where jevify starts a command.

title: fill branch: remote-only branch resolves to origin/<name>, which git switch refuses
description:
Outcome: `jevify fill -- git switch '@{branch:...}'` substitutes a name that `git switch` accepts. When the only match is a remote-tracking branch, the handle is the short branch name (`ticket/TPE-791`), which `git switch` resolves by its remote-tracking DWIM rule (creates a local tracking branch), instead of `origin/ticket/TPE-791`, which `git switch` refuses with `fatal: a branch is expected, got remote branch 'origin/ticket/TPE-791'`.

Evidence (jevify 0.8.0, jev-1.13.0, 2026-09-22, in ~/Projects/testify where the branch exists only as `remotes/origin/ticket/TPE-791`; agent task T1 of the hunch-lpp re-evaluation, a haiku agent given `jevify init agents`):

```
$ jevify fill --dry-run -- git switch '@{branch:allergy model and schema migration}'
'git' 'switch' 'origin/ticket/TPE-791'
jevify fill: branch origin/ticket/TPE-791 1.00 (next 0.00, none 0.00) origin/ticket/TPE-791 — feat(TPE-791): add Allergy model, SchemaV5 migration — 133 days ago; candidates 14, windows 1; model jev-1.13.0
jevify fill: exec 'git' 'switch' 'origin/ticket/TPE-791'
exit 0
```

The pick is right (the agent then ran `git rev-parse origin/ticket/TPE-791` itself and answered correctly), but without `--dry-run` the command that fill runs fails in git: `git switch` takes local branch names only; `git checkout origin/x` would detach HEAD. The branch kind lists candidates as `origin/<name>`, so every remote-only branch produces an argument that the documented example command (`jevify fill -- git switch '@{branch:the auth refactor}'`) cannot use.

Fix direction: for the branch kind, emit the short name when the candidate is a remote-tracking ref and no local branch of that name exists (git's DWIM then does the right thing for switch and checkout), or keep `origin/x` only for commands where a remote ref is valid (log, diff, rev-parse). Keep the ref shown in the status line. Add a contract test in tests/fill.rs with FakeJev: a remote-only branch candidate yields argv `git switch <short-name>`.

Files: src/source.rs or the branch recipe (candidate handle), tests/fill.rs, docs/guide/kinds.md (branch row).
Done when: the dry-run above prints `'git' 'switch' 'ticket/TPE-791'`; local branches keep their name; the contract test passes; the quality gate passes.
notes: Lead: CHANGELOG.md is the lead's; report a one-line Unreleased entry in the final message instead of editing it. Parallel workers: hunch-s2k (src/cmd/why.rs and its tests), hunch-emc (src/source.rs branch handle, tests/fill.rs, docs/guide/kinds.md), hunch-r2t (the dry-run stderr line, likely src/lib.rs or src/cmd/fill.rs). If your fix needs a file in another worker's set, coordinate through Agent Mail and wait for its release.
close_reason: remote-only branch listed by short name when one remote tracks it; qualified ref kept in evidence and for multi-remote names; contract test; dry-run would-run assertions added; gate green

title: The advertised keyless capacity is the one the backend actually serves
description:
The README advertises 3,267 candidates per marker on the keyless backend. A live trial on
2026-09-23 (scratchpad/trial-fresh.md) could not reach half of it: 1,500 commits returned
HTTP 429, then HTTP 502 on retry after a 45 second pause, at 15 to 18 seconds per attempt. 3,000
returned 502, also at JEVIFY_CONCURRENCY=4. 1,000 worked in 2.5 seconds. The user burns 15
seconds per failure to discover the ceiling.

3,267 is an arithmetic limit, W times floor(W/3) at W=99. It is what the request shapes allow,
not what the endpoint serves. The documents present it as capacity.

Measure the real ceiling. Sweep candidate counts on the keyless backend (500, 750, 1000, 1250,
1500, 2000, 3000), several runs each, at the default concurrency and at 1 and 2, recording for
every attempt: HTTP status, wall time, requests, and whether a retry succeeded. Do the same on
TypeSafe so the two are comparable. Find where the failures start, whether they are rate limits
that a lower concurrency survives, and whether the failure is honest (exit 4 with a usable
message) or a long silence.

Then fix the claim and the behaviour:
- README, docs/guide/, ROBOT_MODE and the capability strings state the measured practical
  ceiling per backend next to the arithmetic limit, and say which is which.
- If a lower concurrency or a small delay raises the ceiling materially, make that the keyless
  default and say so.
- The error a user meets at the ceiling must name the ceiling and the next move. Check what
  HTTP 429 and 502 currently produce and whether the message tells the user to narrow the list.

Write set: evals/capacity/**, benchmarks/results.md, README.md, docs/guide/*.md,
docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, src/cmd/agent.rs (capability strings), src/jev/client.rs only if the default
concurrency or retry changes and the measurement supports it.
Done when: the measured ceiling exists for both backends with the sweep recorded; no document
presents 3,267 as capacity without the measured number beside it; a user who exceeds it gets an
error naming the limit; the gate passes. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
notes:
Lead restriction for parallel work: your write set for this pass is evals/capacity/** and benchmarks/results.md ONLY. Do the measurement and write the section. Do NOT edit README.md, docs/ or src/cmd/agent.rs: another worker holds them. Instead, end your report with the exact replacement text for each document sentence that states a capacity, naming file and line, and the lead will apply it.
Lead applied the replacement text to README.md, docs/guide/{verbs,kinds,how-it-works}.md, plugins/jevify/skills/jevify/SKILL.md and the Unavailable hint in src/exit.rs (commit a2aed4d). Still to apply when the current worker releases them: docs/ROBOT_MODE.md:172 and the 'measured' key in src/cmd/agent.rs selection_limits.
close_reason: Measured and applied. The advertised capacity is honest: 151 attempts across both backends, every one at or below the limit answered, 3,267 keyless in 6.3 s and 13,200 on TypeSafe in 3.5 s. The live 429/502 was the per-IP quota window (3,000/min, 20,000/day in classifications; a full marker spends 68, about 294 a day), which no document mentioned and all now do. The unavailable hint no longer blames concurrency.

title: branch prefix: origin/ also matches a local branch named origin/x; match remotes only, state the two forms once
description:
Outcome: a prefixed branch marker (`origin/@{branch:…}`) matches remote refs only, and the two forms of the marker are stated once, in one place, with the rule for choosing between them.

Context (review round 9, synthesis section 1, P2, raised by all four reviewers; keep the two forms, per section 4: no one spelling satisfies both `git switch` and `git log`, src/source.rs:684-689). The bug: the prefixed form at src/source.rs:725-731 strips `refs/heads/` or `refs/remotes/` from every ref before matching the literal prefix, so `origin/` also matches a local branch named `origin/x` (`refs/heads/origin/x`), and the argument `origin/x` then resolves to the remote ref, not the local branch the listing showed. The unprefixed form (source.rs:756-767) folds remotes into locals and is unaffected. Docs: docs/guide/kinds.md:27 and :44-52 explain the two forms twice in different words; the caller must know git's DWIM rule to pick one.

Fix: with a literal prefix, match `refs/remotes/<prefix>…` only (a prefix that names no remote lists nothing, exit 3 or 6 with a hint naming the remotes that exist); state the rule once in kinds.md (bare marker for a command that takes a branch name, prefixed marker for one that takes a revision) and point the other place at it.

Files (write set): src/source.rs, the branch tests (tests/*.rs and source.rs unit tests that build a repository with a local `origin/x`), docs/guide/kinds.md, CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased). Everything else read-only.

Done when: a test repository with local branch `origin/x` and remote ref `refs/remotes/origin/y` lists only `y` under `origin/@{branch:…}` and both `origin/x` and `y` under the bare marker; an unknown prefix fails with the hint; kinds.md states the rule in one place. Gate before handing back (AGENTS.md, sandbox disabled): cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs <changed files>. Never weaken a test to pass. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
close_reason: The prefixed branch marker strips only refs/remotes/, so a local branch named origin/x stays out of the prefixed listing; an empty prefixed match is lister_failed naming the remotes; kinds.md states the rule once; verified live on a scratch clone

title: Build the source-held-out set and its runner (first half of next step 2)
description:
First half of hunch-e4j: build the source-held-out set and its runner, so the three measurement
days can start. This bead does NOT run the three days and does not read meta.decision; it only
builds and adjudicates cases and writes the runner. That is why it does not wait on hunch-ob0.

Outcome: evals/holdout/ holds at least 20 cases per verb touched by 0.9.x -- filter, why, pick,
route, fill -- drawn from sources used nowhere else in evals/ or benchmarks/, with gold labels
and the adjudication recorded; scripts/holdout_run.py runs one backend over the set and writes
one JSONL run file plus a summary.

Source-held-out is the point. Read evals/validation/README.md, evals/why/corpus.jsonl,
evals/fill/finals/ and benchmarks/results.md first and list every repository, log, crash and
PATH they already use. Your cases must come from none of them. Pin every external source by
commit sha in the case record, as evals/fill/finals does. Prefer sources you can pin and re-read:
public repositories at a fixed sha, panics you produce yourself from a pinned crate, a synthetic
PATH you build in a temp directory.

Gold: two independent passes as evals/validation/README.md describes -- label once, label again
from the case alone without looking at the first pass, then adjudicate the disagreements and
record the adjudication with its reason. Keep gold out of the runner's input, as the validation
set does. A case whose right answer is "abstain" is a case; include them deliberately.

The runner: scripts/holdout_run.py, in the style of scripts/validation_run.py. It takes the
backend, sets JEVIFY_NO_CACHE=1, records per case the exit code, the answer, the wall time, and
from the envelope the answering model, and counts 402 and 502 responses. It must not read gold.
A second script or a --score flag scores a run file against gold and reports, separately:
coverage, accuracy on decided cases, abstention correctness, and false actions.

Write set (nothing else): evals/holdout/**, scripts/holdout_run.py, scripts/holdout_score.py.
Do not touch src/, benchmarks/results.md or any other eval directory.

Done when: the set exists with its counts per verb, every source is pinned and demonstrably
absent from the other eval sets (say how you checked), the adjudication is recorded, and both
scripts run end to end on a 5-case smoke subset against the keyless backend. Report the smoke
numbers; do not draw conclusions from them.
Gate before handing back (AGENTS.md, sandbox disabled): ubs <changed files>;
cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1. Never weaken a test. Workers never commit; the lead
commits and closes.
close_reason: 103 source-held-out cases (fill 21, pick 20, why 22, filter 20, route 20) from three pinned repositories, 22 locally produced failure logs and three tool inventories; absence from every other eval set checked and recorded. Gold apart from the run manifest, both passes kept, eight adjudications with their ground. Caveat stated in the set: both passes are one reader, not two annotators. Runner and scorer smoke-tested on 5 keyless cases, 0 402s, all answered by jev-1.13.0. ubs and the full suite pass.

title: Paired pilot: enforce isolation and measure cost per pair
description:
Outcome: a paired agent run whose isolation a reader can verify, and a per-pair cost figure.

Context: the pilot of hunch-evl (benchmarks/agents/PILOT.md, 2026-09-22) met every other criterion but two. Isolation held by construction, not by the harness: the arms were told to stay read-only and one without-jevify run still wrote scratch files, and the 2026-09-20 canaries were not run. Cost was measured per arm, not per pair, and two of the six jevify calls were cache hits, so the with-arm backend cost is understated.

- Enforce isolation instead of asking for it: a per-run working directory the arm cannot leave, a fresh cache directory per run (JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR), the canaries of 2026-09-20 run and reported, and a check after each run that names any file written outside its directory.

title: Decide the execution policy for user-written commands with resolved operands
description:
Owner decision needed. The governing plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md, Constraints and decisions; Task R3) keeps unvalidated command grammar a proposal, and `run` executes only zero-argument true, false, pwd, ls, even with --yes. The semantic-operand wrapper wants to execute a user-written command after grevi substituted a handle.

Argument for a separate, wider policy: in `run` the model chooses the tool and the flags; in the wrapper the user wrote both and the model only chose among existing handles of a declared domain. The residual risk is a wrong handle inside a command with a large effect (rm, mv, kill, git reset), chosen on path-name and excerpt evidence, which R4 calls incomplete evidence for a whole-file action.

Proposed policy to accept, amend or reject: (1) the never-execute list applies to the head command and the proposal is printed only; (2) on a terminal the resolved command and p are shown and the default answer is no; `--yes` skips the question; (3) machine mode needs `--exec --yes`, the child's stdout goes to stderr, child failure is exit 7; (4) no execution when any handle sits within 0.06 of the threshold (the measured jitter); (5) the spec and AGENTS.md principles state the user-written-grammar distinction in one sentence. If accepted: fixtures first (wrong-handle, leading-dash name, declined, never-execute head, no TTY), then the code.
notes: Decided per docs/VISION.md (hunch-vq2): fill prints by default and --run executes. jevify keeps no effect classes, action floors or escalating-flag tables; the caller's permission system decides what may run. Abstention (exit 3) and the margin check are the only guards jevify owns.
close_reason: Superseded by docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md (epic hunch-7zg), section 9.2: the owner decided that fill becomes the command through exec and that the caller's permission system decides what may run.

title: Post-release: update the local install and evaluate jevify on real agent tasks
description:
Outcome: After the 0.7.0 release is published, the local jevify install is updated to it, and jevify is evaluated on real agent tasks: how agents pick it up next to other CLI tools, and how `fill`, `is`, `filter`, `why`, `pick`, `label` and the kinds behave in practice. Done by the lead, not a worker. This bead is no child of the epic hunch-7zg: the epic closes when its children close, and this bead starts after the release bead hunch-7zg.21.
Context: Owner request of 2026-09-21. Plan section "After the language is stable"; every item of that section is an acceptance criterion below. Use Jev itself as a judge for extra feedback: `jevify is` and `jevify label` over agent transcripts (for example "the agent used fill where a listing was needed", "the agent read a long output that filter or why would have reduced"). Agents under test get only the skill or the `jevify init agents` block, never hints in the task. The older evaluation beads (hunch-ric, hunch-3te, hunch-s18, hunch-evl) target the endpoint set of 0.4.0; reuse their task families and gold where a verb survives (`pick`, `why`, `is`, `route`), and file what is missing for the new verbs as new beads here.
Files: no repository source file. Findings go into new beads (one per defect) and into a report outside the repository or under evals/ if the owner asks.
Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.21 (the 0.7.0 release bead).
Done when:
- `jevify --version` on this machine prints the released version.
- A local invocation log exists: every jevify call of the evaluation with its verb, flags, exit code, record and request counts, elapsed time and model, kept on this machine (never in the repository), and the report is computed from it.
- A held-out set per verb and per kind exists (`fill` per kind `-`, `branch`, `commit`, `file`, `dir`, `tool`, one recipe kind, `one`, `flag`; `pick`, `pick --from`, `why`, `filter`, `label`, `is`, `route`), labelled by someone other than the author of the verb, and the report gives the result per set.
- Recall of `filter` at the unsure boundary is measured: over the held-out set, how many true records fall in the unsure band, how many are lost under `--strict`, and the recall with and without it.
- How often the right candidate misses the finalists of its window is measured, for n = 3, 2 and 1 finalists per window (the pool rule of plan §2.1), on lists above one window.
- A set of real agent tasks (git, gh, cargo, logs, files, kubectl/docker if present) has run with and without jevify available; per task: did the agent reach for jevify, which verb, exit codes, turns and tokens saved or lost, wrong picks, misquoted markers, abstentions.
- Jev as a judge: `jevify is` and `jevify label` labels over the transcripts, with the statements used, and a spot check of those labels by hand.
- A short report with the defects filed as beads. Live runs that could not happen are reported as NOT RUN.
notes:
2026-09-21 live note from the 0.6.0 acceptance: fill -- git switch '@{branch:the release automation work}' resolved to wt/bead-06 at 0.55 (next 0.18, none 0.13) on classifier.dev; the ratio guard passed it. Measure branch evidence quality (tip subject only in tier one) and the ratio factor.
From hunch-con (2026-09-22): the file kind resolves name-like phrases but abstains on content phrases even with round-two excerpts (stages hunks -> add.rs: round 2 NONE 0.73 vs best 0.19; the recipe engine -> source.rs: NONE 0.48 vs best 0.27, jev-1.13.0). Evaluate whether content phrases for file matter on real agent tasks and what evidence would carry them.
2026-09-22 evaluation run (subagent for the lead). jevify --version: 0.7.0. Model: jev-1.13.0 (TypeSafe, key). Invocation log: 367 calls in a local scratch directory, outside the repo. The evaluator wrote all gold labels; why reuses evals/why gold (20) plus 3 fresh logs.
Held-out sets (correct / correct abstain / abstain / wrong): fill '-' 9/1/0/0 of 10; branch 10/2/0/0 of 12 (release automation gives wt/bead-16 at 0.71, next 0.26); commit 10/2/0/0 of 12 (testify 409 = 3 windows); file 8/1/2/1 of 12 (name phrases 7/7, content phrases 1/4); dir 6/1/3/0 of 10 (all abstentions are content descriptions); tool 6/1/0/1 of 8 (only via env, argv[0] refused); recipe ci-run 5/1/0/0 of 6; one 12/12; flag 12/12; pick 8/2/1/0 of 11; pick --from 8/1/1/0 of 10; why hit@1 18/23, hit@3 19/23, 2 abstain; is 14/14 statements, 7/7 exits; route 15/3/0/1 of 19; label 29/30 (1 unsure) and 35/44 (6 unsure, 3 wrong).
filter at the unsure boundary: 22 true records over 5 statements; 20 yes, 2 unsure; recall 1.00 default, 0.91 --strict (both losses in one terse statement over test names). The unsure band held 12 records, 2 true.
Finalist miss (proxy: gold's own W=200 window ranked alone, the same content as round one): gold ranked 1st in 36/36 windows (3 lists above one window: 409, 2834, 209), so the miss rate is 0/36 at n=3, 2 and 1. End to end 30/36: all 6 losses in round two against a sibling (docs page for an example file, a same-named file, a cassette; one where the rival fits better than the gold). NOT RUN: exact finalist sets for coded kinds (no hook exposes round-one ranks).
Agent tasks (haiku, 8 tasks, with the init agents block vs without): 8/8 correct in both arms; jevify used in 1/8 (why, T4, exit 0, and the agent still read the whole log); 0 fill/pick/filter/label/is/route calls, 0 misquoted markers, 0 abstentions. Hand check: called-jevify 14 right, 2 unsure; non-zero exit 16/16; listed-and-chose 15 right, 1 unsure; read-long-output 5 right, 2 wrong, 9 unsure (statement too vague). label over 134 commands: 30 unsure; hand sample 15/20 right, 5 unsure, 0 wrong.

NOT RUN: kubectl/docker tasks (no cluster or daemon); pod, container, process and issue kinds; the keyless backend; add and sort.
Beads filed: hunch-cpo (P1, CI fails on release tags), hunch-0pq (P1, agents barely use jevify from the init block), hunch-wxm (P2, argv[0] tool marker refused), hunch-6jv (P2, dir kind lacks content evidence), hunch-b25 (P3, ambiguous status hides NONE; empty no_match field), hunch-wx9 (P3, why and pick print no count line).
After release 0.8.0: re-run the 8 agent tasks with the new init agents block (hunch-0pq: situation -> complete command) and compare adoption with the 1/8 baseline; re-measure the fill-dir and pick-from-dir held-out sets after hunch-6jv (dir children as tier two).

Agent tasks (same 8 tasks, haiku, with the 0.8.0 `init agents` block vs without): adoption 5/8 (T1 fill --dry-run branch, T3 why, T4 why, T7 label --files, T8 route) vs 1/8 at 0.7.0; not used in T2 (commit found by git log --grep), T5 (file by content: find/ls), T6 (test names: grep). Correct 8/8 in both arms (T6 both arms list the 7 gold throttling tests plus extras: 11 with, 5 without). jevify exit codes 0 for all 7 agent calls; 0 abstentions; 0 misquoted markers. Wrong picks: why's top cause was wrong in both uses (T3: cargo-deny toolchain error from a job that succeeded, p 0.86; T4: an expected WARN line 264, p 0.45, instead of the DATA RACE at 155/239); fill, label and route picks were right. Turns with/without: T1 12/17, T2 16/11, T3 35/21, T4 14/8, T5 11/17, T6 78/74, T7 13/18, T8 11/8; input tokens 6.9M with vs 8.4M without (T6 dominates: 3.1M vs 5.3M). After why the agents still read the log (T4 had Read the whole log before calling why; T3 read tail -100 and grep after a wrong cause). T1's fill dry-run picked origin/ticket/TPE-791, a ref git switch refuses (hunch-emc); its status line says exec although nothing ran (hunch-r2t).
Held-out re-measurement (correct / correct abstain / abstain / wrong): fill dir 9/1/0/0 of 10 (0.7.0: 6/1/3/0; the three content descriptions now resolve: evals/why 1.00, plugins/jevify/skills/jevify 0.61, testify-app/Testify/Services 0.99). pick --from 8/1/1/0 of 10 (unchanged; dir 'the test helpers with the fake Jev server' still no_match, closest tests/common 0.32 vs none 0.40; 'the shared test helpers' resolves to tests/common 0.84). fill file 7/1/2/2 of 12 (0.7.0: 8/1/2/1): name phrases 7/7; content phrases 0/4 (was 1/4): stages hunks -> src/gitdiff.rs 0.94 (wrong), splits input into records -> src/input.rs 0.70 (wrong, was records.rs 0.99), recipe engine and retry/backoff abstain with the gold as closest.
NOT RUN at 0.8.0 (unchanged verbs, results of the 0.7.0 run stand): filter unsure-boundary recall, finalist-miss, why/is/route/label sets, Jev-as-judge over the new transcripts, kubectl/docker tasks, pod/container/process/issue kinds, keyless backend, add and sort.
Beads filed: hunch-emc (P2, fill branch gives origin/<name> to git switch), hunch-r2t (P3, --dry-run status says exec), hunch-s2k (P2, why picks error-looking lines from passing steps over the failing test on two real logs), hunch-u7s (P2, file content phrases give confident wrong siblings).

Agent adoption with the init agents block 5/8 (was 1/8), correctness 8/8 both arms; fill dir held-out 9/10 (was 6/10) after child names as tier two; pick --from unchanged 8/10; file content phrases 0/4 with two confident wrong picks; why top cause wrong on both real CI logs. title: why points at the panic header instead of the line that explains the failure
description:
Found by the hunch-evl paired pilot (jevify 0.8.3, jev-1.13.0, TypeSafe, 2026-09-22).

`why` points at the header of a Rust test panic instead of the line that says what went wrong.

On the failing CI run of the v0.7.0 tag (run 35736209634, the log of the failed job, 300+ lines),
`why --json` returns line 185 at p 0.39:

    thread 'documented_input_side_shell_examples_run_against_the_binary' (3856)
        panicked at tests/agent.rs:64:17:

The explanation is four lines later, at 189:

    jevify fill: not run: arg 3 branch: no_match; ; candidates 0 of 0, omitted 0;
        model not requested

The header names the test and the source position; it does not say why the test failed. An agent
that reads the cause `why` prints and stops there quotes the header. In the pilot the arm with
jevify answered T3 with line 185 and the arm without it, reading the log itself, answered with
line 189. That is the one task of eight where the with arm gave the weaker answer.

Both lines are candidates and both are error-like; the one that carries the message a reader needs
scores lower. p 0.39 is itself close to the 0.5 threshold and only passes because the Noul agrees
over round one. Milder than hunch-s2k (closed), which was about lines from steps that passed: here
the pointed line belongs to the real failure but carries no information.

Expected: on a panic block, `why` points at the assertion or message line, not at the `panicked at`
header; or the printed context makes the message impossible to miss. Re-measure with the run above
and with the cargo logs of evals/why.

Suggested write set: src/cmd/why.rs (candidate selection and the nearest-failure context), the why
contract tests, evals/why if a case is added.
close_reason: The finals carry a finalist's whole panic block and their prompt asks for the message line, not the panicked-at header; round one unchanged. Validation why cases 0.80 -> 0.89 accuracy with one false answer fewer; corpus hit@3 20/21 and hit@1 18/21 live (the one flip is model drift against a cached figure, reproduced with the old prompt)

title: Beads export publishes the local checkout path in source_repo_path
description: Every line of .beads/issues.jsonl carries source_repo_path with the absolute path of the local checkout, and the repository is public. About 44 lines are already published. Find whether br can omit or relativize the field at export (config or flag); otherwise decide whether the tracker export belongs in the public repository. Do not rewrite history. Gate: a new export holds no absolute local path, and the push scan of AGENTS.md passes without an exception.
notes:
Lead decision N2 (review round 8, 2026-09-22): P1, resolved before any further beads push. The leak grew from about 44 to about 96 '/Users/' lines in HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl; every beads commit publishes it again, and gitleaks does not flag it, so the AGENTS.md push scan misses it. Worker: check 'br config' (today it lists only issue_prefix and metrics.*) and 'br sync' for a relative or suppressed source_repo_path option, and report. If no option exists, the owner decides whether .beads/issues.jsonl stays tracked in the public repository. Done when: a fresh export and the outgoing diff (git diff origin/main..HEAD) hold no absolute checkout path. Never rewrite history.
Worker report (claude-hunch-nay, 2026-09-22, br 0.5.12): no config key or export flag suppresses or relativizes source_repo_path. 'br config schema' lists no such key; 'br sync' has only --migrate-source-repo-path, which rewrites the field to the canonical ABSOLUTE workspace path (the binary rejects a non-absolute target), so it is the opposite of what we need; 'br init' has no option; no BEADS_*/BR_* env var touches the field. What exists is a per-issue override: 'br update <id> --source-repo-path ""' clears the field (the export then omits it) and 'br update <id> --source-repo-path jevify' stores a relative value; both survive later unrelated updates (verified on hunch-nay, now exported as "jevify"). 'br create' has no such flag and stamps every new issue with the absolute cwd, so any fix must be repeated after each create. Outgoing diff (git diff origin/main..HEAD) is empty; the working-tree export still holds 99 '/Users/' lines (59 jevify, 33 hunch, 7 grevi rows). Owner options, commands verbatim: (A) Bulk clear now and re-run before each beads commit: br list --json --all | jq -r '.[].id' | xargs -n1 -I{} br update {} --source-repo-path '' --json >/dev/null; br sync --flush-only; grep -c '/Users/' .beads/issues.jsonl  (expect 0; touches updated_at on every row; check 'br list --all' flag name, closed issues must be included). (B) Strip at commit time with a git clean filter, per clone, so the DB keeps the value but the repository never does: printf '.beads/issues.jsonl filter=beads-path
' >> .gitattributes; git config filter.beads-path.clean 'sed -E "s#,"source_repo_path":"/Users/[^"]*"##g"'; git config filter.beads-path.smudge cat; git add --renormalize .beads/issues.jsonl  (then add a gitleaks custom rule for '"source_repo_path":"/' in .gitleaks.toml so the push scan catches a clone without the filter). (C) Stop publishing the tracker: git rm --cached .beads/issues.jsonl .beads/beads.base.jsonl; printf '.beads/issues.jsonl
.beads/beads.base.jsonl
' >> .gitignore; commit  (history keeps the old paths either way; never rewrite). Recommendation: B plus the gitleaks rule, because A silently regresses on the next 'br create' and C loses the shared tracker. Nothing in .beads/ was staged or committed by the worker.
OWNER DECISION 2026-09-22: accept source_repo_path in the public export. The path is a local folder name, not a secret. No untracking, no strip step, no history rewrite. Close as accepted.
close_reason: Owner accepts source_repo_path in the public beads export: a local folder name, not a secret. No untracking or strip step.

title: Validate the fill finals shortcut on a held-out content-phrase set, before/after 76e723e
description:
Outcome: the `fill` finals shortcut (a decisive round-one Found skips the finals for a tier-two kind when the runner-up name is out of play) is validated on a held-out set of content-phrase cases that nobody looked at while writing the rule, with a before/after against 76e723e.

Context (review round 9, synthesis section 1, P3, raised by all four; section 4: keep, since reverting has no evidence either): the shortcut at src/cmd/fill.rs:365-373 and `runner_up_matches` at fill.rs:488-495 (`RIVAL_RATIO * field > best.p`) are tested only on hand-picked tuples taken from the runs that motivated them (fill.rs:876-895: "records.rs behind input.rs", "release.sh behind publish-crates.yml"). No before/after measurement of 76e723e exists, and the keyless `fill` calibration accuracy is 0.67 (benchmarks/results.md:111, 5 cases, one false action), so the file/dir kinds are where a confident wrong selection reaching a command costs the most (fill-val-07 at 0.88, results.md:134).

Fix: build a held-out set of at least 20 content-phrase `fill` cases over file and dir kinds in at least three repositories not used for the tuples (phrases about what a file does, not its name), gold by two annotators as in evals/validation/README.md; run both backends at 76e723e^ and HEAD with `JEVIFY_NO_CACHE=1`; record coverage, accuracy, abstentions, false actions and the request count per case. The rule stays if false actions do not rise and requests fall; otherwise file the revert.

Files (write set): evals/fill/ (new cases and gold), benchmarks/results.md (a new subsection with the date, binary versions and backends), scripts/ (an eval script if none fits). No change to src/ in this bead.

Done when: the set exists with its gold and adjudication, both runs are recorded, and results.md states the decision the numbers support. Gate before handing back (AGENTS.md, sandbox disabled): cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs <changed files>. Never weaken a test to pass. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
notes: Measured (see benchmarks/results.md, section 'The fill finals shortcut on a held-out content-phrase set'). 33 held-out cases in evals/fill/finals/ (ripgrep, fzf, bat, pinned; gold from two annotators, 1 adjudicated). head vs finals-always-on: the shortcut fires on 12 (classifier.dev) / 15 (TypeSafe) cases, saves one request per fire, and on one fire per backend selects a wrong name-decoy file the finals would have abstained on (wrapping.rs, pager.rs); one right dir (pkg/brew) is lost to a finals abstention when the finals run. vs 233e946: false actions 4->2 and 4->3, requests +3. Follow-up bead hunch-wka holds the decision; no src change here. Run rows kept under evals/out/fill-finals/ (ignored).
close_reason: Held-out set of 33 content phrases over file and dir in three pinned public repositories, gold apart with two annotators and adjudication; measured on both backends with the shortcut as shipped, as before 233e946, and removed. The rule beats the old code (false 4->2 and 4->3) but loses to the finals always on (false 1 and 2, accuracy 0.96 and 0.92) at the cost of 12 to 15 requests; recorded in results.md and the decision filed as hunch-wka
