title: why: error-looking lines from passing steps outrank the failing test on two real CI logs
description:
Outcome: `jevify why` on a real test or CI log points at the line of the failing test (the panic, the `--- FAIL`, the race report), not at an error-looking line that a passing step or a test's expected output printed. Measured on the two logs below, the top cause is within the gold lines.

Evidence (jevify 0.8.0, jev-1.13.0, 2026-09-22; agent tasks T3 and T4 of the hunch-lpp re-evaluation; a haiku agent given `jevify init agents` reached for `why` in both and had to read the log anyway):

1. Go CI log (300 lines, `go test -race`; the job fails on `--- FAIL: TestPullModelManifestListDownloadsSelectedChildOnly` with `WARNING: DATA RACE` at line 155 and `testing.go:1712: race detected during execution of test` at line 239):
```
$ jevify why --json < sets/why-task/ci.log     # the eval's copy of the log
causes[0]: line 264 p=0.45  time=... level=WARN msg="failed to parse model recommendations snapshot" path=/tmp/TestModelRecommendationsLoadSnapshotInvalidDoesNotOverwrite.../model-recommendations.json error="invalid character 'i' ..."
jevify why: 300 lines, candidates 239, windows 2
```
Line 264 is a warning that the test `TestModelRecommendationsLoadSnapshotInvalidDoesNotOverwrite` provokes on purpose; that test passes. The race report (lines 155-239) is not among the causes.

2. GitHub Actions log of run 35736209634 (jevify, tag v0.7.0; job `test (ubuntu-latest)` failed on `documented_input_side_shell_examples_run_against_the_binary`, cargo-deny succeeded):
```
$ gh run view 35736209634 --log | jevify why --json          # 2611 lines, 14 windows, 15 requests
causes[0]: line 248 p=0.86  cargo-deny  Run EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2  error: override toolchain '1.93.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl' is not installed ...
$ gh run view 35736209634 --log-failed | jevify why --json   # 199 lines, 2 requests
causes[0]: line 143 p=0.81  test (ubuntu-latest)  Run cargo test ...  jevify: output error: permission denied
```
Line 248 belongs to a job that succeeded (`gh run view 35736209634 --json jobs`: cargo-deny success). Line 143 is stderr that a passing test expects. The panic is at line 185 of the `--log-failed` output and the explaining line (`jevify fill: not run: arg 3 branch: no_match; ...`) at 188; neither is a cause.

The pattern: lines with `error:`/`WARN` outrank the lines that state the failure (`panicked at`, `--- FAIL`, `race detected`, `test result: FAILED`). Both logs are kept under the eval directory named in hunch-lpp's notes (r2/results/t3-log-failed.txt and sets/why-task/ci.log) for a regression case.

Fix direction: add both logs to evals/why with gold lines; check what the why prompt asks (a cause versus an error line) and whether the window ranking favours the earliest loud line; consider the failure markers (`panicked at`, `--- FAIL`, `FAILED`, `race detected`) as tier-two evidence for the finalists so that the model sees the test outcome next to the candidate line. No new threshold.

Done when: both logs are in evals/why and why hits the gold at rank 1 on jev-1.13.0 (or the report states the round scores and why); the earlier 23-case set keeps hit@1 18/23 or better; the quality gate passes.
notes:
Lead: CHANGELOG.md is the lead's; report a one-line Unreleased entry in the final message instead of editing it. Parallel workers: hunch-s2k (src/cmd/why.rs and its tests), hunch-emc (src/source.rs branch handle, tests/fill.rs, docs/guide/kinds.md), hunch-r2t (the dry-run stderr line, likely src/lib.rs or src/cmd/fill.rs). If your fix needs a file in another worker's set, coordinate through Agent Mail and wait for its release.
Lead: evals/why/go-05.log and go-05.expect duplicate go-04 and are left untracked, not committed (no rm allowed); an owner may delete them.
close_reason: why finals carry the nearest failure statement, prompt excludes passing steps' loud lines, any = max over rounds; two real CI logs in evals/why; live 19/22 hit@1 (pre-existing 17/20 vs 14/20 before); gate green

title: The documents state how much the answer varies between runs and orders
description:
Two live trials on 2026-09-23 measured run-to-run and order-to-order variation that no document
mentions. A harness author found it in production conditions; a hostile reviewer quantified it.

1. Candidate order changes the answer. The same four lines shuffled, 28 runs: the right file 20
   times (p 0.37 to 0.84), a wrong file 7 times (p 0.35 to 0.63), abstain once. A 25 percent flip
   rate on byte-identical content. Across 7 cases and 8 shuffles, 13 answers degraded and all 13
   went to abstain rather than to a wrong answer. Order comes from whatever produced the pipe:
   `git branch`, `ls`, a find.
2. Cold runs disagree. Five identical `filter --strict` runs with the cache off over 200 records
   kept 48, 55 and 52; union 55, intersection 48. 30 of 166 records changed verdict across the
   five runs. Raising the threshold does not remove it: 3 of 27 unstable at 0.8, 5 of 18 at 0.95.
   The seven-day answer cache hides it, so it bites only when two workers race the same query
   cold, which is exactly a CI fleet.
3. Within one call, batch position matters: 500 records from 6 distinct texts through `label`
   gave the same text `feature` 84 times and `unsure` 10, then 81 and 13, then 79 and 15.

None of this is a bug to fix in this bead, and the direction of failure is honest. But a harness
author who learns it in production learns it the expensive way, and VISION's promise is that the
tool is honest about what it does not know. Variance is part of that.

Do two things.

A. Measure it properly, so the numbers in the documents are ours and not a reviewer's. Use
   evals/holdout and evals/validation. Per backend: rerun a fixed subset cold five times and
   report the per-record verdict flip rate and the kept-set union and intersection; shuffle the
   candidate order of a fixed subset eight times and report how often the answer changes, split
   into changed-to-abstain and changed-to-wrong. Report by verb.

B. Write it down where it is needed, not everywhere. docs/guide/how-it-works.md gets the numbers
   and the reason. ROBOT_MODE gets one paragraph for harness authors: what varies, by how much,
   which direction failures take, and that the answer cache masks it. The `meta.decision` note
   should say the gate scores do not bound this error, since the contract already says no
   calibration is claimed and a reader may take the scores for confidence.

Write set: evals/variance/**, benchmarks/results.md, docs/guide/how-it-works.md,
docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, src/cmd/agent.rs (capability strings only).
Done when: the variance is measured per verb and per backend with the method stated; the two
documents carry the numbers; the gate passes. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
notes:
Lead restriction for parallel work: your write set for this pass is evals/variance/** ONLY, and write your section to evals/variance/FINDING.md rather than benchmarks/results.md, which another worker holds. Do NOT edit docs/ or src/cmd/agent.rs. End your report with the exact text you want added to docs/guide/how-it-works.md and docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, and the lead will apply it.
Lead applied section A to docs/guide/how-it-works.md (commit below). Sections B and C for docs/ROBOT_MODE.md are still to apply: another worker holds that file. Text is in this bead's worker report.
close_reason: Measured and applied. Five cold reruns move 1.6 percent of answers and disagree on 5 of 86 questions; eight candidate orders move 5.0 percent and disagree on 15 of 58. 86 percent of degradations become abstentions; the 2 confident wrong answers were the same question under the same shuffle on both backends, so order sensitivity is in how the list is put to the model. how-it-works carries the table and the method, ROBOT_MODE the harness paragraph and the meta.decision caveat.

title: 1.8 Contract: the skill teaches the 0.5.0 language
description:
Plan bead: 1.8 contract, the skill half (the documents half is hunch-7zg.8). Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: the skill teaches a Claude agent the language of 0.5.0: the situations that call for the output verbs, the habits, the recovery, the permissions. It teaches `jevify run`, `why -- CMD`, a shell loop over `is` and `"$(… | jevify pick …)"` today; the language replaces all four.

Context: plan §6 "Skill, for a Claude agent" and its first paragraph, vision "Where an answer is worth having". Decisions, final:
- Order for 0.5.0: the two sides (output side only), the verbs, the exit codes. The marker joins in bead 2.5 (hunch-7zg.13), where the order becomes: the two sides, the verbs, the marker, the exit codes. The skill names no verb, flag or kind that release 0.5.0 lacks: in this bead that means `why`, `pick`, `filter`, `is`, `route`, `add`, `sort`; NOT `fill`, NOT `label`, NOT `pick --from`, no marker. Bead 4.2 (hunch-7zg.20) adds label.
- Triggers for 0.5.0: a failed build over about 50 lines -> `2>&1 | jevify why`; many records, one question -> `filter`; many files, one question -> `fd -0 | jevify filter -0 --files`; one file out of many by content -> `git ls-files | jevify pick --files '…'`; the next step depends on a fact -> `is … &&`; waiting for a state -> `until … | jevify is '…'`; the long tail of a large PATH -> `route`, which only prints.
- Habits: one jevify process per question, never a loop that starts one per record; cheap tools first (grep, jq, head); yes means act; never `"$(jevify pick …)"` as an argument, because an abstention becomes an empty argument; under `git bisect run`, map exit 3 to 125. `filter -v` inverts, as `grep -v`; verbosity is `--verbose`. `is` with one statement prints nothing; read the exit code.
- Recovery: exit 2 -> copy the corrected argument; `too_many` -> grep or head; exit 4 -> the quota ("daily quota of the free backend reached") or the model, read the line.
- Permissions: allow the output verbs freely.
- The saved input (`why`, `filter`) holds the raw input, secrets included; the skill says so. `--files` withholds the excerpt of hidden files and of files that look like secrets, and says `excerpts withheld: N`.
- The frontmatter description keeps the "use when / do not use" form and drops `run` as an executor.

Files (write set): plugins/jevify/skills/jevify/SKILL.md, plugins/jevify/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (descriptions only; they carry no version). Everything else is read-only; README, docs/, AGENTS.md and src/cmd/agent.rs belong to hunch-7zg.8.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.5 (route), hunch-bx6 (filter), hunch-7zg.6 (is), hunch-7zg.7 (pick and why): a contract bead waits for the behaviour it documents, so every status line it quotes exists on main. Copy status lines from the binary, not from the plan.

Done when:
- Every command line in the skill runs against the binary built from main (`--help` or a FakeJev run); an anchored grep over the three files finds none of: `jevify run`, `why -- `, `jevify fill`, `jevify label`, `@\{[a-z-]+:`, `pick --from`, `route --yes`, `jevify -v`.
- The text is present tense, with no meta and no retrospective language; both JSON manifests still parse (`jq . <file>`).
- The gate below passes (the documents do not change it; the worker's part of it proves the tree is green when the work is handed to the lead).

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
- The `ubs` gate when the changed files are only Markdown or JSON: run `ubs <changed files>`; when it reports that nothing was scanned, record "ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned" in the bead and validate every JSON file with `jq .`. That is a pass. Any file ubs does scan (Rust, shell, Python) must still exit 0.
notes: Worker implementation complete in the three permitted paths. PASSED: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked --no-deps. ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned (exit 3); both manifests pass jq. Twelve shell examples and inline forms pass binary --help checks; forbidden grammar scan has zero matches; Ruby Psych validates frontmatter. Full test and --lib attempts are sandbox-blocked by non-UTF-8 fixture creation: Operation not permitted (os error 1). Supplemental run excludes only that blocked fixture: all remaining 82 unit tests pass, then wiremock fails to bind an OS port (PermissionDenied). Full integration and live tests are NOT RUN. No test source changed. Skill quick_validate cannot start because Python yaml is absent; Psych validation passes instead. Excerpts-withheld status confirmed from binary; quota wording verified in source and passing client unit test, not a live quota response. Agent Mail registration and exact reservations succeeded, but message authentication was rejected by automatic approval review; unauthenticated posting also fails. No independent scratch files created; test fixtures and UBS scratch are retained. Lead must run unsandboxed full gate, commit, push, and close.
close_reason: Skill and plugin manifests teach the 0.5.0 language. ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned (Markdown and JSON). Lead gate outside the sandbox: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full cargo test --locked (18 suites pass, 4 live tests NOT RUN); JSON files validate with jq; anchored greps find no removed or future form.

title: Secret, private-info and PII audit before release
description:
Outcome: Before v0 is tagged and released, the public repo `tpellet/hunch` is audited end to end for secrets, private information and PII: a full-history gitleaks scan, a manual review of every tracked file and of the commit history, a check that no launch draft lives in the repo, a check that the release config and the locally built installer carry no local paths, and a check that user-facing docs use the generic key path and no personal tooling details. Fix-forward findings are fixed in this bead; anything that would need a history rewrite or a key rotation is recorded, never rewritten, and blocks v0 acceptance pending Thomas. The verdict is a short pass/fail note in the close reason with no secret value quoted. Lead-added (Thomas, 2026-09-19: "before the push to public remote we check for any secret/any private information and PII that should not be shared"); the lead's own audit of the pre-code history (2026-09-19) found SECRET 0, and the lead's authorized history rewrite of 2026-09-19 removed the low PRIVATE items, so the pre-code baseline is clean (17 commits at 5ed92d6).

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md ("## Public Repositories — Push With Care") and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints" and "### Task 16: Release — binaries, launch checklist (Homebrew tap and Show HN optional, user-gated)" Step 2b; `.gitleaks.toml` (hunch-task-01-scaffold-p8n); README.md, PRIVACY.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/results.md as shipped.

Context:
- Scope: everything reachable from `git log --all` plus every tracked file at HEAD (`git ls-files`), including `.beads/issues.jsonl` (descriptions, notes, close reasons), `evals/` (inventory, eval outputs, prototype files), `benchmarks/` (results, fixtures), `docs/`, the dist config and `.github/workflows/`. Ignored local files (`.beads/beads.db*`, `evals/out/`, `target/`) are not published and are out of scope, but confirm they are still ignored (`git status --ignored | head`).
- Step 1, scanners (outside the sandbox): `gitleaks version` (8.30.1 installed; `brew install gitleaks` if missing); `gitleaks git . --log-opts="--all" --redact -v --report-path "$TMPDIR/gl-git.json"` and `gitleaks dir . --redact -v --report-path "$TMPDIR/gl-dir.json"`; both must print "no leaks found". A finding that is a real credential value: record the file, commit and rule id only (never the value), do not fix by rewriting, go to Step 6.
- Step 2, manual pattern sweep over `git log --all -p` (read the matches, do not trust counts): `git log --all -p | grep -n -i -E "authorization:|bearer |sk-[a-z0-9]|ghp_|github_pat_|api[_-]?key=|token=|/Users/|/private/tmp/|/home/|claude\.ai/code/session|@gmail\.com|@[a-z0-9-]+\.(com|ai|io)"`; every hit is classified BENIGN (placeholder such as `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=test-key`, the commit author's own email in doc text, a public URL), PRIVATE (a local path, a session URL, a private repo or project name, personal tooling) or SECRET (a value). The commit author identity (name and email) on commits is Thomas's chosen public identity: BENIGN. Absolute paths inside internal files — bead descriptions, notes and close reasons, the plan, AGENTS.md (the checkout /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch, the launch folder /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch-launch/, the skill paths under /Users/tpellet/.claude/skills/) — are instructions: classify BENIGN-internal, no action. Only user-facing docs, code, benchmarks/, eval outputs and release artifacts must be free of them.
- Step 3, tracked-file review, one file at a time, by eye: README.md, PRIVACY.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/README.md, benchmarks/results.md, evals/inventory.json (tool names from this machine are a light fingerprint: BENIGN, keep), evals/prototype/*, docs/superpowers/**, AGENTS.md, `.beads/issues.jsonl` (every `notes` and `close_reason`: no pasted API response, no draft sentence, no value), and every commit message body (`git log --format='%H%n%B' origin/main`). User-facing files (README.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, PRIVACY.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/) must name the key path generically, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key`, and describe the machine as "a typical macOS dev machine" (CPU/OS line allowed), and must carry no personal tooling details: no vault note titles, no `digital-double`/skill names, no reviewer model names, no per-machine tool counts such as "Thomas's Mac: 1,869 tools", no `~/.claude/` paths. Internal files (AGENTS.md, the plan, beads) may keep the real key path `$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key` and the tooling names. `grep -rn -E "typesafe-ai-key|Thomas's Mac|1,869|digital-double|\.claude/|Opus|Kimi" README.md PRIVACY.md docs/ROBOT_MODE.md CHANGELOG.md benchmarks/` must be empty (recursive: `bench.sh` and the fixtures are user-facing too).
- Step 4, launch drafts: `git ls-files | grep -i -E "launch|tweet|show-hn|announce"` must be empty and `ls docs/launch` must fail; `grep -n -i -E "show hn|tweet" .beads/issues.jsonl` may match only bead titles and the words of the rules (no draft sentence). Drafts live only in /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch-launch/ (never listed, never read into the repo).
- Step 5, release surface: read the dist config (`dist-workspace.toml` or `[workspace.metadata.dist]`) and `.github/workflows/release.yml`; then build the installer locally without tagging, `dist build --artifacts=global` (or `dist build`; verify the flag against `dist build --help`), and `grep -n -E "/Users/|/private/tmp/|/home/[a-z]" target/distrib/*installer*.sh` must be empty; the only host in the script is github.com and the only `tpellet` is the repo path. Do not tag, do not push a tag.
- Step 6, findings. Fix-forward class (a local path or personal detail in a tracked file at HEAD, a stray private note in a bead field): fix it in this bead: each finding is its own fix-forward commit `fix: <what> (hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha)` (keep `<what>` ≤ 22 characters) staging the fixed file and `.beads/issues.jsonl` carrying the tracker note (`br update hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "fixed forward: <file>, <class>"`, `br sync --flush-only`, no value), gated as usual and pushed after the pre-push scan; the close reason repeats "fixed forward: <file>, <class>" with the commit SHA. Rewrite/rotation class (a credential value anywhere in history, a private third-party detail in an old commit): do not rewrite, do not force-push, do not delete a tag; record "<class>, <file>, <commit>" in the close reason and with `br update hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2 --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "NOT ACCEPTED pending Thomas: <class, file, commit; no value>"`, `br sync --flush-only`, and leave THIS bead open so acceptance stays blocked; report it first in the hand-off. The lead's authorized history rewrite of 2026-09-19 removed the session trailers, the scratch path and an email line; the pre-code baseline is clean (17 commits at 5ed92d6), so any such item found now is a new finding.
- Step 7, close only after every step ran: the close reason is the pass/fail note: scanner results (commits scanned, leaks found), pattern-sweep classes with counts, files reviewed, launch-draft check, installer check, user-facing docs check, fix-forward commits (SHAs), and "no rewrite/rotation finding" or the blocking record.
- Rules (every bead): strictly serial on `main`, no branches/worktrees/PRs; gate and git with the sandbox disabled; never delete files; never read, print or copy ~/.ssh; treat unexplained working-tree changes as another agent's work: never stash, revert or overwrite them; commit only your own paths. Start with the CI pre-check (the "Before claiming" step of the CI criterion in Done when: a read-only `gh run list`; a red previous run is fixed and pushed under the previous bead's ID before anything else); only then claim: `br update hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha --claim --actor worker-<short-id> --json` (pick a short id such as `worker-a1`; use the same `--actor` on every br command and name it in the close reason), then `br sync --flush-only`. `br` auto-flushes `.beads/issues.jsonl`: that file is yours to stage with your paths — the claim rides in your first commit (the first Step 6 `fix:` commit if there is one, else the close commit) and the close in the close commit (see Done when).

Files:
- Modify only on a fix-forward finding: the tracked file that carries the private detail (a user-facing doc, any file under benchmarks/, a code or eval file named in Steps 2–5), or a bead field through `br update`.
- Generated, not committed: `$TMPDIR/gl-git.json`, `$TMPDIR/gl-dir.json`, `target/distrib/`.
- Tracker: .beads/issues.jsonl (claim + close)

Prerequisites: hunch-task-16-release-ont (the dist config and README Install must exist). Blocks hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2.

Done when:
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `gitleaks git . --log-opts="--all"` and `gitleaks dir .` both printed "no leaks found" (or the finding is recorded by file, commit and rule id, never by value).
- [ ] The manual sweep and the per-file review ran over every tracked file, every bead note and close reason, and every commit body; each hit is classified; user-facing docs use `/path/to/key` and "a typical macOS dev machine" and the grep for personal tooling details is empty.
- [ ] No launch draft is tracked (`git ls-files` grep empty, no docs/launch/); the locally built installer script and the dist config carry no local path.
- [ ] Every fix-forward finding is fixed in a gated commit under this bead's ID; every rewrite/rotation finding is recorded (no value), v0 acceptance carries the NOT ACCEPTED note and this bead stays open. If a rewrite/rotation finding keeps this bead open: do not close it; run the pre-push scan, then commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` alone (this bead's notes and the NOT ACCEPTED note on hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2; never a secret value) as `chore: record audit blocker (hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha)`, push, and stop.
- [ ] `ubs` on any file you changed, outside the sandbox (ubs creates its temp dir under /var/folders): if none is a language ubs scans (.rs, .py, …), ubs exits 3 "nothing scanned" — expected, not a failure: record `ubs: not applicable — nothing scanned (exit 3)` in the close reason; never set `UBS_ALLOW_NO_SCAN` or any override, never touch a code file to make it scan; if it scanned something, exit 0 is the bar. `cargo test -- --test-threads=1` (sandbox disabled) still green if a file it reads changed (PRIVACY.md is `include_str!`'d).
- [ ] Close before committing, once every step ran with no rewrite/rotation finding: `br close hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha --actor worker-<short-id> --reason "<pass/fail note: scanner results, sweep classes with counts, files reviewed, launch-draft check, installer check, docs check, fix-forward SHAs, no rewrite/rotation finding; ubs line; CI conclusion of the previous push (the filtered gh run list of the CI criterion matched on the origin/main SHA, outside the sandbox; a red run there was fixed under its own bead's ID before you claimed; if gh is unavailable, say so)>" --json`, then `br sync --flush-only`. No secret value, no draft text in the reason.
- [ ] One signed close commit: `git add .beads/issues.jsonl` (fix-forward files went in their own `fix:` commits); subject `chore: secret and PII audit before release (hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha)`; `git push origin main` (sandbox disabled). If the push is rejected: `git pull --rebase` (never stash, never force-push), re-run the gate, push again. `git status` shows up to date with origin/main.
- [ ] Pre-push scan (every bead: the repo `tpellet/hunch` is public, so a push is publication; the rule is ~/.claude/AGENTS.md "## Public Repositories — Push With Care", this is the hunch form). Before every `git push`, outside the sandbox: `gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v` (gitleaks 8.30.1 is installed; `brew install gitleaks` if it is missing; the repo's `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist, added by hunch-task-01-scaffold-p8n, is picked up automatically) must end with "no leaks found"; then read `git diff origin/main..HEAD` yourself for private information: API keys or tokens, `Authorization` headers, pasted API responses, emails other than the commit author's, absolute local paths (`/Users/...`, `/private/tmp/...`) anywhere but in bead and plan instructions, which already name the checkout and the launch folder by absolute path, scratchpad or session URLs, names of Thomas's private repos or projects, personal or admin details, other people's data, communications drafts (tweet, Show HN, announcement: those live only in /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch-launch/, never in the repo, bead notes, close reasons or commit messages). User-facing files (README.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, PRIVACY.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/) name the key path generically, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key`, and the machine as "a typical macOS dev machine": never the real key file name, never tool counts of Thomas's Mac, never his personal tooling (vault notes, skills, reviewer models); internal files (AGENTS.md, the plan, beads) may keep the real key path. Any hit: do not push; fix forward in a new commit under this bead's ID (never rewrite history, never force-push), `br update hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "pre-push: <what was removed, no values>"`, `br sync --flush-only`, re-scan, then push. A secret that already reached the remote: stop, do not rewrite, report it in the hand-off (Thomas rotates the key). Commit bodies stay technical: no `Co-Authored-By`, no `Claude-Session:` trailer (whether that trailer counts as private is an open question for Thomas; until he answers, leave it out). State `pre-push scan: clean` in the hand-off.
- [ ] CI (one rule for every bead: a red run belongs to the bead whose push turned it red and is fixed under that bead's ID). Before claiming — the first step of this bead, read-only: `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --limit 3 --json databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion` (outside the sandbox) and use the run whose `headSha` equals `git rev-parse origin/main` (re-list after a few seconds if it is not there yet). If that run is red, fix it under the previous bead's ID before you claim: first `br update <previous-bead-id> --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "CI fix: <what>"` and `br sync --flush-only`, then one commit `fix: <what> (<previous-bead-id>)` staging the fix and `.beads/issues.jsonl` (gate, push; report the fix SHA in the hand-off); only then claim this bead. After your push: the same `gh run list`, using the run whose `headSha` equals `git rev-parse HEAD`, then `gh run watch <databaseId>` until it ends; report the conclusion in the hand-off; a red run is noted first with `br update hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "CI fix: <what>"` and `br sync --flush-only`, then fixed in a follow-up commit `fix: <what> (hunch-secret-pii-audit-8ha)` staging the fix and `.beads/issues.jsonl` (gate, push; report the fix SHA in the hand-off) before your session ends. Fix subjects: keep `<what>` ≤ 22 characters so the subject stays < 72 (check with `git log -1 --format=%s | awk '{print length}'`). A red run your Mac cannot reproduce (Linux-only, or a toolchain difference — CI pins `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.93.1`, the toolchain the plan was verified on; keep it pinned) is fixed the same way under this rule: read `gh run view <databaseId> --log-failed`, fix the cause at the root or the CI environment (e.g. a missing package in `ci.yml`); never `#[ignore]`, `#[cfg]`-gate or delete a test, never loosen a workflow check, and `#[allow]` only a demonstrable false positive, with a one-line comment. Release-workflow (tag) runs belong to the acceptance bead, not to this rule. If `gh` is unavailable, say so in the close reason.
acceptance_criteria: See '## Acceptance Criteria' in the description.
notes: fixed forward: demo.cast + demo.gif (re-rendered from the cast with agg --theme dracula, byte-identical recipe verified), PRIVATE: macOS per-user temp dir path of the recording in scene 1; replaced by /tmp/hunch-demo/buildfail. No value.

title: Task 6: hunch pick
description:
Outcome: `hunch pick "<intent>"` works: stdin lines → tournament → prints the matching line(s) (or 1-based line numbers with `--index`), exit 3 when nothing fits; blank lines are skipped and a repeated line is sent once, while original line numbers are preserved; `tests/pick.rs` (5) passes; committed and pushed.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-hunch-v0-design.md; the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints" and the section "### Task 6: `hunch pick`" (Steps 1–3). The plan holds the verbatim, compile-verified code; copy it exactly, do not redesign. Run `cargo fmt` before `cargo fmt --check`.

Context:
- Consumes: `input::read_stdin_async` (Task 4); `tournament::{rank, Prompts, Ranking, Candidate}` (Task 4); `jev::client::Client` (Task 3); `cmd::Outcome`, `Exit`, `HunchError` (Task 1); `Config { threshold, prewarm }`; harness `common::{mock, hunch, FakeJev, option_containing}`.
- Produces: `cmd::pick::run(ctx, intent: &str, top: usize, index: bool) -> Result<Outcome, HunchError>` (stub signature kept; body replaced); `pub const cmd::pick::MAX_LINES: usize = 20_000` (Task 11's `capabilities()` reads it); data `{ "matches": [{ "line": usize (1-based, ORIGINAL stdin numbering), "text": String, "p": f64 }], "any": f64 }`.
- Rules copied from the plan: `top == 0` → `Usage("-n must be at least 1")`; `Client::new(ctx)?` + prewarm if `ctx.prewarm`; blank lines never leave the machine and a repeated line is sent once (two identical items split the Choice mass; the first occurrence keeps its line number) — build `kept: Vec<usize>` of the first index of each distinct non-blank line (a `HashSet` of trimmed lines, exactly as the plan block does), `items = kept.map(lines)`, and report `line = kept[c.index] + 1` (the blank-line `--index` test fails on the old `c.index + 1`); `kept.len() > MAX_LINES` → `InputTooLarge` (100k lines would be 500 requests, a 429 storm and ~25 s); prompts verbatim: choose "Which entry in `items` is the one described by `request`? title: Task 10: hunch run argument pointing, never-execute list, confirmation, execution, init
description:
Outcome: `hunch run` is complete: argument pointing from man-page flags and tokens copied from the request (`src/args.rs`), the never-execute list by tool name/prefix, `/dev/tty` confirmation or `--yes`, machine-mode execution only with `--exec --yes` (child stdout → stderr so stdout stays one envelope), and `hunch init zsh|bash` (the `,` alias); 5 contract + 3 unit tests pass; the live smoke `live_run_routes_tar` is added and run; committed and pushed.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-hunch-v0-design.md; the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints" (Safety bullet) and the section "### Task 10: `hunch run` — argument pointing, never-execute list, confirmation, execution, shell alias" (Design paragraph, Execution policy, Steps 1–7). The plan holds the verbatim, compile-verified code; copy it exactly, do not redesign. Run `cargo fmt` before `cargo fmt --check`.

Context:
- Consumes: Task 9 `cmd::run::{route, Route, RunFlags, load_tools}`; `manpage::{Flag, options_text, parse_flags}`, `inventory::Tool` (Task 8); `jev::client::Client`, `jev::{Question, Questions}`, `Response.answers` (Tasks 2–3); `cmd::confirm_tty` (Task 1, the shared prompt), `cli::Shell`, `cmd::Outcome`, `Exit`, `HunchError::{Declined, Input}`; `tests/live.rs::live_key_present` (Task 8); harness `common::{mock, hunch, bin, FakeJev, option_containing}`.
- Produces: `args::value_candidates(request: &str) -> Vec<String>` (quoted strings first, then tokens containing a digit, `.`, `/` or `~`, trailing `,.:` trimmed, deduped, ≤ 40); `args::Proposal { argv: Vec<String>, flags: Vec<(String, f64)>, file: Option<(String, f64)>, placeholders: usize }`; `async args::propose(client, request, tool: &Tool, flags: &[Flag], cwd: &[String], threshold: f64) -> Result<Proposal, HunchError>` (ONE request: state `{ request, tool, flags: ["--x — desc"], values: ["[V00] v"], files: ["[F000] f"] }`; per flag i a Noul `use{i:03}` ("Does `request` ask for the behaviour described in `flags[{i}]`?" — what the request is, never whether a flag should be passed), per value-taking flag a Choice `val{i:03}` over V-ids + NONE, one Choice `file` over F-ids + NONE; keep flags whose Noul `p >= threshold.max(FLAG_FLOOR)`; value from the chosen V-id else the placeholder `<VALUE>` (placeholders += 1); file appended only if its Choice `p >= threshold.max(FILE_FLOOR)`; order tool, flags in help order, file; missing Noul answers are `Protocol` errors via `?`). At the top of src/args.rs, `const FLAG_FLOOR: f64 = 0.7; const FILE_FLOOR: f64 = 0.6;` with the plan's doc comment: floors above the user's threshold for composing argv, a higher-stakes step than routing — raising `-t` tightens both, lowering it never loosens them (Global Constraints: the threshold gates absolute Nouls; a Choice probability is never compared to it directly, and the file floor is the one documented exception, as a floor). In src/cmd/run.rs: `const NEVER_EXEC: &[&str]` = rm, rmdir, dd, fdisk, diskutil, shred, srm, wipefs, sudo, su, doas, kill, killall, pkill, reboot, halt, shutdown, poweroff, init, telinit, launchctl, systemctl, sh, bash, zsh, dash, ksh, fish, env, xargs, nohup, nice, timeout, time, exec, eval, command, find, watch, parallel, osascript; `const NEVER_EXEC_PREFIX: &[&str]` = mkfs, newfs, python, perl, ruby, node, php, lua (Linux ships interpreters versioned: python3.12, perl5.36, ruby3.1, nodejs, php8.2, lua5.4; false positives such as phpunit/luacheck fail safe); `pub fn cmd::run::blocked_reason(tool: &str) -> Option<String>` (basename; exact list or prefix → "<base> is on hunch's never-execute list"); `pub fn cmd::run::relevant_files(intent, cwd: &[String]) -> Vec<String>` (only cwd names whose lowercase contains a ≥ 3-char alphanumeric word of the request, sorted, ≤ 200 — the directory listing never leaves the machine otherwise, and `read_dir` order is not canonical: option order moved an uncertain probability by up to 0.23 in Thomas's measurements, and the sorted list is what the cache key hashes); the final `cmd::run::run` (replace the whole Task 9 function; data gains `flags: [{ flag, p }]`, `complete: bool`, `blocked: Option<String>`, `executed`, `child_exit: Option<i32>`); `cmd::agent::init(shell: Shell) -> Outcome` (replace only that stub body; zsh script: `alias ,='noglob hunch run'` plus the opt-in `command_not_found_handler` guarded by `HUNCH_CNF` and routing ≥ 3-word unknown commands; bash: `alias ,='hunch run'` plus `command_not_found_handle`; data `{ "script": body }`, human = body).
- Execution policy (copy exactly): `!flags.no_args` → parse flags via `spawn_blocking(manpage::parse_flags(&manpage::options_text(&name).unwrap_or_default()))`, list cwd (non-hidden names), `files = relevant_files(intent, &cwd)`, and call `args::propose` only if flags or files are non-empty; `complete = placeholders == 0`; `blocked = blocked_reason(&tool.name)`; human mode prints on stderr: the route line when `--dry-run`, each chosen flag with its man-page description, and "hunch: fill the <VALUE> placeholders and run it yourself:" or "hunch: not offering to run this (<why>); check it and run it yourself:"; `may_execute = complete && blocked.is_none() && !dry_run && (machine ? exec && yes : yes || confirm_tty(prompt)? == Some(true))`, where `Some(false)` → `Err(HunchError::Declined)` (exit 130) and `None` (no TTY) → print only, exit 0; execution via `std::process::Command::new(&argv[0]).args(&argv[1..])` (argv only, never a shell), with `child.stdout(std::io::stderr())` in machine mode; `.status()`; exit `ChildFailed` (7) iff executed and child code ≠ 0; human stdout = `argv.join(" ") + "\n"` unless executed. Flags come from `manpage::options_text` only — no binary is ever run with `--help`; `chmod -R`/`chown -R` are deliberately NOT special-cased (the list is by tool name only, lead decision).
- Shell check (Step 5; an agent's shell has no TTY, so use the non-interactive interactive-mode form): after `cargo build`, run `zsh -ic 'eval "$(./target/debug/hunch init zsh)"; alias ,'` and `bash -ic 'eval "$(./target/debug/hunch init bash)"; alias ,'`; both must print the `,` alias; paste both outputs into the commit body. Run both outside the sandbox. Judge by the exit code and the printed alias line on stdout (`,='noglob hunch run'` for zsh, `alias ,='hunch run'` for bash); "cannot set terminal process group" / "no job control in this shell" and rc-file warnings on stderr are expected noise, not a failure — paste stdout into the commit body. Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-hunch-v0-design.md (Principles 7 "Fast"); the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints" and the section "### Task 12: Speed — prewarm evidence and benchmarks" (Steps 1–5). Copy `bench.sh` verbatim from the plan.

Context:
- Evidence task; no new interfaces. Needs the live key: run every benchmark command as `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key <command>` with the sandbox disabled (hunch reads the file; never read, print, copy or echo it). Live-step policy: the benchmark run is expected to happen — the key file exists on this machine. Only if the live calls genuinely fail (network or API down, retried once) may the bead close without numbers: record the exact error with `br update hunch-task-12-benchmarks-usu --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "NOT RUN: benchmarks — <error>"`, create a follow-up bead (`br create --title "Re-run benchmarks and decide prewarm (hunch-task-12-benchmarks-usu)" -t task -p 1 -l live,v0 --description "<bench.sh command, the prewarm decision rule, what to record>" --json`, then `br dep add hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2 <new-id>` so v0 cannot be accepted without numbers), commit bench.sh and the fixture without results.md, keep prewarm unchanged (the decision needs the numbers), state NOT RUN in the close reason, and claim no number anywhere (README does not exist yet; 13b will write "pending").
- Step 1: `cargo build --release`; `brew install hyperfine` if absent (Thomas's Mac).
- Step 2: `benchmarks/bench.sh` verbatim (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`, the header comment `# Run as: TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key benchmarks/bench.sh   (sandbox disabled)` — benchmarks/ is user-facing, so the generic path, never the real key file name — `set -euo pipefail`, `H=./target/release/hunch`, `LS=$(mktemp); ls /usr/bin > "$LS"`, `LOG=benchmarks/fixtures/cargo-fail.log`, then `hyperfine --ignore-failure --warmup 1 --runs 15 --export-markdown benchmarks/results.md` with the 8 named runs: "pick cold" (HUNCH_NO_CACHE=1), "pick cold no-prewarm" (+HUNCH_NO_PREWARM=1), "pick warm", "is cold" (`|| true`), "why cold" (`< $LOG`), "run cold route-only" (`--dry-run --no-args extract a tar archive`), "run cold full" (`--dry-run burn a dvd from this iso`), "rg baseline" (`rg -c compress $LS || true`)). `--ignore-failure` because exit 3/1 are legitimate outcomes and one flaky network error must not abort the run. Make the script executable. Fixture `benchmarks/fixtures/cargo-fail.log`: capture a real failing `cargo build` of a tiny throwaway crate (create it under $TMPDIR, outside the repo) with a deliberate unresolved import; check by eye that the log holds no secrets or personal paths you would not publish. Cargo prints the crate's absolute path on the `Compiling tiny v0.1.0 (…)` line: hand-edit it to `(/tmp/tiny)` in the log before committing; change nothing else in the log. "run cold full" (routing + fit + args + man renders) is the number people feel when they type `, <something>`; it is the one to publish for `run`.
- Step 3 (latency claims rule, binding for 13b/13c/13d/16 and any launch post): every latency number anywhere comes from `benchmarks/results.md` for that verb, as p50 and p95, with machine, network, date and model; no global "0.4 s" claim; if "run cold full" p50 is above 1 s, the README says so.
- Step 4 (prewarm decision): the runtime keeps driving the prewarm GET during stdin/inventory reads (`spawn_blocking`) and prewarm reads the response body so the connection is pooled, so this is a fair test. If "pick cold" p50 is NOT at least 50 ms faster than "pick cold no-prewarm", remove prewarm everywhere (code removal inside files only; never delete a file): the `prewarm` field and the `env("HUNCH_NO_PREWARM")` line in src/config.rs plus its `cfg()` test helper; `Client::prewarm` in src/jev/client.rs; the four `if ctx.prewarm { client.prewarm(); }` blocks in src/cmd/is.rs, pick.rs, why.rs, run.rs; `prewarm: false` in `tests/common::config`; the "HUNCH_NO_PREWARM" entry in `tests/common::bin`; the HUNCH_NO_PREWARM row in `capabilities()` (src/cmd/agent.rs) and its mention in docs/ROBOT_MODE.md; the "pick cold no-prewarm" line in bench.sh; and in the plan document the Global Constraints env bullet, the File Structure line for jev/client.rs and the Task 2/Task 3 Interfaces lines naming prewarm (the plan's Step 4 text names these same plan-document edits; its Files list for this task ends at docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, so the plan file is listed here for staging). If prewarm is kept, change no code. Either way record the two "pick cold" numbers and the decision in benchmarks/README.md.
- benchmarks/README.md: the p50/p95 table per run with machine (model/CPU), network, date, model id (`jev-1.13.0`), hyperfine version, and the prewarm decision.
- Cut order if v0 runs long (plan header, "Launch cut line"): Homebrew tap → `run` argument pointing (ship `--no-args` behaviour as the default) → benchmarks beyond `pick`/`why`, and the README says so. Only the lead or Thomas invokes a cut; never cut the `why` eval, the redaction/privacy work or the quality gate. Do not cut on your own initiative.
- Rules (every bead): strictly serial on `main`, no branches/worktrees/PRs; the gate (must stay green after any prewarm removal) and every `git commit`/`git push` run with the sandbox disabled; never weaken or delete a test; never delete files; treat unexplained working-tree changes as another agent's work: never stash, revert or overwrite them; commit only your own paths. Start with the CI pre-check (the "Before claiming" step of the CI criterion in Done when: a read-only `gh run list`; a red previous run is fixed and pushed under the previous bead's ID before anything else); only then claim: `br update hunch-task-12-benchmarks-usu --claim --actor worker-<short-id> --json` (pick a short id such as `worker-a1`; use the same `--actor` on every br command and name it in the close reason), then `br sync --flush-only`. `br` auto-flushes `.beads/issues.jsonl`: that file is yours to stage with your paths — the claim and the close ride in this bead's one commit (see Done when).

Files:
- Create: benchmarks/bench.sh (executable), benchmarks/README.md, benchmarks/fixtures/cargo-fail.log, benchmarks/results.md (hyperfine output, committed)
- Modify only if Step 4 removes prewarm: benchmarks/bench.sh (the "pick cold no-prewarm" line), src/jev/client.rs, src/cmd/is.rs, src/cmd/pick.rs, src/cmd/why.rs, src/cmd/run.rs, src/config.rs, tests/common/mod.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md
- Tracker: .beads/issues.jsonl (claim + close)

Prerequisites: hunch-task-11-agent-surface-eig

Done when:
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `benchmarks/results.md` exists with all 8 rows produced by a live hyperfine run with the key file (or NOT RUN per the live-step policy above: follow-up bead created, no number claimed anywhere).
- [ ] benchmarks/README.md states p50/p95 per run, machine, network, date, model, and the prewarm decision with both "pick cold" numbers.
- [ ] Gate green (sandbox disabled): `cargo fmt && cargo fmt --check && cargo check --all-targets && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test -- --test-threads=1`.
- [ ] `ubs benchmarks/bench.sh` plus any changed .rs files, run outside the sandbox (ubs creates its temp dir under /var/folders). ubs scans only the languages it supports (.rs, .py, …; shell is not one): if Step 4 changed no .rs file, ubs exits 3 "nothing scanned" — that is expected, not a failure: record `ubs: not applicable — nothing scanned (exit 3)` in the close reason; never set `UBS_ALLOW_NO_SCAN` or any override, never add or touch a code file to make ubs scan. If it scanned .rs files, exit 0 is the bar: fix genuine bugs at the root; do not rewrite compile-verified plan code for stylistic warnings — give the warning count by category in the close reason and name any you judged genuine and fixed.
- [ ] Close before committing, once the gate passed: `br close hunch-task-12-benchmarks-usu --actor worker-<short-id> --reason "<p50 per verb, prewarm decision, ubs warnings left, CI conclusion of the previous push (the filtered gh run list of the CI criterion matched on the origin/main SHA, outside the sandbox; a red run there was fixed under its own bead's ID before you claimed; if gh is unavailable, say so)>" --json`, then `br sync --flush-only`.
- [ ] One signed commit: `git add benchmarks/bench.sh benchmarks/README.md benchmarks/fixtures/cargo-fail.log benchmarks/results.md .beads/issues.jsonl` plus the prewarm-removal files if Step 4 changed them (list them explicitly; never `git add -A`); subject `perf: benchmarks and prewarm decision (hunch-task-12-benchmarks-usu)` with the p50/p95 table in the body; `git push origin main` (sandbox disabled). - [ ] Pre-push scan (every bead: the repo `tpellet/hunch` is public, so a push is publication; the rule is ~/.claude/AGENTS.md "## Public Repositories — Push With Care", this is the hunch form). Commit bodies stay technical: no `Co-Authored-By`, no `Claude-Session:` trailer (whether that trailer counts as private is an open question for Thomas; until he answers, leave it out). State `pre-push scan: clean` in the hand-off.
- [ ] CI (one rule for every bead: a red run belongs to the bead whose push turned it red and is fixed under that bead's ID). Before claiming — the first step of this bead, read-only: `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --limit 3 --json databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion` (outside the sandbox) and use the run whose `headSha` equals `git rev-parse origin/main` (re-list after a few seconds if it is not there yet). After your push: the same `gh run list`, using the run whose `headSha` equals `git rev-parse HEAD`, then `gh run watch <databaseId>` until it ends; report the conclusion in the hand-off; a red run is noted first with `br update hunch-task-12-benchmarks-usu --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "CI fix: <what>"` and `br sync --flush-only`, then fixed in a follow-up commit `fix: <what> (hunch-task-12-benchmarks-usu)` staging the fix and `.beads/issues.jsonl` (gate, push; report the fix SHA in the hand-off) before your session ends. A red run your Mac cannot reproduce (Linux-only, or a toolchain difference — CI pins `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.93.1`, the toolchain the plan was verified on; keep it pinned) is fixed the same way under this rule: read `gh run view <databaseId> --log-failed`, fix the cause at the root or the CI environment (e.g. a missing package in `ci.yml`); never `#[ignore]`, `#[cfg]`-gate or delete a test, never loosen a workflow check, and `#[allow]` only a demonstrable false positive, with a one-line comment. close_reason: Integrated by lead from parallel worktree wt/bead-12 (worker 3b9ae31). hyperfine 15 runs, jev-1.13.0, p50: pick cold 721 ms, pick warm 7 ms, is 434 ms, why 602 ms, run route-only 1,879 ms, run full 1,946 ms, rg 2 ms (p95 in benchmarks/results.md). No live eval run yet (that is 13d); this bead needs no API key.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-hunch-v0-design.md ("Evidence at launch"); the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints", the intro of "### Task 13: Evals, README, PRIVACY review, demo — four beads (13a–13d)" and the section "#### Task 13a: Eval data and scripts" (Steps 1–6). Copy `scripts/eval_run.py` and the freeze recipe verbatim from the plan.

Context:
- Consumes: the binary's `--json` contract only (`hunch run --json --dry-run --no-args <request>` → `data.tool`, `data.fit`, `meta.cost_usd`, `exit_code`; `hunch why --json -n 3 < log` → `data.causes[].line`), env `HUNCH_INVENTORY_FILE` (Task 9), the inventory cache naming `inventory-<fp>.json` and its `(no man page)` summaries (Task 8), the `SIGNAL` regex from src/cmd/why.rs (Task 7; copied into eval_why.py). Read-only inputs: evals/prototype/{intents.json, eval_nl2bash_out.json, eval_intents_out.json, eval_nl2bash_report.txt, router.py, args_probe.py}.
- Step 1 (routing data + inventory freeze): copy evals/prototype/intents.json → evals/run_intents.json (format `[{ "request": str, "ok": [tool, ...] }]`, 49 rows; `ok: []` = should abstain). Build evals/nl2bash_sample.json from evals/prototype/eval_nl2bash_out.json keeping `request`, `head` (gold utility) and `leaks_name` per row (120 rows; not written by the author; the prototype report shows it is hard — top-1 0.29, 73/120 abstained — publish whatever v0 gets). Freeze the inventory with the plan's exact recipe and the sandbox DISABLED (inside it `man -k` is refused and the list silently degrades to names only, which is not cached): `D=$(mktemp -d)`; `cargo build --release`; `env -u HUNCH_NO_CACHE -u HUNCH_INVENTORY_FILE TYPESAFE_API_KEY=dummy HUNCH_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9 HUNCH_CACHE_DIR=$D ./target/release/hunch run --dry-run --no-args x` (exit 4 after the connect error is expected; the cache file is written before the first API call; nothing reaches TypeSafe); `ls /opt/homebrew/bin /opt/homebrew/sbin /usr/local/bin /usr/local/sbin 2>/dev/null | jq -R . | jq -s unique > "$D/public.json"`; `jq --slurpfile pub "$D/public.json" '[.[] | select(.summary != "(no man page)" or (.name as $n | $pub[0] | index($n) != null))]' "$D"/inventory-*.json > evals/inventory.json` — keeps every documented tool and only those undocumented names that also live in a system-wide prefix (the repo is public; personal ~/.local/bin, ~/.cargo/bin, plugin dirs and private scripts are dropped; Homebrew tools the evals need — uv, yq, fd, rg, entr, exiftool, tesseract — survive). Check with jq: documented count > 300; count undocumented kept (in evals/inventory.json) and undocumented on this machine (in `$D/inventory-*.json`, kept + dropped). If no `inventory-*.json` exists in `$D`, the man index was empty: re-run outside the sandbox. Record the three counts (documented / undocumented kept / dropped) in the commit body only — 13d copies them into the README. Skim the kept `(no man page)` names once before committing. Reference (round 3, Thomas's Mac): exit 4, 1,869 cached, 1,260 documented, 430 kept, 179 dropped.
- Step 2 (`why` data; TIMEBOX 60 minutes; do NOT start on LogChunks — licence review plus relabelling does not fit): collect 20 real failing logs from public GitHub Actions runs of MIT/Apache projects (at least 4 each of cargo, npm/tsc, pytest, go, docker); run each through `input::redact` semantics (a throwaway `cargo run` snippet or by eye); hand-label the root-cause line range; save `evals/why/<id>.log` + `evals/why/<id>.expect` (JSON `{ "lines": [start, end], "source": "<run URL>", "license": "<SPDX>" }`); document provenance per file in evals/why/README.md. Fetching needs network access to github.com/api.github.com (gh CLI or curl); if fewer than 20 land inside the timebox, stop at the timebox and state the count in the README (13b) and the hand-off.
- Step 3: scripts/eval_run.py verbatim (uv inline metadata `requires-python = ">=3.11"`, no deps; sets HUNCH_INVENTORY_FILE=evals/inventory.json; BM25 over the same frozen list; rows written to evals/out/ (gitignored) after every request; per-set `errors` count for missing or error envelopes; reliability table labelled "routes hunch acted on" — abstain and error rows excluded in both sets; a last line counting the routes whose `fit` is within 0.06 of `meta.threshold`, the measured run-to-run jitter of identical requests, which 13d pastes next to the table). Lint: `uvx ruff check scripts/` must print "All checks passed!" (verified in rounds 3–4 on this block).
- Step 4: scripts/eval_why.py (uv inline script): for each evals/why/<id>.log run `hunch why --json -n 3 < log`, report hit@1 and hit@3 (a hit = the pointed line is inside `expect.lines`), and the same for two free baselines on the same files — first line matching SIGNAL and last line matching SIGNAL (regex copied from src/cmd/why.rs); print one table, plus the min and median of `data.any` over the cases (every case contains a failure, so this shows where found cases' absolute Noul sits against the 0.5 threshold — the knob gates that Noul, never the Choice). If hunch does not beat first-match, the README (13d) says so.
- Step 5 (optional for v0; skip if time is short and say so): evals/run_args.json — 20 requests with the flags a correct command must contain (e.g. `extract foo.tar.gz` → tar with -x and -f/-xzf; start from evals/prototype/args_probe.py); extend eval_run.py to run them without `--no-args` and report "tool right", "all required flags present", "any extra flag" separately.

description:

title: file kind: content phrases give confident wrong siblings (gitdiff.rs 0.94, input.rs 0.70)
description:
Outcome: the `file` kind does not return a confident wrong file for a phrase that describes what a file does. On the hunch-lpp held-out set, content phrases either resolve to the gold file or abstain; no content phrase yields a sibling at p ≥ 0.7.

Evidence (jevify 0.8.0, jev-1.13.0, 2026-09-22, ~/Projects/jevify, 191 candidates, one window; the same 12-item set as the 0.7.0 evaluation):

```
$ jevify fill --dry-run --json -- wc -l '@{file:the module that stages hunks}'
jevify fill: file src/gitdiff.rs 0.94 (next 0.01, none 0.05) src/gitdiff.rs; candidates 191, windows 1     # gold src/cmd/add.rs
$ jevify fill --dry-run --json -- wc -l '@{file:the code that splits input into records}'
jevify fill: file src/input.rs 0.70 (next 0.19, none 0.05) src/input.rs; candidates 191, windows 1          # gold src/records.rs (0.7.0 gave src/records.rs 0.99)
$ jevify fill --dry-run --json -- wc -l '@{file:the recipe engine}'
jevify fill: not run: arg 3 file: no_match; closest: none (0.55), docs/guide/how-it-works.md (0.25), ...       # gold src/source.rs
$ jevify fill --dry-run --json -- wc -l '@{file:retry and backoff for HTTP requests to the backend}'
jevify fill: not run: arg 3 file: no_match; closest: none (0.79), src/jev/client.rs (0.20), ...              # gold src/jev/client.rs
```

Content phrases: 0 of 4 correct (0.7.0: 1 of 4), 2 confident wrong picks, 2 abstentions. Name phrases stay 7 of 7 (marker parser, release script, privacy policy, man pages, publish workflow, BaselineDetectionService, ClinicianReportPDFGenerator). hunch-con closed the abstentions as a documented known limit; the wrong picks are not covered by that limit: a `fill` without `--dry-run` would run `wc -l src/gitdiff.rs` at 0.94 for "stages hunks". With `src/input.rs` (0.70) the excerpts made a neighbour that also splits lines (`split_lines`, `read_stdin`) look better than the parser in `src/records.rs`, which 0.7.0 chose at 0.99 from names alone.

Fix direction: for the `file` kind, let round two only confirm or reject the round-one leader (or require the round-two winner to beat NONE and the round-one leader by the ratio guard), instead of letting a sibling's excerpt overturn a strong name match; check whether the excerpt of `src/cmd/add.rs` (module doc comment) reaches the model at all; add these four phrases to a fill held-out set under evals/ with their gold.

Done when: the four commands above give gold or exit 3 (no wrong pick), the name phrases keep 7/7, and the result per phrase is recorded next to the model version.
notes: Lead: plan line ~327 (origin/x for a remote-only ref) is stale since hunch-emc; not this bead's job. For u7s: VISION's asymmetric doubt says fill and pick abstain when unsure; a confident wrong sibling (gitdiff.rs 0.94 for a content phrase) is the failure. Find why round two is confident on a wrong file (evidence, question wording, or excerpt content), fix the cause; do not tune the threshold or ratio. Report live before/after on the 4 content-phrase items of the evaluation (scratchpad eval/r2 results). CHANGELOG line goes in the final report.
close_reason: Single-window finals take every non-zero name (up to 24) instead of the top three; stages hunks -> add.rs 0.68 (was gitdiff.rs 0.94); recipe engine and retry phrases abstain correctly; name phrases unchanged; residual decisive-names case filed as hunch-8ar; gate green

description:

Context:
- Authorization (lead note): the plan marks Task 16 Step 3 "(needs Thomas)". Thomas explicitly authorized publishing a public v0 while AFK — "push it to the public remote ... v0 online and public" (2026-09-19) — and the repo tpellet/hunch is already public. That authorization covers the tag and the release below; no further approval is needed. It covers a verified v0 only: this bead does not close unless every live check below actually passed.
- Live test — sandbox DISABLED, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key` in each command's environment (hunch reads the file; you never read, print, copy or echo it). The per-verb matrix below is this bead's acceptance contract (the plan's Step 3 names only health, one `why`, one `pick`, one `run --dry-run`; the rest is lead-added). `cargo build --release`; `H="$PWD/target/release/hunch"` (absolute: two checks below run from another directory). Run and record exit code + one-line output for each:
  - `$H health` and `$H health --json` → 0, key accepted; `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=wrong $H health` → 5.
  - `$H capabilities --json` → 0; commands are exactly pick, why, run, is, capabilities, robot-docs, health, init (no add/sort); HUNCH_MODEL default jev-1.13.0.
  - `$H robot-docs`, `$H robot-docs privacy` → 0; `$H robot-docs nope` → 2.
  - `ls /usr/bin | $H pick "compress files"` → 0 and prints a real /usr/bin name; `printf 'a\nb\n' | $H pick "a spaceship"` → 3, empty stdout; `$H pick x < /dev/null` → 6.
  - `$H --json why -- sh -c "echo ok; echo 'error[E0432]: boom' >&2; exit 1"` → 0, cause text contains E0432, `data.child_exit == 1`; `$H why < benchmarks/fixtures/cargo-fail.log` → 0 with a `>` marked line.
  - `echo "I want my money back" | $H is "asks for a refund"; echo $?` → 0; `echo "hello" | $H is "asks for a refund"; echo $?` → 1 or 3; `$H is --band 0.9 x < /dev/null` → 2.
  - `$H run --dry-run "extract the gzipped archive"` → 0, proposes tar/bsdtar/gunzip/gzip, not executed; `$H --json run --dry-run "make a qr code"` → 3 unless something installed does it; the two `list files` checks run from an empty scratch directory (`cd "$(mktemp -d)"`, absolute `$H`) so argument pointing cannot pick up repo file names: `$H --json run --yes "list files"` → executed false (no --exec); `$H --json run --exec --yes "list files"` → executed true, stdout is exactly one envelope; `$H --json run --dry-run "delete the temp file"` → `data.tool` is `rm` or another deleter, `data.blocked` non-null, `data.executed == false`, nothing run (use `--json`: in human mode `blocked` is only a stderr sentence and is printed only when the proposal is complete).
  - `zsh -ic 'eval "$(./target/release/hunch init zsh)"; alias ,'` and `bash -ic 'eval "$(./target/release/hunch init bash)"; alias ,'` each show the `,=` alias (no TTY is available; `-ic` is the form to use).
  - `TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=$HOME/.ssh/typesafe-ai-key cargo test --test live -- --ignored --test-threads=1` → both live tests actually run (a SKIPPED line means NOT RUN — fix the environment, do not accept); `inventory_finds_many_tools_here` passes; a `live_run_routes_tar` miss follows the model-judgment rule below.
  Two kinds of check, two rules (lead decision, pass 2). Deterministic contract checks — exit codes 2/5/6, the envelope shape, `executed`, `blocked`, the alias, the capabilities list, `data.child_exit`, the live inventory test (Task 8's `inventory_finds_many_tools_here`; deterministic: > 300 documented tools, no key needed) — must pass: a failure there is a code defect; fix in place with the gate and a commit `fix: <what> (hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2)`, or report NOT ACCEPTED with the evidence and leave the bead open. Model-judgment checks — `is` refund → 0, `why` naming a cause / E0432, the `pick "compress files"` name, `pick "a spaceship"` over a/b → 3 (abstention), the `run` proposals (tar family, qr → 3, rm for "delete the temp file"), `live_run_routes_tar` (the same tar-family judgment, in tests/live.rs), `hello` → 1 or 3 — get exactly one re-run with `--no-cache` (`HUNCH_NO_CACHE=1` in the environment for the live test, which takes no flag); a miss that persists is recorded verbatim (command, exit code, output) in the close reason and with `br update hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2 --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "<miss>"`, and, if it is not already there, added to README "What it is bad at" (commit `docs: record v0 acceptance miss (hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2)`); it does not block acceptance. Never change prompts, constants, `WINDOW`, the threshold or any calibrated surface in this bead to "fix" one example. Only if every model-judgment check misses is it a code defect (the pipeline, not the model): investigate, fix in place or NOT ACCEPTED. If the API or network is down, append the error with `br update hunch-v0-acceptance-xp2 --actor worker-<short-id> --append-notes "<error>"`, leave the bead open and stop; retry later. There is no NOT RUN close for this bead. The live tests must actually run (not SKIPPED). `inventory_finds_many_tools_here` is deterministic. `live_run_routes_tar` asserts a model route, the same judgment as the matrix's tar-family row: if it fails on the tool name while the envelope is well-formed and the exit code is 0 or 3, treat it as a model-judgment miss — re-run it once with `HUNCH_NO_CACHE=1` and record verbatim; it is a code defect only if the envelope or the exit contract broke.

title: Build the paired study harness and price the full run
description:
First half of hunch-3cd: build the study harness and prove it on a subset, so the lead can price
the full run before committing to it. This bead does NOT run the full study.

Why a harness at all: the two existing runs (benchmarks/agents/PILOT.md) have one run per cell,
a baseline that was restricted in ways a real user is not, a sandbox an agent escaped by `cd`
(PILOT.md:155), and one recorded gap where the with-arm never called jevify (PILOT.md:196-200).
Those four faults are properties of how the study was run, not of what it found, and a harness is
how they stop recurring.

Read benchmarks/agents/PILOT.md first, in full, including the parts that record its own
weaknesses, and scripts/pilot_r4/ if it exists.

Build:
1. A task set of at least eight paired tasks, each with a checkable answer that a third party
   could score without knowing which arm produced it. A task whose answer is a commit sha, a file
   path, a branch name or a yes/no is checkable; "explain X" is not. Draw them from repositories
   that evals/ does not already use, and pin every one by sha.
2. A runner that executes one cell: one task, one arm, one run, recording correct (against the
   pinned answer, scored without seeing the arm), turns, input tokens, wall time, every jevify
   invocation with its argv and exit code, and the transcript. The with-arm has jevify available
   and told about it; the control arm is UNRESTRICTED -- it may use git log --grep, rg, find, fzf,
   reading listings, anything it would normally reach for. A control that is handicapped proves
   nothing.
3. A sandbox the agent cannot leave. The last study's agent escaped with `cd`. State how yours
   holds and show it holding.
4. A scorer that reports correctness per cell with a confidence interval, not a bare count, and
   that refuses to score a run whose transcript shows the task was leaked to the agent.

Then prove it: run TWO tasks at n = 3 per cell per arm (12 runs total). Report what the harness
produced, whether the scoring worked blind, and any fault you found in your own design. Do not
draw a conclusion about jevify from 12 runs, and say so in the write-up.

Finally, price the full study: from the 12 runs, give the lead the projected cost of 8 tasks at
n = 5 per cell per arm (80 runs) in wall time, in tokens, and in jevify classifications against
the keyless daily allowance of 20,000. Say what you would cut if the budget were half.

Write set: benchmarks/agents/** and scripts/study/** only. No change to src/, no change to
README.md.
Done when: the task set, runner, sandbox and scorer exist and are documented; the 12 validation
runs are recorded with their numbers; the faults you found in your own harness are written down;
the projection for the full study is stated with its assumptions. Gate: ubs on changed files;
cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
notes: Harness built and validated; not committed (lead commits). New: scripts/study/{tasks.jsonl,setup.sh,run_cell.py,run_study.sh,jevify_log.py,canary.py,blind.py,score.py,unblind.py,probe.py,price.py,README.md} and benchmarks/agents/STUDY.md; one paragraph added to benchmarks/agents/README.md. 12 validation runs (S1,S8 at n=3 per cell per arm): 12/12 correct both arms, every cell 95% Wilson [0.44,1.00], zero jevify calls in the with arm, zero escapes. Full study 8 tasks n=5 (80 runs) priced at ~32 min wall, 4.6 M input tokens, $2.53 agent inference, ceiling 1,100 keyless classifications. Gates: ubs exit 0; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1 green. Run artefacts outside the repo under ~/jevify-study/.
close_reason: Harness built and validated, commit 9b47740. Sandbox applied to the agent process so children and file tools inherit it; both arms denied exec of every jevify binary but the instrumented copy, so the call log is complete by construction; scoring split so the gold comparison sees arm-free records only. 12 validation runs: 12/12 correct both arms, no escapes. Two design faults exposed: the tasks are too easy for any design to discriminate, and the with arm called jevify zero times in six runs. Full 80-run study priced at 32 minutes, 4.6M tokens, 2.53 USD, 5.5 percent of the keyless day. Eight self-reported harness faults recorded.
