title: The envelope says whether ok is the field to branch on, and a deadline reads like one
description:
Two leftovers from hunch-098q, both small, both in the envelope's honesty.

1. `ok` is true on exit 1 and on exit 3. A harness that branches on `.ok` treats "no" and
   "abstained" as success, then fails on the `data` key that is not there. A live harness trial
   found this the expensive way. The construction site is `ok: true` in src/lib.rs.

   Decide what `ok` means and make the envelope say it. The candidates: `ok` means "jevify ran
   without error", which is what it does today and which makes it useless for branching; or `ok`
   means "the verb reached a decision and acted on it", which makes exit 1 and exit 3 false. The
   second reads better but it is a contract change, and a caller that treats `ok` as "no error"
   would start seeing false on a working `is` that answers no. Weigh both, choose, and say what
   breaks. If you keep the present meaning, then the envelope documentation and the capability
   strings must say plainly that `ok` is not the field to branch on and name the exit code as the
   branch, in the place a reader meets `ok` first.

2. A deadline's human message still reads "API unavailable: overall deadline of N s passed",
   because Display sits on the shared Unavailable variant that src/jev/client.rs builds. The
   kind is now correct (`api_deadline`); only the sentence a person reads is wrong. Give the
   deadline its own sentence, naming the deadline and JEVIFY_DEADLINE, so a person reading stderr
   learns the next move the way the kind already tells a machine.

Write set: src/lib.rs, src/exit.rs, src/jev/client.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md,
docs/guide/agents.md, CHANGELOG.md, tests/**.
Done when: a reader who meets `ok` learns whether to branch on it; the deadline's human sentence
names the deadline and the variable; tests pin both; the gate passes (cargo fmt --check, cargo
check --locked --all-targets, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test
--locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed files). Workers never commit; the lead commits.
notes:
--- decision, claude-hunch-w32n, before code ---

ITEM 1, what `ok` means. CHOICE: keep today's meaning, "jevify ran without error", and make
every place a reader meets `ok` say plainly that it is not the field to branch on and that
`exit_code` is.
Rejected: `ok` mirrors `exit_code == 0`, which would make exit 1 and exit 3 false.

Why, on the same grounds as hunch-098q. That bead refused to remap a child's exit code because
VISION's "One grammar" makes the exit codes the contract and because an existing caller's script
would have changed meaning under it with no way to notice. `ok` is the same shape of question.
Today `ok` is true whenever the verb decided and printed, which includes `is` answering no
(exit 1) and an abstention (exit 3). Redefining it would flip `ok` to false on a working `is`
that answers no. A caller who wrote `jq -e .ok` as "the call worked" would start reading a
correct no as a failure, silently: the envelope carries no schema version, `error` stays null on
exit 1 and exit 3, so nothing in the output would tell the caller its branch had changed sense.
That is exactly the silent change of meaning the precedent refused. Nothing forces the change
either: `exit_code` is already in the envelope, already equals the process status, and already
distinguishes all three cases, so the harness that got burned has a correct field to read today.

COST, stated plainly. `ok` stays useless for branching, and it stays a trap for a caller who
never reads the documentation: `.ok` is true on exit 1 and exit 3, and the `data` a caller then
expects may be absent. The mitigation is documentation, not code, so it only reaches a caller
who looks. Paid where `ok` is first met: the envelope field list in docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, the same
list in docs/guide/agents.md, and `capabilities.envelope`, which is the machine interface a
harness reads. A test pins the capability string and pins `ok == true` on exit 1 and exit 3, so
the meaning cannot drift away from what the documentation promises.

WHAT BREAKS for an existing caller: nothing. No field changes value. The change is documentation
plus one new `capabilities.envelope.ok` string.

ITEM 2, the deadline's sentence. The overall deadline gets its own `JevifyError::Deadline`
variant, so Display stops inheriting the shared `Unavailable` prefix. Before:
`API unavailable: overall deadline of 600 s passed (JEVIFY_DEADLINE)`. The exit stays 4 and the
kind stays `api_deadline`; the sentence names the deadline and JEVIFY_DEADLINE and no longer
blames the API for jevify's own budget. A real expiry in tests/deadline.rs pins the sentence.

--- implemented, claude-hunch-w32n ---
Files: src/lib.rs (comment at the ok: true site), src/exit.rs (new JevifyError::Deadline variant
with its own Display; kind/hint/example arms moved off the DEADLINE_PREFIX string match; the
const now only pins the phrase for tests), src/jev/client.rs (deadline_error builds Deadline),
src/cmd/agent.rs (capabilities.envelope gains ok and branch_on), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md,
docs/guide/agents.md. Tests: tests/is.rs (ok true on exit 0, 1 and 3 with exit_code telling them
apart), tests/agent.rs (capabilities.envelope.ok and branch_on, and both pages carry the
sentence), tests/deadline.rs (a real 1 s expiry: the envelope message no longer says "API
unavailable", and a new human-format run pins the stderr sentence).
CHANGELOG.md untouched: the lead writes the entry from the report.
Gate: cargo fmt --check PASSED, cargo check --locked --all-targets PASSED, cargo clippy --locked
--all-targets -- -D warnings PASSED, cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1 PASSED (394 passed,
12 ignored), ubs on the changed files PASSED (exit 0; its 15 "critical" hits are the pre-existing
== heuristic on enum and JSON comparisons and the sh -c of the reproduction tests).
Live tests (tests/live.rs, all #[ignore]) NOT RUN.
close_reason: Kept ok's meaning on the hunch-098q precedent: redefining it would flip ok to false on a working 'is' answering no and on an abstention, with nothing in the envelope to signal the change, and exit_code already separates all three cases. capabilities.envelope now carries ok and branch_on, and both agent-facing documents say it at the field. The deadline got its own error variant, so its human sentence names the deadline and JEVIFY_DEADLINE instead of claiming an outage; exit 4 and api_deadline unchanged. 404 tests pass.

title: fill: the finals shortcut fires on name decoys; decide whether a one-sided names round may skip the finals
description:
Measurement (hunch-ng2, benchmarks/results.md 'The fill finals shortcut on a held-out content-phrase set', evals/fill/finals/): on 33 held-out content phrases the shortcut at src/cmd/fill.rs (a decisive names Found with the runner-up out of play skips the finals of a tier-two kind) fires on 12 cases (classifier.dev) and 15 (TypeSafe), saves one request per fire (18-23% of the set's requests with the finals always on), and on one fire per backend selects a wrong file that the finals would have abstained on: src/wrapping.rs (0.72) for the wrapping code that lives in src/printer.rs, src/pager.rs (0.66) for the code that starts the pager in src/output.rs. Both are files named for the concept and holding something else, the case the rule assumes a one-sided names round rules out. The finals always on: false actions 1 and 2 (none touched by the rule), coverage 0.76 (pkg/brew abstains on both backends once read). Against 233e946 the current rule is an improvement (false actions 4 to 2 and 4 to 3, +3 requests).

Decide: keep the shortcut (one request per fire against a 7-8% false-action rate on the cases it decides alone), drop it for file and dir (finals always run when a tier-two kind has a single window; +12-15 requests on this set, one right directory lost to a finals abstention), or a narrower test. Whatever is chosen, re-run scripts/eval_fill_finals.py on both backends and record it under the same results.md section; do not tune on this set, it is the held-out one. Files: src/cmd/fill.rs, tests/fill.rs, docs/guide/kinds.md, benchmarks/results.md, CHANGELOG.md.
notes: LEAD DECISION 2026-09-22: drop the shortcut for the file and dir kinds; those finals always run. Reason, from the held-out measurement of hunch-ng2: with the shortcut the two backends make 2 and 3 false actions; with the finals always on they make 1 and 2, at accuracy 0.96 and 0.92 against 0.93 and 0.89. Coverage falls from 0.85 and 0.82 to 0.76, and the set costs 12 to 15 more requests (66 against 54 and 51). docs/VISION.md's asymmetric doubt says fill abstains rather than acts, and fill is the one verb that runs the caller's command, so a name decoy substituted into an argument costs more than a request. Keep the rule for branch and commit, where no held-out evidence exists yet; say so in the code comment and in the kinds guide. Re-measure with scripts/eval_fill_finals.py after the change and record the numbers in benchmarks/results.md.
close_reason: Lead decision applied: file and dir always run their finals; branch and commit keep the shortcut for lack of held-out evidence, stated in the code, the kinds guide and capabilities. Re-measured on the held-out set: classifier 1 false action at coverage 0.73, TypeSafe 3 at 0.85, 66 requests each. The repeat exposes run-to-run variation (the pager decoy flips), recorded in results.md; a single run per cell cannot separate the rest

title: why and pick print no record or request count on stderr, unlike filter and label
description:
Found by the hunch-lpp evaluation (jevify 0.7.0, 2026-09-22).

Evidence: docs/VISION.md says "A verb states its record and request counts before the first request and then does the work." filter and label do this ("jevify filter: 70 records, 70 distinct, 1 requests"). why and stdin pick do not:

    $ jevify why --no-cache < py-job.log
    jevify why: full output: <cache>/outputs/c207c1d17aa765d9.log        (no record or request count)
    $ seq 1 300 | sed 's/^/item /' | jevify pick --no-cache 'item 42'
    item 42                                                              (nothing on stderr)

The local invocation log of the evaluation reads counts from these lines. For human-mode why and pick it could record neither the request count nor the model.

Expected: why and pick (stdin and --from) print the same count line as filter and label before the first request: records or candidates, windows or requests. -q keeps it silent where the verb has -q.

Suggested write set: src/cmd/why.rs, src/cmd/pick.rs, tests/pick.rs and the why contract test (stderr assertions).
close_reason: why and stdin pick print counts and windows on stderr before the first request; contract assertions added; gate 336 green, ubs 0

title: fill refuses a marker in argv[0] (tool kind) with a misleading usage message
description:
Found by the hunch-lpp evaluation (jevify 0.7.0, jev-1.13.0, 2026-09-22).

Evidence: a tool marker in argv[0] is refused whenever its description holds a space, which is nearly always.

    $ jevify fill --dry-run -- '@{tool:the GitHub command line}' --version
    jevify fill: not run: usage: pass the command as separate arguments, for example 'git' 'switch' '@{branch:description}'
    exit 2

The same marker one position later works:

    $ jevify fill --dry-run -- env '@{tool:the GitHub command line}' --version
    jevify fill: tool gh 0.94 (next 0.05, none 0.01) gh: GitHub CLI; candidates 1884, windows 10; model jev-1.13.0
    exit 0

All 8 items of the held-out fill set for the tool kind hit this refusal. src/marker.rs `parse` rejects any argv[0] that contains a byte ' ' before it lexes markers. That guard is meant to catch `fill -- "git switch x"`, but it also catches the one place where the tool kind belongs. Plan section 5 lists "a marker in argv[0]" as a marker-table row.

Expected: the space guard applies only when argv[0] holds no marker. A marker in argv[0] resolves like any other argument. The usage message never tells the caller to split an argument that is already separate.

Suggested write set: src/marker.rs (guard and its unit test), tests/fill.rs (argv[0] tool marker, dry run).
notes:
Lead decision M1 (2026-09-22): a marker in argv[0] stays exit 2 (plan §1 lexer rows: 'a marker in argv[0]'; VISION line 132 scopes tool to route and pick --from tool). jevify never runs a model-chosen program. Fix only the message: when argv[0] holds a marker, the error says the command must be literal and gives the corrected form, e.g. "jevify pick --from tool '<description>'" to find the tool first; it never says 'pass the command as separate arguments' for a marker. Revert the check_program skip in src/cmd/fill.rs.
Lead decision N10 (review round 8, 2026-09-22): the guarantee is a grammar boundary, not a sandbox. argv[0] must be literal (exit 2 on a marker there, src/marker.rs), but a caller can still write a literal wrapper, e.g. env '@{tool:...}', whose resolved argument that wrapper executes. jevify authorizes nothing and the caller owns the command; 'never runs a model-chosen program' is false through such a wrapper. State it that way wherever the guarantee appears (capabilities safety text, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, docs/guide/verbs.md, VISION tool scope); keep the exit-2 tests (src/marker.rs:142). The doc wording change belongs to the next docs bead that touches those pages (hunch-hd8 may carry it if the lead assigns it).
close_reason: M1: argv[0] marker stays exit 2 with 'command must be literal; jevify pick --from tool ...' message; literal argv[0] with space keeps split message; unit + contract tests; gate green

title: Sufficiency gate: ask whether the evidence is enough before asking which one
description:
Workflow from a Jev practitioner's measured tip (2026-09-20, JEV TIP 005): an 'I don't know' option inside a Choice does not work (it won 0 of 80 runs, because it mixes 'which one' with 'is there enough evidence'), and a Choice over a state that supports two answers flips with option order. A separate Noul, 'does the state hold enough decision-relevant evidence to answer this question', was stable: 38.75 to 38.95 percent, and reversing the order moved it by 0.20 points. Rule: calibrate a sufficiency threshold on labelled examples, ask the intent question only above it, otherwise get more evidence and ask again.

In jevify: (1) compare the present any Noul of tournament::window ('is at least one entry the thing described') with a sufficiency wording, on the held-out queries of the operand experiment; (2) evidence escalation: handle line first, richer evidence (commit body, file excerpt, pod status) only when sufficiency is low, as a declared second evidence level of a source; dogfood case in hunch-1qa: git log --oneline lacks the commit body and pick exits 3; (3) a distinct abstention for agents, error kind insufficient_evidence with a hint that names the evidence to add, apart from no_match; (4) the round budget: sufficiency and Choice can share one request, an escalation is a new decision level and needs the AGENTS.md wording on rounds; (5) the measured sufficiency value sat far from 0.5, so the one-threshold principle needs a per-question-type calibration answer (feeds hunch-o88). Gate: numbers from recorded runs on both backends; no claim of calibration without labelled examples. Part of epic hunch-4z4.
notes:
Owner, 2026-09-20: the sufficiency question also works when asked AFTER the intent question. Three placements to measure on the same held-out set: (a) before: gate whether to ask at all, cheapest on poor evidence and the trigger for evidence escalation; (b) alongside, in the same request: no extra latency, but it cannot name the winner because the Choice result is not known yet (this is where today's any Noul sits); (c) after, conditioned on the winner: 'does the state hold enough evidence that <winner> is the thing described', candidate-specific, which closes the gap found in review (pick, why and sort confirm that something fits, never that the winner fits; run already confirms per candidate). For a domain of one window, (a or b) plus (c) stays inside two rounds. Report accepted precision, coverage and requests for each placement.
Deferred per docs/VISION.md: fill and pick start with Choice plus NONE and the margin check. Evidence tiers stay; the any/enough Noul pair returns only if dogfooding shows wrong picks on thin evidence.
close_reason: Superseded by docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md (epic hunch-7zg): the guards are NONE, the any Noul, the ratio p(best) >= 2 x max(p(second), p(NONE)) and the insufficient_evidence budget check (section 2.1 step 5); no separate sufficiency round.

title: fill @{branch:}: a remote-only branch resolves to its bare name, which git cannot use
description: Seen in the hunch-iu8 pilot (jevify 0.9.1, T1 with-arm) in ~/Projects/testify, where ticket/TPE-791 exists only as origin/ticket/TPE-791: `jevify fill -- git log --all --oneline --graph --decorate '@{branch:allergy model and schema migration}'` printed 'branch ticket/TPE-791 0.99 ... origin/ticket/TPE-791 - feat(TPE-791): add Allergy model, SchemaV5 migration' then exec'd git log ... 'ticket/TPE-791' and git failed: fatal: ambiguous argument 'ticket/TPE-791': unknown revision (exit 128). The branch lister strips the remote prefix from the chosen record, but git only resolves the bare name when a local branch or a unique remote-tracking ref of that name exists; here the bare name is not a ref at all (git rev-parse ticket/TPE-791 exits 128 too, origin/ticket/TPE-791 works). Expected: the substituted value is a ref the command can resolve (origin/ticket/TPE-791 when there is no local branch), or the local name only when it exists; the status line already knows the full ref. The pilot agent recovered by hand (git rev-parse origin/...), so the answer was right but the fill call cost a request and failed.
notes: Decision (hunch-x4w). No single spelling of a remote-only branch satisfies both commands, verified with git 2.55: git switch accepts only the short name (ticket/TPE-791, by its remote-tracking DWIM rule) and refuses origin/ticket/TPE-791, remotes/origin/... and refs/remotes/origin/... ('a branch is expected, got remote branch'); git log, rev-parse, diff, merge and every other rev-taking command resolve only the qualified forms and fail on the short name (exit 128). Rejected: making the handle depend on the command (jevify does not parse the caller's command); listing both spellings as two candidates (the same branch twice splits the probability, so the marker abstains or picks arbitrarily); creating a local tracking branch or a ref before exec (a mutation nobody authorized, and --dry-run must run nothing); flipping the bare handle back to origin/x (git switch fails loudly, git checkout origin/x detaches HEAD silently, git push origin origin/x names a remote branch wrong: silent damage, against asymmetric doubt). Chosen: the caller says which by the literal it writes, as with src/@{file:...}. Bare @{branch:x} keeps hunch-emc's short name for commands that take a branch name (switch, checkout, push, branch -d). A literal prefix makes the branch kind list the refs whose short ref name (main, origin/ticket/TPE-791) starts with it, unfolded, with the rest as the handle: 'git log origin/@{branch:x}' substitutes origin/ticket/TPE-791. Rule 1 holds: the value is the handle the lister printed after the literal the caller wrote. Tier-two evidence for a prefixed branch logs prefix+handle. Docs to update (lead): docs/guide/kinds.md branch row and docs/guide/agents.md line 28 (git log -1 --format=%H '@{branch:...}' fails on a remote-only branch; write origin/@{branch:...} for a revision).
close_reason: The branch kind takes the marker's literal prefix as its scope, so 'origin/@{branch:x}' substitutes the qualified ref that git log and rev-parse resolve while the bare marker keeps the short name git switch takes; verified live on this repository and on a scratch clone with a remote-only branch. No single spelling satisfies both commands (checked against git 2.55), and the caller's literal is the only signal jevify may use

title: route answers a near-tie confidently: no margin rule
description:
Outcome: route treats two tools that serve a task equally well as what they are, instead of naming one at a margin no wider than noise.

Evidence (hunch-o88, 2026-09-22, frozen validation set, jev-1.13.0): route-val-dev-02 scored json_pp 0.93 against jq 0.91 on TypeSafe and named json_pp. The gold accepts either, so it counted as correct, but the same shape would name the wrong tool at a 0.02 margin. fill and pick apply the winner ratio (src/tournament.rs) and abstain on a near-tie; route compares fits and has no margin rule (src/cmd/run.rs).

Also recorded there: route-val-dev-03 ("translate into Japanese", gold none) is a false action on both backends because this machine's PATH carries an LLM translator. That case's gold is environment-dependent in a way the manifest's "requires" field does not capture. Fix the manifest case or state the limit; that part belongs to evals/validation, not to the verb.

Consider: apply the winner ratio route already has available, or name the runners-up when the margin is thin. Decide against docs/VISION.md (asymmetric doubt: route prints and starts nothing, so a near-tie costs less than for fill) before changing behaviour.

Files (write set): src/cmd/run.rs, the route contract test, docs/guide/verbs.md (route section), src/cmd/agent.rs if the capabilities text states the rule, CHANGELOG.md.

Done when: a near-tie either names both or abstains; a contract test covers the tie and the clear case; the document and capabilities state the rule; the AGENTS.md gate passes.
notes:
Decision against docs/VISION.md (2026-09-22): the winner ratio (tournament.rs, best >= 2x second) is not applied to route. It is built for one Choice distribution where the finalists' probabilities compete; route's round 2 scores each finalist with an absolute Noul of its own ("is this command a correct, direct way"), so every command that serves the task scores high at once. On the frozen set (jev-1.13.0, TypeSafe) the ratio would have abstained on 6 of 11 decided cases (tr 0.87/0.58, tar 0.78/0.45, zipinfo 0.94/0.87, curl 0.69/0.67, host 0.96/0.95, jq 0.92/0.92), 5 of them correct. VISION: route is `pick --from tool`, it prints and starts nothing, and "jevify never picks the first of several silently"; the asymmetric cost is a glance at names, not a wrong action. Rule chosen: a runner-up with fit >= threshold and within TIE_MARGIN = 0.05 of the best is a tie; route still names the best on stdout (exit 0) and names the ties in data.ties and on stderr ("also fits: dig (0.96), nslookup (0.95)"), so the caller sees the tie before writing the command. No abstention on a tie: a tie between two tools that both serve the task is the common case (dig/host/nslookup, unzip/zipinfo), an exit 3 would cost coverage for no safety.
Validation before/after (scripts/validation_run.py --verb route, TypeSafe, all 12 cases): before cov 0.92 acc 0.91 false 1; after cov 0.92 acc 0.82 false 2. The extra "false action" is route-val-dev-01: json_pp 0.91 named, ties [json-glib-format 0.89, jq 0.87]; the run before it had jq 0.92 on top with perl 0.92 next. Which of the tied tools lands on top is run-to-run noise, exactly the bead's shape; the scorer reads data.tool only and does not credit a gold tool present in ties. Ties named after the change: cal-arch-02 zipinfo + [unzip], val-net-02 host + [dig, nslookup, ahost], val-dev-01 json_pp + [json-glib-format, jq].
route-val-dev-03 ("translate into Japanese", gold none) stays a false action on this machine: `spit` on the PATH is an LLM translator, fit 0.87 with no tie. title: The README demo shows a right answer, and the threshold's meaning is written down
description:
Two items, both found while tracing measured claims (hunch-34c). Documents and one demo only;
no logic change.

A. The README commit demo shows a wrong answer. `git show '@{commit:stopped sending the free
backend batches it refuses}'` prints `candidates 246, windows 3` and decides at 0.56 (next 0.12,
none 0.21) on `332191a fix: pick prefers the thing to its documentation page`, which is not the
commit the description names. Three repeats gave 0.50, 0.56, 0.58 and the same wrong commit. The
transcript in README.md and docs/guide/getting-started.md is now truthful but sells the product
badly, and docs/demo/examples.sh still runs the old command.

Replace the demo in all three files with this substitute, verified today:
  git log --oneline -30 | jevify fill --field 1 --dry-run -- git show --stat --format=%s '@{-:made route abstain when two commands are too close}'
  -> 317cbf7 0.99 (next 0.00, none 0.01); candidates 30, windows 1
Re-run it yourself and paste what you get; do not copy those numbers. Keep the three files
identical and keep examples.sh able to run every README example. If the substitute does not
reproduce, report that and change nothing.

B. The threshold's meaning is undocumented and a careful reader misreads it. `meta.threshold`
gates `ranking.any` -- whether anything in the pool matches at all -- while the winner is picked
by a ratio against the runner-up and P(NONE) (src/tournament.rs:142-155, WINNER_RATIO). So a
marker can resolve with a winner whose own p is below `meta.threshold`; observed at p 0.41 with
threshold 0.5 over 246 candidates, which is correct behaviour, not a bug, because p is a
relative Choice probability over the pool and falls as the pool grows.

Read every place that mentions the threshold -- README.md, docs/guide/*.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md,
docs/VISION.md, the capabilities strings in src/cmd/agent.rs -- and find the ones whose wording
implies the winner's own score must reach it. Correct them and state the rule once, in
docs/guide/how-it-works.md, in two or three sentences: what the threshold gates, what the ratio
decides, and that a candidate probability is relative to the pool size so it cannot be compared
across runs with different pools. Link to it from ROBOT_MODE rather than repeating it.
If docs/VISION.md itself is wrong here, do not edit it: report it to the lead.

Write set: README.md, docs/guide/how-it-works.md, docs/guide/getting-started.md,
docs/guide/verbs.md, docs/guide/faq.md, docs/guide/agents.md, docs/guide/configuration.md,
docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, docs/demo/examples.sh, src/cmd/agent.rs (capability strings only),
tests/agent.rs (only if a doc-example assertion must follow the new demo).
Also fix, while you are there: docs/guide/configuration.md:77 and the doc comment at
src/cmd/run.rs:17 still say "1,900 commands"; the measurement is 1,883. src/cmd/run.rs is in
your write set for that comment only.

Done when: the new demo is in the three files identically and reproduces; no document implies
the winner's score must pass the threshold; the rule is stated once and linked; the two 1,900
figures are 1,883; and the gate passes (cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked --all-targets,
cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc
--locked --no-deps, cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1, ubs on changed files).
Workers never commit; the lead commits and closes.

The threshold rule is stated once in how-it-works and linked from ROBOT_MODE and the capability string; three documents that implied the winner's own score must pass the threshold are corrected. VISION needed no change. Both 1,900 figures are 1,883. ubs exits non-zero identically before and after on the same two files (three test-code false positives).

title: Deadline starts at Client::new, after the excerpts are read; take the instant before evidence
description:
Outcome: the overall deadline (`JEVIFY_DEADLINE`, 600 s by default) covers the whole verb, including reading the evidence, as docs/ROBOT_MODE.md:280-282 and docs/guide/configuration.md:16 promise ("the verb's overall budget").

Context (review round 9, synthesis section 3, P2, raised by astra; verified in the synthesis): the deadline instant is taken in `Client::new` (src/jev/client.rs:196-206, `deadline: Instant::now() + budget`), but `filter --files` reads the excerpts first (src/cmd/filter.rs:52-57 `records::excerpts`) and builds the client at filter.rs:62. Slow filesystem work (a network mount, thousands of files) runs outside the budget, so a verb can exceed `JEVIFY_DEADLINE` by any amount before the first request. Check the other verbs that gather evidence before building the client (fill's listings, pick --from, why's log read, route's PATH scan) and treat them the same way.

Fix: take the instant once at verb start (in the Ctx, before evidence is read) and pass it to `Client::new`, or build the client before reading evidence in every verb; one mechanism, stated in the client.

Files (write set): src/jev/client.rs, src/cmd/filter.rs and any verb that reads evidence before `Client::new` (src/cmd/fill.rs, src/cmd/pick.rs, src/cmd/why.rs, src/cmd/run.rs, src/cmd/mod.rs (Ctx)), a test that proves the budget includes evidence reading, docs/guide/configuration.md:16 and docs/ROBOT_MODE.md:280 only if the wording changes. Everything else read-only.

Done when: a test with a small `JEVIFY_DEADLINE` and a slow evidence read (a records source that sleeps past the budget, or a fake clock) ends exit 4 naming the deadline without sending a request; the budget is taken in one place. Gate before handing back (AGENTS.md, sandbox disabled): cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs <changed files>. Never weaken a test to pass. Workers never commit; the lead commits.
close_reason: The deadline counts from the instant Config::load builds Stats, so reading stdin, excerpts and listings is inside the budget; the client build and every POST refuse once it has passed, before a connection opens. A contract test holds stdin past a one-second budget for filter --files and pick: exit 4, the deadline named, zero requests. Proven against the old code, which sent the request at 1002 ms

title: Document the branch marker's two forms: bare for git switch, prefixed for a revision
description:
Outcome: the documents and capabilities state the branch rule that hunch-x4w implemented.

A bare marker names a branch the way git switch takes it (the short name, for a remote-only branch too). A literal prefix scopes the kind to that remote's refs and substitutes the qualified ref, which is what git log, git rev-parse and every other rev-taking command resolve: `git log -1 --format=%H 'origin/@{branch:the auth refactor}'`.

- README.md only if it shows a branch marker with a rev-taking command.

title: Evaluate run for agents on tools the model cannot know
description: The pilot in benchmarks/agents/ only needed tools a frontier model knows by name, so it could not show whether run helps an agent. Test the case it is built for. Design: a scratch bin directory on PATH and MANPATH with invented internal CLIs (neutral names that do not reveal their function, each with a man page and a script that records a correct invocation), mixed into the real PATH of about 2,000 commands. A multi-step job stated as outcomes. Arms: plain agent versus agent with skills/grevi/SKILL.md, 5 or more runs per arm, same model. Both arms are told internal tools exist on PATH, neither is told their names. Measure: steps passed by the checker, tokens, tool calls, wall time, and how each agent discovered the tool (apropos, man -k, ls, grevi run). Also measure at two inventory sizes (tens and hundreds of internal tools), because the alternative to run is reading man-page summaries and that cost grows with the inventory. Report whatever comes out. If run loses, find out why (routing, flags, latency) and feed hunch-eil. Gate: checker script plus results in benchmarks/agents/, numbers only from recorded runs.
notes:
Use benchmarks/agents/EXPERIMENT.md as the experiment contract. This issue supplies the unfamiliar-tool run cohort for hunch-ric/hunch-evl; the earlier five-runs suggestion is a smoke test, not a powered performance claim. Preserve familiar-tool controls, identical discovery permissions and actual executable outcomes.
Lowered per docs/VISION.md (hunch-vq2): build fill, filter and label first; measurement follows use.

title: 2.2 Pool rule: one finalists rule (3, 2, 1 by rank) for every caller of tournament::rank
description:
Plan bead: 2.2, the pool-rule half — src/tournament.rs (the source half of 2.2 is hunch-q8p, which writes src/source.rs). Epic hunch-7zg. This bead replaces the earlier "measure candidate survival" framing with the rule the plan fixes; the measurement is the evaluation that follows the language (hunch-lpp).

Outcome: a long list is searched in two rounds without ever comparing a probability from one request with one from another, and without cutting the pool: the right candidate in any window reaches the finals. One rule serves every caller of `tournament::rank`: `fill`, stdin `pick`, `pick --from` and `why`.

Context: plan §2.1 (the paragraph "One pool rule for every caller" with its table, steps 4 and 5), §2 "Changed in place" (src/tournament.rs), §8.1, §9.4; vision "A long list is searched in two rounds". Today src/tournament.rs:126-127 sorts the finalists of all windows by probability and truncates to 24 (`MAX_FINALISTS`), which compares probabilities across requests. Decisions, final:
- W is the window of the backend: 200 candidates on TypeSafe, 99 on classifier.dev (`Backend::window`, src/config.rs:34). F = W x (W / 3): 13,200 and 3,267.
- ONE RULE for every caller of `tournament::rank`: finalists per window `n` = 3 when `3 x windows <= W`, else 2 when `2 x windows <= W`, else 1. Always by rank inside a window, never by a probability from another request. Capacity is `W x W` candidates (9,801 keyless; on TypeSafe the 20,000 ceiling is reached first).
- `fill` uses `n = 3` only, so its limit stays `F = W x (W / 3)`: the caller passes a mode (for example `Finalists::ThreeOnly` against `Finalists::Auto`), and above F in that mode `rank` returns the capacity error with no request.
- `pick`, `pick --from` and `why` use the full rule. Above `W x W`: an ordered list keeps its newest `W x W` and the status line says so; any other list is exit 6 `too_many` (narrow with `grep`, `head` or a prefix). stdin `pick` allows 20,000 lines today (`MAX_LINES`, src/cmd/pick.rs:9): its stdin list is not ordered, so on the classifier backend 9,802 lines are `too_many` with no request; `MAX_LINES` stays as the second bound (it is the first one reached on TypeSafe).
- `why` keeps `MAX_KEEP = 4000` (src/cmd/why.rs:13): 41 windows keyless, n = 2, 82 finalists in one finals request. `why` needs no capacity error: 4,000 is below 9,801.
- The two statements of the earlier text, "callers keep their behaviour" and "never compare across requests", cannot both hold for 41 windows; the second wins. The behaviour that stays is the contract of each verb (exit codes, envelope, output format), not the identity of the 24 finalists.
- The API keeps its shape; finalist evidence needs no callback ("a closure or a second slice" is gone). A caller with tier-two evidence makes two calls: `shortlist` (round 1, :149), then it fetches the evidence of the finalists itself (async, inside spawn_blocking, after the withholding check), then `window` (:55, `pub(crate)` since hunch-7zg.7; keep that) for the finals. `fill`, `pick --from` and `pick --files` use these two calls. `rank` stays for callers with no tier two (stdin `pick`, `why`), and it KEEPS its `finalist_text` parameter for `why`: `why` is its remaining user (src/cmd/why.rs:116-122 passes `Some(&with_context)`, so the finals carry each line with its context lines, and a one-window `why` still sends two requests, src/tournament.rs:110); stdin `pick` passes `None` (src/cmd/pick.rs:87). The pool rule applies to both paths: `rank` internally, and `shortlist`, whose `per_window` becomes the `n` of the rule (it reports `windows` and `n`); `pick --files`, which cut its shortlist to 24 in src/cmd/pick.rs since hunch-7zg.7 (`MAX_FINALISTS`, :10, and the `truncate` at :62-64), moves to the rule here. `route` passes its own `per_window` and asks its own absolute second question; it stays as it is.
- THE FINALIST ORDER is defined once, here, and hunch-bkb and hunch-7zg.12 use it: by rank, then by window index (rank 1 of every window in window order, then rank 2 of every window, then rank 3). No probability from one request is compared with one from another to build it. "Tier-two evidence for the first 24" (`MAX_FINALISTS`) means the first 24 of that order, so every window's best candidate gets tier-two evidence before any window's second.
- `shortlist` returns the per-window `Ranking`s (candidates, `any`, `none`), not only candidates, and alongside them the finalists in the order above (for example `struct Shortlist { windows: Vec<Ranking>, finalists: Vec<Candidate>, n: usize }`); today src/tournament.rs:149-167 flattens the windows, sorts them by probability (:166) and discards `any` and `none`. With ONE window the caller decides from that `Ranking` (through `decide`) with no second request. `route` calls `shortlist` at src/cmd/run.rs:42 and then takes `.take(12)` over a pool sorted by probability across windows; that is `route`'s own, present behaviour and it stays: the adapter in src/cmd/run.rs re-flattens the windows' candidates, sorts them by probability and keeps its `take(12)`.
- The tier-two evidence of the finalists comes from `source::enrich(kind, handles)` (hunch-q8p), called by `fill` and `pick --from` between `shortlist` and `window`; tournament.rs never calls it.
- Round 1: one `window` per W candidates (one Choice with NONE, one `any` Noul), all in flight at the same time.
- Round 2, one request: with several windows it is the finals: the `n` best of each window BY RANK, all of them, with tier-two evidence for the first 24 of the finalist order (`MAX_FINALISTS` bounds tier-two evidence only, not the pool). With one window, round 2 runs only when the ratio failed and the kind has tier-two evidence: this one-window shortcut applies to `fill` and `pick --from` (their callers decide it, since they make the two calls); `pick --files` always runs round two, as today. Never a third round.
- `decide(&Ranking, threshold: f64)` (tournament.rs has no `Config`; the caller passes `ctx.threshold`): found when `any >= threshold` and `p(best) >= 2 x max(p(second), p(NONE))`. A ratio holds for 3 options and for 200. Equal scores abstain. The factor is a constant in tournament.rs; there is no setting for it. `decide` returns found / no_match / ambiguous with the two closest candidates, for the status lines of `fill` and `pick --from`. `decide` serves `fill` and `pick --from` ONLY: stdin `pick` keeps its present found rule (`any >= threshold` and best > NONE, src/cmd/pick.rs:89-94) and its `-n N` semantics; `why` keeps its own rule.
- tournament.rs does no I/O. The `Ranking` reports `windows` and `n`, so a caller prints `finalists per window: 2` when n is not 3.
- `why`, `pick` and `route` call `rank` and `shortlist` today (imports: src/cmd/why.rs:5, src/cmd/pick.rs:6, src/cmd/run.rs:8; calls: src/cmd/why.rs:116, src/cmd/pick.rs:62 and :87, src/cmd/run.rs:42). Adapt the call sites of `rank` to the new signature, make stdin `pick` map the capacity error to exit 6 `too_many`, and print the `finalists per window` line. `shortlist` (src/tournament.rs:149) keeps every window's top `per_window` and cuts nothing (the sort by probability at :166 orders, it does not truncate; it leaves with this bead, replaced by the finalist order above). It gains the mode of the rule (`Finalists::ThreeOnly`, `Finalists::Auto`, or the fixed `per_window` that `route` passes today) and the capacity error. `route` asks its own absolute second question and keeps its behaviour; src/cmd/run.rs is touched only for the changed signature.

Files (write set): src/tournament.rs, tests/tournament.rs; call-site adaptation and the capacity behaviour in src/cmd/why.rs, src/cmd/pick.rs, src/cmd/run.rs, with their contract tests in tests/pick.rs and tests/why.rs (added tests only). Everything else is read-only (tests/common/mod.rs gives probability vectors per question since bead 1.2). For the classifier backend, tests/tournament.rs builds a literal `jevify::config::Config { backend: Backend::Classifier, key: None, base_url: server.uri(), … }` against `common::mock_classifier` (tests/common/mod.rs:274), because `common::config()` builds a TypeSafe config only (tests/common/mod.rs:335-348) and that file is read-only here. hunch-7zg.12 (`pick --from`) writes src/cmd/pick.rs and tests/pick.rs after this bead; hunch-q8p runs in parallel and shares no file.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.10.

Done when, as tests:
- 250 candidates resolve in two rounds and the finals request holds three finalists of every window (inspect the captured request).
- The rule: for W = 99, 33 windows give n = 3, 34 give n = 2, 49 give n = 2, 50 give n = 1, 99 give n = 1; the same boundaries for W = 200 (66/67, 100/101).
- Classifier backend, 4,000 items: 41 windows, n = 2, one finals request with 82 finalists, the planted answer wins. Classifier backend, 9,802 items: the capacity error, no request; through stdin `pick` that is exit 6 `too_many` with the ways to narrow (tests/pick.rs); 9,801 items resolve with n = 1.
- `why` with `MAX_KEEP` kept lines on the classifier backend resolves in two rounds with n = 2 (tests/why.rs), and its output format is unchanged.
- `why` keeps `finalist_text` (tests/why.rs, inspect the captured requests): the finals request still carries the context lines of each finalist (`context only, not a candidate; before: …`), and a `why` whose lines fit ONE window still sends two requests.
- The finalist order: with 3 windows and n = 3, the finals request lists rank 1 of windows 0, 1, 2, then rank 2 of each, then rank 3 of each, whatever the round-one probabilities; `shortlist` returns the finalists in that order next to the per-window `Ranking`s. `route` over several windows still takes its 12 by probability (tests/run_route.rs stays green, read-only).
- `ThreeOnly` (fill): F candidates resolve; F + 1 is the capacity error with no request.
- The right candidate in the last window wins even when another window's finalists have higher round-one probabilities.
- Two close rivals in one window both reach the finals and end as `ambiguous`; a tie abstains; NONE close to the best abstains; `any` below the threshold is `no_match`.
- `shortlist` with one window, then `decide` on its `Ranking`, each with EXACTLY ONE request: a decisive winner is found; a low `any` is `no_match`; a dominant `NONE` is `no_match`.
- Classifier backend, 9,802 candidates: an unordered list is the capacity error (`too_many` at the caller) with no request; for an ordered kind the caller trims to the newest 9,801 before calling and says so (that trim is the caller's, hunch-7zg.12; here: 9,801 resolve).
- `decide` as a pure function: the ratio holds, the ratio fails, equal scores, NONE close to the best, `any` below the threshold. The one-window shortcut itself is tested by its callers (hunch-bkb, hunch-7zg.12). stdin `pick` with a best that beats NONE but fails the ratio is still found (its rule is unchanged), and `-n 3` still prints three.
- `pick --files` above one window follows the pool rule (the 24-cut of src/cmd/pick.rs is gone) and still always runs round two.
- W, W + 1, F candidates on each backend: the request counts are 1, 2 + 1, and W/3 windows + 1.
- A deterministic 1,800-item regression: the planted answer survives in every position of every window.
- Existing why, pick and route suites stay green; a test that asserted the old 24-finalist pool is rewritten to the rule above and the finish message names it, for the lead's commit body (this is the decided rule, not a weakened test).
- The gate below passes.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
